The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "I am asking you a proper question; why do you shout recklessly? The monk shouted again.
The Master raised his staff. A monk stepped forward, held him back, and said, "What are you doing?
The Master replied, "It is difficult to deceive those with clear eyes," and then he pushed the staff away. The monk said, "You thief!"
A monk asked the Chan Master of Zuozhou, "What is the guest within the guest? The Master said, "Leaning on the gate and hanging by the door, as if drunk;
speaking and breathing without any sense of shame. The student asked, "What is the host within the guest?
The Master said, "Mouth reciting Amitābha with two staffs; eyes blind, the pupils do not emerge from their sockets. The student asked, "..."
“What is the guest within the host? The Master said, “Highly holding up the ancestral seal, it is used to meet the occasion;

to benefit beings, one must know that the words carry compassion. The student asked, “What is the host within the host? The Master said, “Horizontally grasping the Mohe sword, the true command is fully maintained;
throughout the realm of Great Peace, the foolish and stubborn are executed. The student asked, “Since it is a realm of Great Peace, for what reason...”
"Ma! Cut off this dull-witted obstinacy! The Master said: "Night travel is not permitted; you must insistently carry a torch. You must then show it to people on the road.
Linji ascended the hall and presented four kinds of "discriminating speech," saying: "Sometimes I take away the person but do not take away the environment; sometimes..."
At times the realm is taken away but not the person; at times both the person and the realm are taken away; at times neither the person nor the realm is taken away.
The Master then came forward and asked, "What is 'taking away the person but not the realm'? Ji said, "The warm sun brings forth life, spreading carpets of brocade upon the earth;
the infant’s hanging hair is as white as silk. He further asked, "What is 'taking away the realm but not the person'?"
Ji said, "The King’s decree has been issued and reached all under heaven; the General has cleared the smoke and dust beyond the frontier.
Jian asked, "What is it like when both the person and the environment are seized? Ji said, "In Bingfen there is no news; one dwells alone in a single region.
Jian asked, "What is it like when neither the person nor the environment are seized? Ji said, "The King ascends the jeweled palace; the village elders sing and chant."
The Master then offered this verse:
To take away the person but not the environment, Is to be caught in the clamor of one's own conditions. If you wish to seek the profound essence, Your deliberations will only lead to self-reproach.
The pearl from the black dragon’s mane shines with brilliant luster; The leaves of the moon-bright cassia tree are lush and dense.
Beholding the essence, there is no divergence; yet one still remains entangled in the net.
When the realm is seized but not the person, where can truth be found by seeking through words? Inquiring about Chan, Chan is but a delusion;
investigating the principle, the principle is not intimate. The sun shines upon the pale light of frost; the mountains sway with fresh verdant hues.
Even if you could intuitively grasp the profound mystery, it would be as tranquil as dust in the eye;

when both person and environment are stripped away, the true command has always been in effect. There is no accounting for Buddhas or Patriarchs—how can one speak of sentiments regarding the holy and the mundane?
To even attempt to violate this is like encountering a "blow-off" sword; one retreats wounded, like a blind man stumbling against a tree.
Advancing forward to seek the wondrous meeting, Suddenly striking the vital spirit;
Person and environment are both unseizable, Thought and intention are not biased. The words of host and guest do not differ, The principle of question and answer is complete in all.
Treading through the moon upon the clear pool, Piercing open the azure sky.
Unable to clarify the wondrous function, They sink and drown within the unconditioned.
Master’s Verses, Thirty-Eight:
The First Patriarch on Xiong’er Peak.
Casually wearing the Vairocana seal, he is honored as the highest among men and devas; His jewel-boat crosses the Phoenix Pond, his golden staff hangs at the Dragon Gate.
After his departure, King Liang was moved to feeling; upon his arrival, the Lord of Wei received his grace.
Carrying his single shoe across the Onion Mountains, half a verse shook heaven and earth.

The Second Patriarch, Feng of Zhangchuan, succeeded the Ancestral Patriarch of the Divine Land; The Linked Lamps turn once more. He secretly transmitted the Seal of the Third Patriarch and returned in a dream to the Five Lords' Street;
The Mysterious Word encompasses Heaven and Earth, And Compassionate Heaven opens the Sun and Moon.
Flowing upstream against the waves to Zhangpu, Heaven was moved to tears, clouds thundered, and the Three Patriarchs appeared like a unicorn among the mountains and valleys.
Having received the seal of transmission from the Northern Qi, He walked alone beyond the mundane world; In the land of the Patriarchs, the rivers and streams are vast.
Following the days and months of heaven in leisure, Wondrous sounds flow through the four seas; Auspicious vapors overflow the three mountains.
One phrase of news comes from the south: The clear breeze shakes the Snow Pass, And the pines of the Twin Peaks at the Fourth Patriarch’s abode.
Emerald hues merge with the trees of Mount Ji; The towering pines of the ancestral peaks rise high.
Frost gathers upon the five petals; snow holds within the two summits. The moon is distant within the Golden River;
Pearls are added to the jade mirror. Whistling breezes carry subtle sounds; Throughout the world, the True Doctrine is spread.
The Fifth Patriarch, Moon of Dongshan:
the ancestral seal is divided at Dongshan. In the void, the moon forms its wheel; The green eyes behold the wind-light, the emerald hue of the Huangmei trees is spring.
Nine branches add to the auspicious cranes; A single leaf brushes past the auspicious qilin.
Separately receiving the prediction of the Golden Immortal; The fifth person at Caoxi, the Sixth Patriarch.
At Nan Bao of Caoxi, he attained the intent of Huangmei; The record of the Dharma-fountain at Caoxi; The three robes together with the patriarchal seal.
A single bowl, the lineage of the masters complete; The compassionate moonlight illuminates a thousand oceans. The profound river pours into a hundred streams;
Twelve generations in the Divine Continent, The Dharma-eye transmitted in succession, the seal of Vairocana.
The moon of compassion in the heavens shines afar upon the three peaks; Beyond the finger-pointing, the cascading river flows deep in ten thousand streams.
A solitary celestial vessel sails alone upon the ocean of Huazang; Boundless rivers and marshes rejoice as the heart turns toward home at Xiong’er Rock.
The Master Xiong’er was buried at Luoyang; The Son of Heaven of Longcheng sat in his place for a thousand rows.
Carrying a single sandal on his shoulder back to Mount Cong, He startled to death King Liang and King Wei—Mazu Lin.
The Qilin sleeps within the Dharma Garden, its scales unfolding like a thousand petals; the horse treads upon Caoxi, gushing forth ten thousand springs.
Among the ancient Buddhas’ transmissions, he received a direct prediction; the moon turns and grinds through the heavens within the sea—the Hundred-Fathom Pine.
Baizhang’s Harmony with the Pines on Frosty Ridge: A serpent coils; the crane’s nature is lean as a dragon.
Descending from the hall, he calls for names; The Master’s mind is beyond measure—ten thousand layers deep.
Linji, the Dragon.
The Dragon controls the hanging river; the sea moon is autumnal. Mist, clouds, wind, and rain are gathered all at once.
The waves surge so violently that people find it hard to comprehend; He cuts off the waters of the thousand rivers so they no longer flow—the Moon in the Dragon Pond.
The ancestral lineage’s waves and billows, the mystery of the half-verse; The boat and oars of Caoxi meet with wind and mist.
A single turn reveals the moon in the dragon-pool at the ocean floor; It grinds through the snow-capped peaks of Mount Ji, before the cassia tree of the Twin Groves.
In person receiving the Lord of the Three Assemblies of the Dragon Flower; He hews open the nine-layered city of the Phoenix Pavilion.
King Liang topples the Diamond Buddha; How could he fail to preach the sutras at the Gate of Medicine?
Yaoshan’s blade.
The Dragon Spring at Yaoshan illuminates the pure gaze; the Master of Heaven and Earth has spread his style throughout.
A single line of such lofty standard is difficult to distinguish, yet it suddenly becomes clear at the mouth of Yunyan’s cloud-valley, like the sun amidst the crimson clouds.
One day of vermilion clouds meets Shitou; how can the pair of qilin and phoenixes be transmitted?
If one wishes to speak of the sharp edge of the Zen school’s seal, one is choked and must cover one's ears—rest, Master!
Dwelling among the cypress trees of Niaoke.
White phoenixes soar through mist and clouds, commanding the bird’s nest; The pearl of the black dragon shines upon the mountains and rivers of the patriarchs.
The original intent when he first grasped the cloth-hair— Its essence and function are more than a mere fragment of Vairocana.
Shigong’s bow.
The dragon-sword and carved bow bear the majesty of the Patriarchs and Buddhas; Their frost-sharp blades and thunderous bolts are swift and difficult to follow.
When that golden arrow first passed through his breast, He remained within the profound mystery of the "Not-One" and "Not-Two," Becoming a stone for the Stone-Returning School.
The brilliance of snow and the majesty of frost bear the style of Mazu;
A tiger with lofty character and a dragon-like spirit— Who can understand the path of Guizong? A single arrow penetrates the three barriers throughout the land;
The frost of Damei.
The tiger sees smoke and vines permeating the cave gate; In his heart, the ancient Buddha shakes heaven and earth.
The dragon spring cuts off the horn of the qilin; He stirs the sea-moon of Vairocana until it grows dim, And the waters of Guankxi flow forth.
One school from Cao Yuan and Guankui, where dragons move and wind and rain stir the clouds and mists;
the subsequent mechanism is as swift as arrowheads meeting bowstrings, its waves surging so violently they shake the sea and mountains of Vairocana low.
The Emperor’s Bamboo.
The dragon’s roar and the phoenix’s luster shake heaven and earth; the Bear-Ear, Chicken-Head, and Sea mountains are heard within the realm.
A single expanse of frost and snow beyond the Three Isles; the tiger’s heart and half a verse sprinkle wind and clouds—Snow at Ox Head.
The six-leafed ox-head tree is planted separately; In the Five Indias, the Xiong’er peak roars with clouds and thunder.
One must know that the Fourth Patriarch lowered his hook to receive [the disciple]; The hundred birds carrying flowers shall not come again to Wuxie Spring.
At the very moment of generating the resolve, he questioned Shitou; The mind of the rivers and streams surges and flows apart in vast currents.
He called it back and pointed it out as the Seal of Vairocana; Thus, like a mountain, all things were at rest.
Luzu’s Rock.
Tiger trails and dragon springs wind around the cliffs; Phoenixes perch upon frosty pines, cranes harmonize with the cypress.
Who can grasp the intent of the Master? To turn the pivot of heaven and earth—how could one not study the Jade of Fenzhou?
The Dragon Palace and Deer Park connect through a hundred rivers; The Eight Treasuries and Three Vehicles rest within the palm.
Yet it was at Jiangxi that he met Mazu; Turning his head, he stepped across the great void.
—Sushan Song.
Sparse ridges of pines and creepers, five-leaved clouds; beyond the realm of Vairocana, another Qin.
A dragon of Li-qi tramples the moon from the void; a wooden horse neighs again as the dew and rain renew.
Drums beat south of the pass.
The bell clashing against wind and frost makes tigers and leopards wail; within the walls of the King of Chu’s city, he rides his ox backward.
With unrestrained vigor, he beats the drums of Guannan, their sound overwhelming clouds and thunder, stirring the Nine Categories of the Odes and resonating through mountain crags.
Xiongeri and Jishan, five seals of mystery; The serpent coils at the phoenix’s mouth, nine hollows spring forth.
Upon the summit of Zixiao Peak, a single wheel of moon Shatters the midnight gloom of Caoxi, leaving it whole.
Chan Master Nanyue Huairang, the Phoenix.
Having separately bathed in the waters of Caoxi, I dwell amidst the myriad peaks of Mount Heng. With intent, I transmit the Five Leaves; without seeking, I occupy the thousand peaks.
The crag-dwelling cranes vie to hide their wings; The cliff-roosting cocks cease their plaintive cries.
A single sound resonates beyond the celestial realm; Within the seas, I continue the true tradition.
The carp of Jizhou receive the fine rain of the Five Days of Compassion; The Master moistens the Zen groves. The blue eyes seal the thousand lamps;
the pure source is the single stream of the mind. Its origins come from the distant past; its depths are bottomless and profound.
A separate successor to Caoxi, whose virtuous reputation is revered by all;
At Nanquan’s bamboo roots, where shall one seek its stem? Solitary and extraordinary, it stands apart from the forest; The phoenix arrives and strikes its nodes.
The dragon departs, dawn knows its tune; Its spirit shakes the snow—extraordinary. Its form intones with the wind, profoundly perceiving things;
Amidst the usual mist and clouds, it moves and turns, vibrating the empty heart—the pine on the stone.

Emerging from the rocks, it stretches vast and remote; Tangled forests, moreover, cannot compare to its likeness. It harbors emerald hues beyond the mist and clouds, And spreads its layers amidst the snow and frost.
Its shadows stir the moonlight of a thousand ravines, Its sounds join the wind of the Five Leaves.
Its wondrous tones reach the Medicine Peaks; Throughout the world, the True Doctrine is established.
At Jia Shan Lei, the waters of the Li River surge with wind and waves; The mountains and peaks crumble in disarray. Amidst the billows, the moon is clarified;
beyond the heavens, thunder roars in alarm. The dragon’s pearl is difficult to seize; the treasure of the mountain ravines is easy to plant.
The path connecting human realms is perilous; throughout the vast oceans, who else can be his peer?
Dongshan’s spring is deep and profound, its branching streams distinct; Beyond the mundane world, a solitary orb— A clear celestial mirror at the bottom of the sea.
The azure-eyed pearl within the pool, A thousand layers of snow-lined banks, Half a verse that penetrates the crystal pitcher,
Transmitted after the Imprint School, A model for devas and humans—
Zhaozhou’s Barrier.
Solitary and lofty, of the Nanquan lineage, the Master’s pivot has attained ease. The three robes are transmitted within the ancestral realm;
a single phrase moves the multitudes. The pearl’s radiance in the secluded valley is extraordinary; the jade’s luster in Lantian is variegated.
If you do not clarify the root and the stalk, it will be difficult to pass Zhaozhou’s barrier.
Cloud-dwelling moon, its pure countenance beyond the realm of space; Vast and expansive, it reaches infinitely far. The jade mirror unites the thousand regions;
the golden wheel encompasses the five heavens. Frost gathers on Mount Xiong’er like a seal; Ice floods Mount Vulture Peak in profound mystery.
Not the Dragon’s Abode nor the Moon, It is difficult to illuminate the spring above the peak.
A verse for the whole assembly: My dwelling place is truly fit for seclusion; How many tens of thousands of times have I swallowed charcoal and hidden my body?
Without touching the waves, he summons the moon of auspiciousness;
moving the clouds and rain, he drums the mountain thunder. Master Tōfū Anju sat within his hermitage. When a monk arrived before the hermitage and simply departed, the Master said, “Ācārya.
The monk turned his head and let out a shout. After a long silence, the Master said, “That fellow is dead! The monk said, “He is dead indeed. The Master [nodded].
The Master struck him; the monk remained silent. The Master laughed loudly. When the monk saw the Master, he asked, "Where is the Abbot of Tongfeng Hermitage?
The Master struck him again. The monk said, "This monk is so reckless!
The Master said, "What was it you just asked? The monk stood with his hands hanging down. The Master said, "But this one—"

The attendant said, "I am leaving. The Master called out, "Ācārya! Wait a moment! The attendant shouted, "Monk! and then went out. The Master said, "If you act like this, you will cause all people to fall into delusion.
A monk asked the Hermitage Master, "If a tiger were to suddenly appear here, what would you do?
The Master then let out a tiger's roar. The monk made a gesture of fear. The Master laughed loudly, "Ha ha! The monk... [remained silent].
The Master said, "You thief! The Master said, "What can you do about me? A monk went up the mountain to visit the Master. Upon seeing him, the Master asked, "What are you doing here?
The monk replied, "I have come specifically to pay my respects. The Master struck him. The monk seized him and said:
"Do not act so rudely," the Master said, pushing him away. He then returned to his hut. The monk said, "This mountain ghost!
The Master asked, "Where did you get this monk? The monk said, "What can be done about this public case? The Master then struck him.
The monk laughed loudly and departed. When the monk returned, the master of the hermitage seized him and said, "You have killed someone! You have killed someone!
The monk pushed him away and said, "What are you shouting about? The Master asked, "Who? The monk then gave a shout. The Master struck him.
The monk said, "Wait a moment, wait a moment. The Master laughed heartily.
While the Master was making straw sandals, a monk came up from behind and let out a tiger’s roar. The Master then shouted.

The monk said, “This does not hinder you from making your straw sandals. The Master said, “You have brought this upon yourself, *ācārya*. The monk shouted. The Master said, “I am the one who invited it.”
An old man entered the mountains to visit the Master. The Master asked, "Where do you reside? The old man remained silent.
The Master said, "You are well able to respond to the occasion. The old man picked up a blade of grass from the ground and showed it to the Master.
The Master gave a shout. The old man bowed. The Master then returned to his hut. The old man said, "In this way, you leave everyone in a state of doubt.
The monk (who was formerly a fellow practitioner) looked at the hut master and asked the Master, "Do you still remember the matters of your travels when you were a wandering monk? The Master said:
The monk said, "Since we parted, how much time has passed? The Master said, "That too was an event of the past.
The monk said, "Why do you not say, 'The affairs of the abbot are troublesome'? The Master said, "The past still lingers.
The monk said, "I have come to visit you recently; take care," and he departed. The Master said, "From the beginning, I have been suspicious of him."
Upon seeing the abbot of the hermitage, the monk gave a shout. The Master said, "You have nearly frightened me to death!
The monk said, "Is it a tiger? The Master then shouted. The monk ran away. The Master pursued him with his staff. The monk made the gesture of bracing a spear.
The Master stood still, leaning on his staff. The monk said, "I am defeated. The Master said, "I grant you twenty blows of grace."
The monk saw the hermitage master and said, "I have come specifically to visit you. The Master did not look back. The monk stepped forward to observe him, and the Master struck him.
The monk said, "With a great battle array before us, I beg the Master for skillful means. The Master struck him again. The monk said, "A true artist is rarely encountered.
The Master asked, "From where have you come? The monk replied, "I have come specifically to visit you."
The Master asked, "Rarely does one encounter a true connoisseur.
At that time, the Abbot of Shanyang was sitting inside his hut. A monk arrived before the hut and stood with his hands folded in *añjali*.
The Master asked, "Who is there? The monk replied, "The Abbot of Shanyang. The Master said, "I am he. The monk then gave a shout.
The Master said, "Heh! Heh! A monk said, "I still want to eat a blow of the staff. The Master then struck him. A monk asked, "I have long heard of Shanyang;
why is it that upon arriving, I do not see it? The Master said, "Black as lacquer. The monk pointed his finger.
The Master said, "You have arrived personally at Shanyang. Another monk came before the hermitage and sat together with the Master.
The monk said, "Master, what principle have you realized that you have come to dwell on this mountain?
The Master said, "I also wished to convey some news, but I feared being scrutinized by others. The monk laughed loudly and departed. The Master said, "Today I have been greatly deceived."
The Master was sitting in meditation before his hermitage when a monk approached him. The monk struck the Master with a palm;
the Master immediately returned to his hut, while the monk remained seated. The Master came back out, and the monk said, "A fierce tiger stands before us;
who dares to oppose it? The Master struck him, and the monk cried, "Suffering! Suffering! Another monk asked the Hermitage Master, "When a realm of experience appears before one..."
"How do you drive him away? The Master shouted, "This is a demon! The monk said, "Today I have been deluded once;
it is no small matter. The Master said, "Fortunately, this is a deep mountain where no one sees us. The monk said, "If you know, then you have attained it."
The Master laughed heartily.
When the Master saw a monk enter the gate at Huxi Hermitage, he gave a shout; the monk remained silent, so the Master struck him.
The monk shouted back, and the Master said, "What a fine petty thief! A monk asked, "The Hermitage Master has been here for a long time..."
The youth said, “Master, I have only seen the withering in winter and the growth in summer; I do not remember the years at all.
The monk said, “It is most wonderful that you cannot remember them. The Master said, “Tell me, how many years have I been here?
The monk said, “Withering in winter and growing in summer. The Master said, “A tiger in the marketplace! A monk asked, “Is this not the tiger?”
"Master of Xixian? The Master said, "It is not. The monk asked, "Why is it not?
The Master said, "Facing each other, we do not recognize one another. The monk said, "You have killed me! The Master said, "What was it you were asking just now?
The monk gave a shout. Another monk came to pay his respects; the Master ignored him entirely. The monk said, "I know."
The abbot possessed such a sharp wit. The Master snapped his fingers once. The monk asked, "What is your fundamental principle? The Master struck him.
The monk said, "I know that today I have fallen into his trap. The Master said, "You still want to eat my staff!
A monk asked, "Where are you from, Abbot? The Master said, "A man from Longxi. The monk— [continued].
[The Master] said, "I have heard it said that Lingxi produces parrots—is this true? The Master made the sound of a parrot.
The monk said, "A fine parrot! The Master then struck him. Later, a monk came to visit the Master; seeing him, the Master asked, "Where have you come from?
The monk then shouted. The Master said, "An adept. After a long while, the Master said, "This fellow is dead!"
The monk then went out. The Master said, "He is still moving. When the monk saw that the Master was sitting, he approached and said, "How do you do, Hermit Master?
The Master asked, "Who is it? The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "How can you be so devoid of guest and host?
The monk said, "There is still room for a second shout. The Master then shouted.
The Master Fupo was sitting inside his hermitage when a monk came weeping up from the foot of the mountain.
The Master closed the door; the monk drew a circle on the wall and stood outside.
The Master went out through the back door and then came weeping up from the foot of the mountain. The monk shouted, "Still doing this very thing—this is where you stand!"
The Master beat his breast and said, "What a pity! Our late master has been utterly buried. The monk said, "Bitter! Bitter! The Master said, "The abbot has been deceived.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "I have come down from Mount Fupen. The Master said, "Did you see the abbot?
The monk gave a shout. The Master struck him. The monk said, "Why did you do that?"
The Master raised his staff. As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him again. The monk asked, "I have long heard of Mount Fupen;
which one is it? The Master pointed directly at him. The monk looked in the direction of the pointing hand, and the Master slapped him.
The monk said, "A true master! After a long pause, the monk slapped the Master once, and the Master stepped forward and seized him.
The monk then ran away, and the Master clapped his hands and laughed loudly.

When the Master arrived at Linji, he asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? As soon as Linji stepped down from his meditation seat and seized him by the collar, the Master hesitated;
Linji then struck him with his palm. Thereupon, the Master attained great enlightenment. The Master then departed from Linji.

Zhēn. [The character "zhù" (to kill) over "tǔ" (earth)] refers to one who urinates on his bedding. When the Master was at a vegetarian feast in the Prefectural Government office, he returned across a bridge and encountered three *zuozhǔ* (seated masters).

"What did he say that would allow him to escape being censured by those from all quarters?

At that time, a monk asked: "When Niutou had not yet seen the Fourth Patriarch..."
The Master said, "There is such a person who, from birth, possesses no knowledge. The monk asked, "After seeing [the truth], what is it like?
The Master said, "There is no such person who, from birth, possesses knowledge. A monk asked, "An awakened person has long remained mired in delusion; I pray that the Master will receive me.
The Master said, "Receive. The monk bowed. The Master then struck him. A monk asked, "Surrounded by the fourfold assembly..."
"How is it at such a time? The Master said, "One does not hear the sound of the Brahma-voice.

He raised his staff; as the monk hesitated, the Master struck him.

The monk bowed, and the Master struck him.

The Master struck him immediately. The monk asked, "Neither saint nor ordinary person—please, Master, answer my question.
The Master said, "Very well. As the monk hesitated, the Master gave a shout. The monk asked, "What is the realm of great compassion?

[The Master] struck [him]. He asked: "When one is so full that one forgets a hundred hungers, what is it like? The Master said: "A poor child encountering spoiled rice. He asked:

The student stepped forward and asked: “Is it not simply this very thing? The Master said: “Heh! Heh!”

Xingjun said, "It would not be right to call this 'acting aggressively. The Master then gave a shout. Xingjun said, "The hook has caught me in a place of no doubt. The Master shouted again.

how does its double radiance manifest as an assistant? The Master said: "Though you know it, you do not touch that which lies beyond the waves. ...carrying [it].
The horned beast with its shaggy fur is right before your eyes. Question: The black stallion has a pearl in its jaw;
how is it obtained? The Master said: "I once thrust a dry bamboo splinter into the sea; even until now, I continue to tune my plain zither. Question: A great ship drifts through the void;
how does one raise the oars? The Master said: "Free and easy, he does not strike his chest; the whole family does not like to see him. Question: How is it?

"This is within the jurisdiction of your state. The Master said: "The Patriarch’s ancestral property has been stolen by Zhang Xingman; he has established his nest among the overlapping villages and neighboring hamlets.
Question: "The wind pursues him, yet it is difficult to seize him; what will become of his future path? The Master said: "The Persian loosens the sleeve of his robe. Question:
"When the Prince was born, did he still require the assistance of his younger brothers? The Master said: "A single phrase attempts to illuminate the light."

The Chan student was astonished. [The Master] remained silent for three moments, yet his response was in accord with the ingenuity of the ancients. The student asked, "Having long followed the plum and the willow, why is there no name upon the golden tablet?
The Master said, "Coming in thousands and going in tens of thousands, one must simply undergo refinement."
The Master ascended the hall and said, “Come, one after another, to offer sustenance; come, one after another, to offer sustenance. A monk then asked, “With what do you offer sustenance?
The Master said, “Tilt your head, open your mouth, and look at my face! Another asked, “When beings of different species are about to be born, there are full signs and omens.
How is it when the sharp point of the pivot carries both meaning and intent? The Master said, “I am emptying my excrement into the incense burner! Another asked, “The Truth...”
Question: "If nature does not follow conditions, how can one attain realization? The Master said: "Pressing pork with milk incense dripping upon it. Question:

"When sight and hearing are difficult to harmonize, how does one engage in thorough inquiry? The Master said: "A single thought penetrates the profound arrow; the three *śi* demons lose their hold. Question:
"When one who remains unchanging while following conditions suddenly encounters a true friend (a '知音'), what then? The Master said: [Silence].
Clad in *xiangce* robes, he stands amidst a thousand peaks; leading water, he irrigates the sparse groves before the Five Elders.

Question: "There is no room for a single step; by which path is the lineage most swift? The Master said: "The northern wind does not borrow an ordinary melody; to turn back, one must transcend the mechanism of both contrariness and compliance.
Question: "In a place where right and wrong do not reach, I ask the Master to speak. The Master said: "Heating the wheel-rim to chase the fleeing horse."

While traveling along the Hu River and crossing the Jian Creek, the Master halted his carriage, loosened his girth, and brushed his yellow horse. He asked, "What is it like during the three swift movements of the lion?
The Master replied, "The taking up and lifting are not in the hand; the wondrous function does not come from another. He asked, "What is the pure Dharma-body?

The Master replied, "The horse-herder’s wife on the sands of the Jinshe River. He asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master replied, "The sands of the Jinshe River."
Master Yì said: "Though flesh and bone may be separated, the grievance is difficult to wash away. Question:
"Even though King Yao exists now, if someone passes by the Orchid Terrace, what then? Master said: "The sleeve is rolled up without carrying the *xiāo* bird;

the point is concealed, yet one still thinks of the monk from the snowy forest. Question: "If one seeks it by marking the boat, it cannot be found. What is the matter that is constantly used? Master said: [He remained silent.]
[The Master] said: "Great merit is not rewarded; the thatched gate is naturally overgrown with weeds. Question: "Since ancient times, the patriarchs have had their seals accord with one another.

What is this seal of mutual accord? The Master said: "The light and boisterous practitioner shifts according to circumstances; take up the handkerchief for wiping tears and summoning the soul. Question:
"Regarding the reward for labor at the end of the summer retreat, I ask the Master to offer a recommendation. The Master said: "Take it out from the sleeve."
Sweeping away the rain from the dragon cave, he raises his cup as the waves surge and the flower-basket bag floats. Question: At the very beginning of the *pravāraṇā*, what should one face?
The Master said: "A handful of fragrant *kuśa* grass has not yet been set down; the six-ringed golden staff resonates, shaking the void."
Question: "In the place where secrets are held in harmony, I request the Master to provide an illustration. The Master said: "A single lamp reflects outside the curtain;
a sincere heart continues through the long night. Question: "What is the ancestral style of the ancient Buddhas? The Master said: "Who would dare to open their mouth? [The student] further asked.
The student said, "Is it like this? The Master said, "A sword on the shoulder. The student asked, "What is the matter regarding the hoe?
The Master said, "A stretch of vacant land before the mountain; planting bamboo and pines, a wide realm. The student asked, "... (The question is omitted).
"What is the guest within the guest? The Master said: "Knitting brows, sitting amidst white clouds. Question: "What is the host within the guest? The Master said:
"Entering the marketplace with both eyes blind. Question: "What is the guest within the host? The Master said:
"Turning the imperial carriage back, the two luminaries shine anew. Question: "What is the host within the host? The Master said: "Grinding and polishing the three [jewels]."
"A foot-long sword waits to slay those who are unjust. Question: "What about when one is already supported by being the Valedictorian of the Golden Tablet?
The Master said: "In the Eastern Hall, competing for excellence, one knows both bitterness and sweetness; on the northern road, driving sheep in haste, do not calculate the distance. Question:

"When all things are of one color and difficult to distinguish, we pray the Master will reveal it. The Master said: "Even as you add charcoal to the full furnace, you still complain it is cold; you walk upon the road."
People merely cling to the cold. A question was asked: "How far apart are the Way of the Kings and the Way of the Buddhas? The Master said: "When the straw dog barks, heaven and earth merge;
after the wooden cock crows, the ancestral lamp shines. A question was asked: "The Heart-Seal of the Patriarchs—please, Master, wipe it clean for me.
The Master said: "The Patriarchal Moon soars into the void, perfecting holy wisdom; on what mountain would the pines and cypresses not be lush and green?"

Question: What is the functioning of *prajñā*? The Master said: "As soon as the sharp edge is deployed to strike at the shadow of the neck, one already hears the sighs of lamentation for the lost Nirgrantha.
Question: What is the place where a student establishes themselves? The Master said: "The mud ox bellows from the bottom of the well;
the jade hare is startled in the forest. Question: What is the Way (*mārga*)? The Master said: "Before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion."
Jin asked, "What is the person on the Way? The Master said, "Ask the Imperial City Commander. Jin asked, "How far apart are the Way and the person on the Way?
The Master said, "The moon is like a mirror within a gauze screen; the stars are like lamps in the mist.
Jin asked, "What is the nature that remains unchanging while following the flow? The Master said, "Beside the ink-well where the ink is splashed."
Once he fought for victory; his beak was sharp and expectant atop the Azure Terrace. A question was asked: "The ancient melody has no rhyme or meter;
how can one harmonize it? The Master said: "Fine rain falls as sweat flows in the mountain ghosts' caves; the *kāṣāya* covers the face in the village of spirits."
Question: When the radiance of the Seven Stars turns the Milky Way and cuts off the waves of Mount Sumeru and the ocean of Vairocana, what then?
The Master said: "When Bo Le briefly lowers his whip, the common mule boasts of being one of the Eight Divine Steeds. Question: When seeking the tracks of a bird in the sky, what then?
The Master said: "The three kinds of precious chariots are arrayed; call out in a low voice to the people within the house."
The Master ascended the hall and said: "If even a single speck of dust is established, the state and its family will flourish, yet the village elders will frown.

If not even a single speck of dust is established, the state and its family will perish, yet the village elders will be at peace. If you can understand this clearly, you have no share in it; it is entirely the old monk’s."
"Do you wish to recognize the *ācārya*? He struck once on the right side and said, "Right here is the *ācārya*.
"Do you wish to recognize this old monk? He struck once on the left side and said, "Right here is this old monk.
"This old monk and the *ācārya* can both cause all people in the world to attain enlightenment, and we can both cause all people in the world to remain deluded. Thereupon, he descended from his seat.
The Master ascended the hall. A monk asked, "The great assembly has gathered; we pray that the Master will preach the Dharma.

The Master said, "The barefoot man chases the rabbit; the one wearing boots eats the meat. A monk asked, "Without having extensively studied the teachings of the Empty King, may I briefly borrow your wondrous mechanism to test you?
Please speak. The Master said, "White jade is without flaw; Bian He had his feet cut off. A monk asked, "Even if an iron wheel were placed upon your head..."
[The student] turns upward. “How can one ensure that concentration and wisdom are perfectly clear and never miss their time? The Master said: “A toothpick entering the fire is difficult to retrieve;
an elephant-drawn carriage pushing a wheel is already two or three steps behind. [The student] asked: “Before any intention has been formed, how does one distinguish between this and that?
The Master said: “When the tiger in the azure ravine is startled, it is not by forceful snatching; only when the golden-haired lion plants its paws on the ground does it let out a roar.”
Question: Regarding the principle of not harming things, I request the Master to speak directly on it. Master: To split open the belly and expose the heart, yet one is still not awakened.
Question: What is the single phrase for the moment of encounter? Master: Blowing fire with the wind; little effort is required. Question:
When the waters are turbid and unsettled, how can one attain illumination? Master: Not running while going downhill; this is the swift opportunity.
Nan-feng asked: "When one’s true face is presented as it is, how is that? The Master said: "Remove the veil covering your face. He asked:
"What is the breath of a patch-robed monk? The Master said: "Crawling on knees and walking with elbows. When the assembly saw this, they were struck.
Question: "The purple chrysanthemums are half-bloomed; autumn is already late. When the moon is full at noon, what is your intention? The Master said:
"The moon rises over Mount Penglai and all gaze upon it; last night it met with frost, yet you do not know. Question: "What is the traveling gear of a patch-robed monk? The Master said:
"He receives blows upon his head, yet he mumbles on in his mouth. Question: "What is that which is indestructible? The Master said: "He receives blows upon his head, yet he mumbles on in his mouth."
The Master said: "The sound of the shout and the staff outside the gate. Question: "The Wondrous Peak has no divergent paths; as for the solitary wheel, what is its reality? The Master said:
"The whole world is unaware of the stationless station; when the opportunity arises, one must manifest the most profound and mysterious phrase."
The Great Master Jingxin came from the Western Heavens and asked the Master, "A student’s body acts in one way while the mouth speaks in four;
I pray that the Master will perform repentance for me. The Master snapped his fingers once and said, "May your offenses be extinguished! May your offenses be extinguished! He asked again.
"You have traveled throughout both the Western Heaven and this land. What is the matter of daily use? The Master said: "Ghee is smeared on the door;
rock honey guards the wall. The questioner asked: "On Mount Ling, the moon was painted; at Caoxi, the moon was pointed out. Setting aside these two paths, I ask the Master to point directly.
The Master said: "To be without words is not to be mute. The questioner pressed further: "I ask the Master to provide a definitive judgment."
The Master said: "First, cross the Muli River. A monk asked: "What is the word of ultimate truth?
The Master said: "The mind hangs upon the wall.
The Master ascended the hall and said: "If there are those of the highest caliber who each possess their own verification, they need only briefly meet the requirements of this stage."
Those who have not yet attained realization are each individually brilliant; they arise right where they are and perish right where they are, like the cracking of a tortoise shell.
When it cracks, it forms a pattern; when it does not crack, it remains dull. If you wish to crack it but cannot, squeeze it straight down.
The monk asked, "What is the student’s own self? The Master said, "This is your own self. The monk bowed. The Master then struck him.
Question: "What is it like when the dragon penetrates the clear pool? The Master said: "The seal stamps the horse’s tail. Question: "What is it like when one floats or sinks according to nature?
The Master said: "Leading an ox that will not enter the corral. Question: "What is it like when one understands immediately upon becoming still and composed?
The Master said: "Cutting off one's ears and lying in the street. Question: "What is it like when phrases and names are cut off? The Master said: [Silence].
The entire body is subtle and does not emerge. A question was asked: "When the chick pecks and the mother hen pips at the same moment, how is it?
The Master said: "An echo. Question: "When the bright moon is suspended in the sky, how is it? The Master said: "Sleeping on clouds and lying in waters. Question:
"When the smoke of the war-signs has forever ceased, how is it? The Master said: "Both feet pointing toward the void."
The Master ascended the hall and said: "For now, let us rely on the meaning of 'stopping the crying' for those of middling and lower capacity.

But if we speak of the Patriarchal Command, even a blue-eyed barbarian monk appearing here would have to beg for his life. If one says that the command is carried out to its full extent, then one must immediately ask another to look after the *dhāraṇī*.
At that time, a monk asked: "What is it like when the command is carried out? The Master said: "You intend to disperse the assembly."
The monk hesitated; the Master struck him. The monk asked, "When the Patriarch’s mandate is to be carried out, what then? The Master said, "A dot.
The monk asked, "When there is neither existence nor non-existence, and no place to go, what then? The Master said, "For three months, weary of wandering the roads beneath the plum blossoms;
for an entire household, sorrowfully closing the door in the rain. The monk asked, "When there is both existence and non-existence, and a place to go, what then?"
The Master said: "With a sword-like shoulder blade, he surrenders and submits; with an iron-made chest, he reaches the coastal shores. Question:
"What is it like when standing alone in a solitary boat? The Master said: "Meeting a pardon within Sha-men Island; gazing at Wo-zhou from the peak of Hua-zheng. Question:
"What is it like when one is peerless in all the world? The Master said: "The mountain peak marks the tip of the crescent moon."
"Born across the pass of the ghost-gate. Question: "Speech and silence involve departure and subtlety; how can one pass through without transgression? The Master said:
"I long remember the third month in Jiangnan, where the flowers bloom where the partridges cry. Question: "Without employing a single blade,"
[Question: "What is it like when one ascends to the position of the Nine and Five? [Master: "Whipping the corpse and bending the neck. [Question:

"What is it like when ordinary people and sages do not communicate? [Master: "Shaving the head and dividing the offices; departing from Luoyang. [Question: "What is the Seal of the Empty King? [Master:
"Vast and expansive, the net of the Three Emptinesses; its traces leave no path to penetrate."
The Master ascended the hall and said: "I have a pair of arrows; they have not undergone long refinement, nor have they been shot throughout the ten directions, yet for now, no one has seen them.
At that time, a monk asked, "What is the Master’s arrow? The Master made the gesture of drawing a bow.
The monk bowed. The Master said, "Drag this dead man out! A monk asked, "Without stirring human sentiment, please [speak]."
The Master used the whole [phrase]. The Master said, "Cut off your tongue-roots. The student advanced and said, "I request the Master’s direct instruction.
The Master said, "A live-captured tiger; one fears the blind turtle even when it is dead. The student said, "I have not yet understood. How can I attain intimacy?
The Master said, "In the Three Wu regions, the bow is bent at midnight; in the Five Ling tombs, the sword is carried forth at dawn."
The student asked, "How does one enjoy [it]? The Master said, "Cut it off with your hand. The student asked, "What is the phrase that shatters all appearances?
The Master said, "Pick it out. The student asked, "What is the Lord of Lords? The Master said, "Pork pressed upon the heart of the Ancient Buddha.
The student asked, "When the Lion’s Roar is let forth, the spirit is total; what is the meaning of Mañjuśrī brandishing his sword?"
The Master said, "A stroke across the forehead. Question: "What is it like when one transcends all things alone?
The Master said, "If you wish to recognize the pure blade, do not grasp the horn of a sheep. Question: "What is the mouth of Sita that swallows the ten directions?

The Master said, "Leaping into the tiger’s ravine; boarding a fish-boat with broken legs. Question: "What is it like when the royal journey has its limits? The Master said, "A stroke across the forehead."
The Master said, "Five hundred [miles] galloping daily. Question: "What is it like when one obtains a boat and crosses over? The Master said, "Next, you shall reach the edge of the sea.
Question: "What is it like when there is no place to rest the body? The Master said, "The Bear Ear Pagoda opens; there is no guest with a seal.
[The student] stepped forward and asked, "How is it so? The Master said, "Precisely what needs to be cut off. Question: "How is it?"
"This is a mark of a great man. The Master said, "A bright red pauper. The student asked, "I do not understand how he acts in his daily life.
The Master said, "Carrying a basket and holding a staff. The student asked, "What was it like before Ox-head saw the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said, "Spreading out a mat and holding a bowl. The student asked, "What was it like after he saw him? The Master said, "Spreading out a mat and holding a bowl."

The Master ascended the hall and said: "Three thousand swordsmen are ashamed to appear before Zhuang Zhou. With red-browed rebels shoulder-to-shoulder, how could there not be error? When the time comes for the leopard to change its spots, look back after five days.

Be careful. A monk asked: "When the Fragrant Elephant lets out a roar, what then? The Master said: "In the marketplace, even Zeng Shen was suspected of murdering his mother. Another asked: "If the Seal of the Mind is not yet clear, how can one enter it?
The Master said: "In the marketplace, even Zeng Shen was suspected of murdering his mother. (Repeating the previous answer as a response to the lack of clarity.)
The Master said, "Although I have heard that Master Qiou has surrendered his allegiance, I have not yet seen him come with the sheep and the jade tablet. A question was asked:

"If the enlightened ruler does not hold the mirror of Xuanyuan, how can he discern the affairs of the court administration? The Master said, "Since those objects do not come, the pure court is left without its ministers.
A question was asked: "What is the matter under the Linji lineage? The Master said, "The dog of Jie barks at Yao. A question was asked: [The text ends here.]
"Why are the marks of a Great Man not fully possessed? The Master said: "The owl deceives the eagle at midnight. Question:
"What is it like when the military deadline is urgent? The Master said: "Bones and firewood beneath the city of surrender. Question: [Unanswered]
"When one has not yet reached the source, what is it like? The Master said, "A crane, cold, leaves its nest easily; a dragon, cold, leaves its cave with difficulty. Question:
"Regarding the phrase that does not reveal its edge or point, how does one distinguish between host and guest? The Master said, "Mouth holding a ram's horn, stuck with fish-glue.
Question: "When the source of the mind is not yet clear, what is it like? The Master said, "Just as one rejoices at wearing the *xuī* (a child’s sash), one has ascended the *ruò* (the bowstring)."

[The Master] put on his cap, then immediately encountered [the official] who had him shaved bald, his hair cut even with his eyebrows. He asked, "The root source is not yet clear; how can one manifest the Way?
The Master said, "The golden star shines across the wilds, abounding in sharp horns; iron cavalry marches on the frontier, causing great slaughter.

He asked, "The wisdom of differentiation is not yet clear; how can one attain freedom from doubt? The Master said, "As long as the wheel of suffering has not ceased, it is difficult to dispel the slaughter. [Only at] the Terrace of Ambrosia [is it possible]."

Formerly, when his arm was severed, he asked: "When one uses the body to navigate perilous terrain, how is it? The Master said: "The long proclamation of the manifest document writes out the source of transgressions.
He further asked: "At such a time as this, what would you call it? The Master said: "Entering and exiting while shaking the bell, always maintaining the true execution. He asked:
"If one does not cultivate meditative concentration, why is there no doubt that one will attain Buddhahood? The Master said: [He remained silent.]

[The Master] said: "The golden rooster exclusively announces the dawn; the black lacquer bucket produces light at night. A question was asked: "When the mist rolls up and the clouds are withdrawn, what then?
The Master said: "Blind in the midst of the blue sky. A question was asked: "Deer and elk gather in herds;

how does one shoot the Lord of Lords? The Master said: "The fishing boat carries one to the banks of the Xiao and Xiang rivers; breath choked and despondent, one asks the white gulls. A question was asked.

The student asked a question about a confusing and contentious phrase, requesting the Master to manifest his marvelous faculty. The Master said: "It is clear within the mind, yet the eyes are dark. The student asked:
"When the time of birth and death arrives, what then? The Master said: "A blue cloth cut into a shirt invites the dog's bark. The student pressed further:
"How can one ensure it does not bark? The Master said: "It is better to let the sleeves hang down in silence."
Wusheng asked: "How is it when the great bell has not yet been struck? The Master said: "The myriad realms are filled to overflowing; there is nothing that does not resonate with subtle wonder.

Containing the profound within its depths, how could ordinary wisdom discern it? He further asked: "How is it after it has been struck? The Master said: "Stone walls and mountain rivers present no obstruction.
After hearing it echoing through the clouds, one should inquire further. He asked: "When the lotus flower has not yet emerged from the water..."
"How is it? The Master said, "One has not yet transcended the turbid water; one is not invaded by the mud. The student asked, "What is it like after emerging from the water?
The Master said, "Though the solitary wheel is distinct, the lotuses are no longer fresh. The student asked, "What is it like after they have fully blossomed?
The Master said, "Worn upon the head of the Water God; its beauty must not be sought or grasped. [The student] asked, "As for..."
"What is this matter of face-to-face encounter? The Master said, "I know not what year or month. "I see again the slopes of Mawei.
The student asked, "What is a true person on the Way? The Master said, "Worshipping the Western Paradise atop the tip of a bamboo pole.
The student asked, "In the midst of the vast and chaotic, how does one discern the host? The Master said, "The eyeless immortal can palpate bones; he opens his shop in the bustling marketplace."
[The monk] grasped [the Master’s] hand in surprise. [The Master] asked, "What is the place from which the Buddhas of the three periods emerge?
The Master said, "Turn your head and look at the dragon throne. He then asked the messenger who had previously arrived, "When a fish hides in a deep pool, what then? The Master said, [silently].
“Scalding in hot water and burning with fire. A question was asked: “What is the point of intimacy for a student? The Master said:
“Beating drums together on the southern side of Mount Sumeru; drying leather balls beneath Mount Helan. A question was asked:
“Within the secret chamber, what is the Way? The Master said: “The moon beyond the pines piercing the heavens; the evening glow penetrating the room. A question was asked: “What are all things?”
[The Master] said: "Where the Buddha travels. Question: "What is the place where the Buddhas of the three periods emerge?
The Master said: "The three peaks of Mount Hua touch the ground; the Emperor of Great Peace is often startled.
Question: "What is the Dharma-body Buddha? The Master said: "The Mengjin Pass is not far; it is best to lie down."
The Tathāgata asked: "Yesterday, while playing with the children, I inadvertently offended you, Master; were you angry? The Master said:
"The iron wedge bursts open, the snake's belly gapes, and the sound of *sè-máo* (a rattling or hissing) is clearly revealed. He asked: "What is a great *kalyāṇamitra* (virtuous friend)?
The Master said: "Killing people without blinking an eye. He pressed further: "Since he is a great *kalyāṇamitra*..."
[The student] said, "Master, why do you kill people without blinking? The Master said, "In the midst of dust and shadows, one does not brush away the sleeves;
before the raised halberds, one grinds an inch of gold."
Daobao of Ruizhou asked the Master, "Every day you lead the assembly in chanting; what is the essential principle [of this]?
The Master said, "The auspicious grass has no root from the start; I take it up and use it as my hand reaches it. He further asked, "I do not know what it is that is used.
The Master said, "A thousand ways to manifest the meaning are difficult to clarify; a single point is distinct, smiling at the spring sun. He asked again, "And..."
Baoshou asked, "How many years old are you? The Master said, "A tree does not manifest its own name; now there is nothing that cannot be attained.
Baoshou further asked, "I do not yet understand: exactly how many years is it? The Master said, "This old monk is seventy-three years old. Baoshou said, "So there was actually a specific number.
The Master said, "Had I known what matters would be today, I would have regretted not being more careful in the beginning. Baoshou asked again.

Baoyun said, "If one discusses this matter, one must not duck behind a sword or dodge an arrow; one must simply bring it all together so that even a thousand bows and ten thousand arrows cannot strike it.
The Master said, "Only when a thousand bows and ten thousand arrows cannot strike it can one succeed.
Baoyun said, "I do not yet understand: what kind of human power does that which cannot be struck possess? The Master said, "It is the lion shaking its majestic aura."
[The Master] was bound. The Elephant King leaped up and pulled out his tusks. Baoyun said, "Is there still something above this?
The Master said, "There is. Baoyun said, "What is the matter above this? The Master said, "Even turning one's body, there is still a path."
To transcend the body and realize the Way must be difficult.
The Master ascended the hall and said: "The World-Honored One’s samādhi—Kāśyapa did not know it. Kāśyapa’s samādhi—Ānanda did not know it."
Ānanda’s samādhi was unknown to Śāṇakavāsin; even up until my own samādhi, you have likewise not known it. Once, a monk asked:
"I wonder, Master, who can know your samādhi? The Master said: "True gold does not require testing in a furnace;
its original brilliance is fresh through and through. The monk asked: "At night in the darkness, it is not hidden; by day..."

At such a time as this, is there still a distinction between guest and host? The Master said: "Zhang Qian severed the dragon's head upon the river.
