Question: "He constantly rides a fine steed through the city markets; he does not guard the withered pine tree or gaze at the lunar disc."
"How so? The Master said, "Before the waterfall cliff, a ghost hurls a bowl. The student asked, "What can be done when the whole world is helpless?
The Master said, "A fine livelihood in the depths of the turbulent clouds. [The student] asked, "One is six; six is one."
"Question: When both 'one' and 'six' have perished, what then? The Master said: 'A single arrow brings down two vultures. The student asked: 'What is the underlying meaning? The Master said:
'The body is gone and the traces have vanished. Question: "The twelve divisions of the teachings are the peripheral; what is the direct approach? The Master said:
"The mechanism of biting the arrowhead must be applied with precision. The student said: "What is the underlying meaning?"
The Master said, "From the side, it comes to the front; the sound is empty. The Master asked a monk, "The sound comes before;
where does the phrase end? The monk said, "Yes. The Master said, "The tip of the spear is hidden in the sleeve; there is no fixed place. Your tomb has been overturned twice, and the flag is lowered.
The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "You have entered the cage. He was asked, "Wandering alone within the ocean of the Flower Treasury."
"How is it at this time? The Master said, "Urgent! "Question: What is the first phrase? The Master said, "The seal of the Three Essentials opens;
the vermilion dot is narrow. There is no room for hesitation; host and guest remain. He then gave a shout. "Question: What is the second phrase?
The Master said, "How could a subtle understanding allow for the question of Wuzhuo? The song and response compete to give rise to the mechanism that cuts off the stream. (He did not finish.)
[The student] having previously asked incorrectly, now asks: "What is the third phrase? The Master says: "Just look at the puppeteer on the stage manipulating the puppets;
all the pulling and tugging comes from someone within. To explain this through intellectual analysis is not permitted.

The Imperial Secretary Ouyang of Western Shu asked: "The Dharma King’s Heart-Seal was brought here by Bodhidharma and transmitted by the Fifth Patriarch to Caoxi. Since then, the robe and bowl have not been passed on. I wonder, from whom did you, Master, receive it? The Master replied with a verse:

The Dharma is not a thing that can be transmitted; How could it be contained within a robe? Since ancient times, the Buddhas and patriarchs Have never spoken of it as a secret. If you wish to know the true source, Look directly at your own face. If you can see it clearly right now, Then you will understand the meaning of the Heart-Seal.
The tradition of being able to endure has been passed down for barely two or three generations; as for the robes and bowl of faith and practice, who else can carry them?
Clearly, beyond the thousand lamps of successive ages, from whom was this obtained?

How can one bear to ask again? When ancients met, they strictly avoided revealing their "heads"; they did not expose the edge of their words—how could one know the essential meaning? The Master composed a verse:
The answer says:
Before the Terrace of Ambrosia, there is nothing one does not encounter;
having escaped the terrors of light and darkness that blind and deafen, one was originally relegated to the place where Mañjuśrī dwells—this old fellow of Hanshan makes one laugh to death!
He asked again: "The Suchness remains unmoving, yet the cycle of rebirth turns without end. When the five aggregates perish, upon what does one rely for support?
The Master answered in verse:
"Densely and profoundly majestic, it pervades every place; It is all because of deluded consciousness that it grasps at floating bubbles."
Over three thousand wild flowers of the marsh bloom in profusion; how extraordinary it is that he met Shitou by natural course!
When a monk asked him a question, he had two verses:
"The myriad dharmas are empty and void, the ultimate reality is profound; Steadfast and unmoving, if delusion is severed, there is neither distance nor intimacy."
For those traveling the path of the wondrous principle that severs permanence and annihilation, The mirror-image should be supported by frequent awakening and illumination.
The myriad forms—square and round—are present before the moon; Lower your head in contemplation, and the ten thousand layers shall open.
The "hair-cutting" blade cannot be compared to the sharpness of Mohe; A single point radiates light throughout the great chiliocosm.
While Chan Master An of Yingqiao in汝州 (Ruzhou) was sitting inside the meditation hall by the brazier, Minister Zhong came to visit him.
He asked, "The three realms are ablaze; how can one escape? The Master used his incense spoon to poke at the fire and said, "Minister! Minister!
Later, because a monk went to pay his respects to the Great Master Jingguo of Huguo Monastery in Suizhou, Huguo asked him, "Where have you come from?"
The monk said, "I have come from Nan-yuan in汝州 (Ruzhou). Guo said, "How are things at Nan-yuan these days?
The monk said, "Please try to say something, Master. Guo then gave a shout. The monk also gave a shout.
Guo said, "Stop! Stop! One shout from Huoguo is Huoguo’s command; as for your shout, Elder, what is it? The monk said, "Its function is the same as the Master’s."
When National Teacher Huiguo saw his father, the Master, he said, "Look at this blind donkey and his kind of understanding!

He then struck him and drove him out of the monastery. When that monk reached the top of this ridge, he encountered the Master; recognizing him, he sat down and recounted the preceding incident to the Master.
The Master said, "Did you see how National Teacher’s staff broke? The Master then followed him to Huguo as well.
National Teacher Huiguo saw him coming and asked, "Where have you recently departed from? The Master said, "Ruzhou.
Huiguo said, "May I ask you a question? The Master said, "Shut your dog's mouth! Huiguo then desisted.
A monk asked, "What is the Master’s intimate way of helping people? The Master raised his staff. The monk hesitated.
The Master then struck him.
*Tiansheng Guangdeng Lu*, Scroll Fifteen;
*Tiansheng Guangdeng Lu*, Scroll Sixteen. [Compiled during the Song Dynasty]
When Chan Master Jing of Xingyang Mountain in Yingzhou first visited Xiyan, he asked, "What is it like when one intends to ask but does not ask?
Xiyan struck him immediately. The Master remained silent for a long while. Xiyan said, "If you call this a staff, your eyebrows and whiskers will fall off.
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. When the Master ascended the seat to open the hall, a monk asked, "Whose song does the Master sing?"
Song: Whom does the ancestral style succeed? The Master said: "Before the mountain of Shaoshi, there is no divergent path.
On the day of the opening of the hall at Guanghui Chan Monastery in Ruizhou, a monk asked: "What is the realm of Guanghui?"
The Master said, "Before the small temple; after Ziqing. A question was asked: "What is the patriarchal style of the Master's house?

The Master said, "The hoe and the broom. When the Master was at Fengxue, one day Fengxue asked, "Zhen, the head gardener, when the Huichang persecution of the Dharma occurred, where did the Dharma-protecting deities go? The Master said, "They are always in the midst of the marketplace."
"Essentially, no one sees him. Fengxue said, "You have thoroughly penetrated it.
Chan Master Shengnian of Baoying Chan Monastery in Ruzhou was a native of Lai Prefecture. His secular surname was Di.
He received his monastic training at Nan Chan Monastery in his home prefecture and attained the Dharma from Fengxue.

When the Master first opened the hall, he ascended the seat and said: "The Buddha-dharma has been entrusted to kings, ministers, and powerful patrons so that the Dharma may not be severed, with lamp following lamp in succession down to this very day. O Great Assembly, tell me: what is it that continues?"
After a long silence, he said, "It must be my elder brother Kāśyapa. At that time, a monk asked, "What is different about this assembly at Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa compared to today?
The Master said, "Falling into a pit, falling into a ditch. The monk pressed further, "Why is it so? The Master said, "Blind!
A monk asked, "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind do you succeed? The Master said, "Shaoshi (the Small Room)."
Before the cliff, [the Master] personally held up his palm and showed it. The student said, "I pray you further harmonize this with one more loud sound.
The Master said, "I want everyone to know. Question: "What is the Master’s family style? The Master said: "A single word cuts off the mouths of a thousand rivers;
only before a ten-thousand-fathom peak does the mystery begin. Question: "What is the realm of Shoushan? The Master said: [He remained silent.]
"Let everyone look as they please. A monk stepped forward and asked, "What is it like to be a person within the realm? The Master said, "Even getting a beating would be too much for you.
The monk bowed, and the Master said, "Wait until another time for that beating. A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "At the edge of the city of King Chu, the Ru River flows eastward. A monk asked, "Regarding all the patriarchs of the past..."
The Master said, "Plowing with the plow and pulling the harrow. Question: "What was the meaning when the ancients raised their mallets and brandished their fly-whisks?
The Master said, "There are no overnight guests on the solitary peak. The questioner pressed further: "I do not yet understand how this principle works.
The Master said, "One who is not a person merely waiting by a stump. Question: "What is Shoushan? The Master said—
The Master said, "The eastern mountain is high; the western mountain is low. The monk asked, "What is it like to be among the mountains?
The Master said, "It happens that the staff is not here. The monk bowed, and the Master struck him. A monk asked, "What is the Way?
The Master said, "In the hearth there is fire, though no one stirs it; everywhere one traverses freely as one pleases. The monk asked further, "How is this so?"
"A traveler on this path. The Master said: "Sit and behold the beauty of the mist and clouds; it does not level with the floating clouds. Question:
"At the place where all the sages have failed to reach, we ask the Master to proclaim it. The Master said: "The divine light of ten thousand miles shines as one;
who dares to rival the sun in its brilliance? Question: "Before the precious sword has emerged from its scabbard, what is it like? The Master said: "The great ocean."
"The Sea-Bottom Mirror of Clarified Mind. The student asked, "What is it like after it has been removed from its case? The Master said, "Beyond the heavens, *ṭhakka-sa*, alone swinging the oar.
The student asked, "What is it like when the precious sword has not yet emerged from its case? The Master said, "It might still be possible if you did not begrudge [the truth].
The student asked, "What is it like after it has been removed from its case? The Master said, "I humbly pray that you may continue to enjoy [this offering]. The student asked, "How is it?"
"This Way. The Master said: "Three feet deep beneath one's feet. Question: "How is it when the lotus flower has not yet emerged from the water?
The Master said: "The water is ten feet deep. [The student] further asked: "How is it after it has emerged? The Master said: "It stands three feet above the ground. Question:
"What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas? The Master said: "Three old ladies standing in formation."
Prostrations. The Master ascended the hall and said: "If you wish to attain intimacy, do not bring questions to ask. The question lies within the answer; the answer lies within the question.
If you bring forth the gate, I, the old monk, am beneath your feet. If you hesitate to deliberate, there will be no connection."
At that time, a monk came forward to pay his respects. The Master struck him. The monk did not retreat, but asked, "What is it like when one hangs up one's staff in a secluded crag?
The Master said, "Wrong. The student said, "Wrong. The Master struck him again. He asked, "How does emptiness serve as the essence?
The Master said, "I, the old monk, am beneath your feet. The student stepped forward and asked, "Why, Preceptor..."

"Where is Ma? [The Master] said, "I know you are a blind fellow. Later, the monk entered the room to ask for instruction, saying, "As for what you said, 'The old monk is under your feet,' what is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "Lying across the body, not shrinking from wading through mud and water;
casting off the whole person to await a true adept. The monk further asked, "I know you are a... [The Master] said, "A blind fellow."
“Blind fellow! What is the meaning of this? The Master said, “One offers a treasure to the ruler, yet the person does not recognize it;

instead, one causes the blind man to fall into lifelong blindness. A student asked, “What is it like when all is serene and still? The Master said, “If you have not yet clarified the truth within the mind, you will not pass the barrier of Shoushan.
As the student was about to offer a word in response, the Master struck him. A student asked, “When not even a single hair has yet emerged...”
"How is it? The Master said, "Meeting a person with pierced ears on the road. The student asked, "What about after setting out?
The Master said, "There is no need for further hesitation. A question was asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "The wind blows and the eyes are scorched. Court Official An Hongjian asked, "When not a single thing can be brought forth, what then? The Master said: [silence].
"How can you speak such falsehoods before the assembly? Jian said this as he prepared to deliberate [on the matter], and the Master struck him.
Jian asked again, "The Dharma abides in its own place; the characteristics of the world are eternally abiding. What is this eternally abiding Dharma?
The Master held up his staff and said, "Tell me, does it abide or not abide? Jian said, "How can those who have not yet attained understanding comprehend this?"
The Master said, "Vaguely resembling a melody, it is just barely fit to be heard; yet it is blown by the wind into another tune. He asked again, "I, your disciple, do not understand;
I ask you to instruct me. The Master said, "The water is swift and the waves part, and the fish appear of themselves;
the golden-scaled one leaps through into the azure depths."
The Master ascended the hall and said, "If one discusses this matter, it does not hang upon a single word. At that time, a monk asked, "What was the meaning behind Baizhang rolling up his mat?
The Master said, "When the dragon’s sleeve is swept aside, the entire body is revealed. The monk pressed further, "And what about your own intention, Master?
The Master said, "Where the Elephant King walks, the tracks of the foxes are cut off. There was an official, Officer Liu, who asked, "The Dragon..."

In the *Ting Jinshi Wèn* (Questions from the Hall of Stone and Metal), it is asked: "How does one respond to the Jade Mechanism? The Master said: "A single wheel transcends far beyond the three realms;

facing the window, it shines through the doors of ten thousand households. On the day of his departure, [the questioner] asked again: "I request the Master’s instruction on a single phrase for my final journey."
The Master patted him on the back once with his hand. The monk stepped forward and said, "Do not mistake the weight of the scale.
The Master ascended the hall and said, "Venerable seniors, do not shout blindly or shout recklessly. Here, I have always told you this."
The guest remains the guest from beginning to end; the host remains the host from beginning to end. There is no second guest, nor is there a second host.
If there were two guests or two hosts, they would simply be two blind men. It is also said: "When I stand, you must sit;
when I sit, you must stand. When sitting, I sit together with you; when standing, I stand together with you. Nevertheless...
It is so. Upon arriving here, you must keep your eyes wide open. If your eyes blink or waver, then you are already a thousand or ten thousand miles away.
Why is this? It is like looking at a horseman through a window; if you hesitate, there is no connection. All you venerable seniors!
Since you have focused your attention here, you must be thorough and precise; do not engage in empty pretense. Otherwise, at some future time, it will deceive all of you.
If you have business, come forward; if you have no business, return to the hall.
The Master ascended the hall. A monk asked, "All day long one is in a state of bustle; how is it that 'that matter' is not hindered?
The Master said, "A thousand blossoms flourish atop the solitary peak; one walks where ten-thousand-fathom cliffs are steep and perilous.

The monk stepped forward and asked, "Is this not precisely the place for a student of the Way? The Master said, "The great assembly sings the song of farewell; the thousand peaks shall never again be seen."

[The student] turns back and says, "As for that matter which has been turned back, how is it? The Master says, "Even if my bones were ground to powder and my body shattered to pieces, I would still not let it go.
Once every three years, they send money and goods. The student bows. The Master says, "Heh! Heh!"
Question: "What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas? The Master said: "The radish of Zhenzhou weighs three catties. At the end of summer, he composed a verse for the monks who remained with him:
"This year I have reached sixty-seven; Old age and illness accompany me as I pass the days."
"Record this year so that next autumn it may be remembered; record next year so that the month and year thereafter may be known.
On the fourth day of the twelfth month in the fourth year of the Chunhua era, the Master ascended the hall and spoke two verses to the assembly, saying:
The various sons wander aimlessly through many Ganges Rivers; though Avalokiteśvara points toward Maitreya and Mañjuśrī, they are helpless.
Furthermore, in the world of white silver, there is a golden body; sentient and insentient beings share in one true reality.
"When light and darkness are both exhausted, there is nothing to be illumined; at midday, the solar orb reveals its entire body.
Having spoken these words, the Master sat in the lotus posture upon the Dharma seat and entered nirvana. His secular age was sixty-seven, and his monastic seniority was forty-nine.
After his cremation, his relics were collected and a stupa was erected at his home mountain.
Chan Master Man of Changxing Chan Monastery in Fengxiang Prefecture ascends the hall. A monk asks: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind do you succeed? The Master says:
"On the shores of the four seas, there was once a lack of excellence. The monk presses: "The student does not understand this meaning;
what is it? The Master says: "Having lost the oars and rudders until this very day. [Another] asks: "What is..."
"An ancient Buddha’s site of practice. The Master said, "If you walk, you step right upon it. The student asked, "What is it like after stepping upon it?
The Master said, "The ice melts and the walls crumble. The student asked, "Why is it so? The Master said, "A gentleman in the city."
A young boy outside the city walls asked, "What is the 'blow-off-hair sword'? The Master said, "It cannot be touched or struck. The boy pressed further, "And what of one who uses it?
The Master said, "One's bones would be ground to powder and one's body shattered. The boy remarked, "Truly excellent that it cannot be touched or struck!
The Master then struck him. Another asked, "What is a pure monastery? The Master said, "The entire courtyard is full."
[The Master] added a fly to his foot. A monk asked, "What is your 'bright pearl in the sea'? The Master said, "It cannot be looked upon.
The monk stepped forward and said, "Do you permit this student to draw near to it? The Master said, "How would you draw near?
The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "I grant you one point. As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him. [A monk] asked, "The Great..."
"How is it when [the truth] is manifest? The Master said: "Rolling about in the midst of a bustling marketplace.
Zen Master Lingquan of Tanzhou ascended the hall. A monk asked: "From patriarch to patriarch, what is transmitted? And as for you, Master, whose dharma heir are you now?
The Master said: "Grasping and lifting do not fall within the hands. The monk pressed further: "I wonder, in the end..."
[The monk] asked, "Who is the successor? The Master said, "When there is need, one acts with total freedom.
[The monk] asked, "I have heard the former master say, 'The horse-herding woman on the sands of Jinshe. What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Outside the East Gate, the people are countless.
[The monk] further asked, "If one understands it in this way, what then? The Master said, "On the Tianjin Bridge, those passing to and fro are many."
Question: "Since this is a sacred spring, why does it flow as a long stream? The Master said: "There is no place for you to put your mouth.
The student asked: "What about those who drink from it? The Master said: "Not even a drop is suitable. Question: "What is the Master’s livelihood? The Master said: "There is not a single thing.
The student asked: "I do not understand; what things are used in daily life? The Master said: [The text here ends abruptly.]
He then shouted. The monks prostrated, and the Master struck them. When asked, "What if one brings nothing at all?
the Master said, "The sleeves hang down on both sides."
Chan Master Huai-zhi of Qianming Monastery at Shou Mountain in汝州 (Ruzhou) ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the seamless stupa?
The Master said, "On the southern bank of the Yellow River, at Pucheng Town. The monk pressed further, "Who is inside the stupa?
The Master said, "Countless idle fields belong to the Liu family. A monk asked, "What is the Patriarch from the West? The Master said, [as above].
Regarding the intent of the inquiry, the Master said: "A three-foot staff and a broken tile bowl. Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said:
"The bottom of the bucket has fallen off. Question: "What is the realm of Shoushan? The Master said: "North of Jiangdian is Gaoyang Mountain.
He further asked: "Who is within that realm? The Master said: "The two mountain monks come and go constantly."
Chan Master Guisong of Guangjiao Monastery in Ye County,汝州 (Ruzhou), was a native of Jizhou. His surname was Jia.
When he reached the age of twenty, he left the household life and received full ordination at Baoshou Monastery in Yizhou. Later, he traveled south to visit Chan Master Xingnian of Ruzhou.
Upon seeing him arrive, the Master held up a bamboo stick and said, "You must not call this a bamboo stick."
"If you call it a bamboo whisk, you hit [the mark]; if you do not call it a bamboo whisk, you turn your back. "What shall I call it?
The Master stepped forward, seized it, and threw it down the steps, saying, "Where is it? Nan said, "Blind! At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
He remained by the Master's side, attending to him with towel and pitcher for several years.

On the day the Master opened the hall, he held up the incense and said: "This one portion of incense was not obtained from another land; it is simply the water and soil of汝州 (Ruzhou). A question was asked:
"The patriarchs have transmitted the patriarchal seal to one another in succession; whom does the Master now take as his Dharma heir? The Master replied: [He remained silent.]
"The Son of Heaven within the realm; the General beyond the passes. The student said, "You have received one drop of the profound mystery from your teacher.

As for the 'atmosphere' of the Ultimate Direction—what is it like? The Master said, "Fan Kuai’s rage before the Hall of the High Ancestor; you must know that ten thousand miles away, smoke and dust are utterly absent.
The student asked, "In the past, when the World-Honored One preached the Dharma, Brahma King attended in person. On this day, the Imperial Mounts arrive at the assembly."
"What instructions do you have for me? The Master said, "When the cold geese pass by, their cries are choked; the magpies chatter, delighting people to death.
The student further asked, "If that is so, then the Dharma rain falls deeply, and humans and devas have something to rely upon.

The Master said, "Clouds part to reveal the moon in every house; spring comes and flowers bloom everywhere. The student asked, "Without falling into conceptual categories, please speak directly, Master. The Master said: [He remained silent.]
[The Master] said, "Clouds fall. A question was asked: "What is it to be a renunciant? The Master said, "Tightly inside. The student further asked:
"In that case, is there both 'at home' and 'renunciation'? The Master said, "Deer-skin sandals. A question was asked: "What is the seamless stupa?
The Master said, "Hair not combed; face not washed. A question was asked: "Having consumed the food offered by a donor, with what shall one repay them?"
The Master replied, “This old monk has committed a transgression. The student pressed further, “If that is so, then even ten thousand taels of gold could not repay it.
The Master said, “Family disgrace is not to be broadcast abroad. A student asked, “What is the livelihood of a monk in his sleeves?

The monk said, "If that is so, then I thank the Master for personally opening the gate of expedient means. The Master— [remained silent].
[The Master] said: "Do not forget this even after ten million years. A question was asked: "What is it like when the numinous tortoise has not yet shown its signs? The Master said:
"Rowing a boat upon the sea, one smiles while looking toward the journey ahead. A question was asked: "The nectar-water is sprinkled repeatedly;
why do the hundred grasses fail to sprout? The Master said: "When the fields are parched, they cannot hold water; what can the Dragon King do about that?"
Question: "As the cold and heat gradually intensify, on what does the poor person rely? The Master said: "Unattached to the private matters of the world, all day long he laughs with joy.
The student said: "If that is so, then he must not be left exposed. The Master said: "He cannot be hidden in deep ravines;
he reveals no form upon the open ground. Question: "What is the site of enlightenment (dōjō)? The Master said: "One must not set foot there."
Question: "When one has not awakened to the ancestral source and does not believe in the Great Way, what is it like?
The Master said: "Shatter the lapis lazuli egg; let the phoenix chick fly forth. The student said: "Today I have personally seen the Master. The Master said:

The Master said, "Raising his hand, he did not grasp the bow; lowering his head, he lost the arrow. The student asked, "The Master is a great *kalyāṇamitra*.
Why do you act like this? The Master said, "A defeated general is not executed. The student asked, "I wish to soar into the clouds and mists.
Once I have arrived there, how shall I act for the sake of sentient beings? The Master said, "The General Beyond the Frontier carries out the true command."
Unfurling the red banner, he returns victorious. The student asked: "With nothing obstructing one's path before, why is it that one cannot open one's mouth?

A monk asked, "What is the matter beneath the patched robe? The Master said, "A stark naked pauper. The monk said, "I beg the Master for a skillful means;
please point out a wondrous and swift phrase for me to see. The Master said, "A wooden woman threading a needle."
The mountain scenery is exquisite; a famous man draws the line, and sea-clouds arise. [A student] asks: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?

The moon is three feet deep; a boat travels ten thousand *li* on dry land. Xue said, "What kind of mental activity is this, Master?
The Master said, "It is actually your own mental activity."

The Master traveled extensively through various monasteries and attained a profound mastery of their deep principles. While conversing with Master Jie about the essential points of the Cao-Dong school, he remarked:
"In seeking the five ranks, one must know the vital essentials; The slightest movement of thought already constitutes a deviation."
Who can penetrate the Vajra casket? Only Nalakuvara possesses the foremost faculty.
A single glance causes the three realms to fall silent; shaking his bell, he causes the nine heavens to return to their source.
Within the center, the wondrous skillful means interpenetrate; yet as soon as one attempts to grasp it, its sharp edge loses its power.
The Master had just finished composing his verses on the Five Ranks when a monk asked: "What is 'coming from within the center'? The Master said:
"Stemless lotuses bloom in clusters upon dry land. The student asked: "What is it like after they have bloomed? The Master said:
"Golden stamens and silver filaments receive the jade dew; the eminent monk does not sit upon the phoenix terrace. [The monk] asked: "What is 'the partial within the center'?"
The Master said: "The jade hare seeks brightness after the first watch of night; the golden rooster must announce the fifth watch before dawn.
Question: "What is 'correcting within partiality'? The Master said: "A mere hair grows into a great tree; a drop of water becomes a river. Question:
"What is 'arriving within the comprehensive'? The Master said: "One's spirit and will are not obtained from heaven and earth; how could a hero rely on the four seasons?"
Zhui asked, "What is it to arrive within the 'Simultaneous'? The Master said, "The jade maiden casts her shuttle, the loom whirrs;
the stone man beats the drum, the sound rings out. Because a monk had requested instruction, the Master subsequently composed verses for each stage, saying:
Coming from the Center: The Vajra-jewel sword sweeps open the heavens;
A single flash of divine light spans the world, Its crystalline brilliance shining brightly, free from all dust.
Deviation from the Center: The thunderbolt’s sharp mechanism—look with your own eyes!
Even sparks from flint and flashes of lightning are dull; If you deliberate or hesitate, ten thousand mountains stand between you.
Observe the Universal Monarch as he exercises his rightful command:
The seven precious treasures and a thousand sons all follow him, Yet even on the road, he still seeks the golden mirror.
Simultaneously Reaching the Center: The three-year-old golden-haired lion has its fangs and claws fully prepared;
when a thousand evils and a hundred monsters emerge, a single roar causes them all to prostrate on the ground.
Simultaneously Arriving at the Center: Greatly manifesting the state of no-effort, cease all contriving and creating.
The wooden ox walks step by step through fire; Truly, the Dharma King is the most wondrous among wonders.
In the Verse on the Six Characteristics, seeing is Aniruddha; Clearly, there is not a single thing— Neither the great earth nor the mountains and rivers.
The performance of the pāramitās—having heard this, Bhadanta, the sound penetrates all without distinction;
whether far or near, it is understood simultaneously. One no longer thinks of "Mahā" [Mahāprajāpatī];

this fragrance is that of the daughter of the Gaṅgā, whose heart of compassion is all-pervasive, capable of knowing both the pure and the defiled entirely. She is none other than the mother of us all.

To speak of the Way is already a mistake; To seek the Way is a further error. If you can avoid these two errors, You will naturally attain liberation. Do not look for it in the ten directions; Do not seek it within yourself. If you can let go of both self and other, You will find the Way right where you stand. Relying on yourself and practicing alone, You will achieve the Great Matter. Do not be deluded by appearances; Do not be attached to forms. Forms are empty and false; They are but passing illusions. If you can see through these illusions, You will transcend birth and death. Do not seek the Way in books; Do not study it in words. Words are like echoes in a valley; They have no real substance. If you can cast away words and letters, You will see the true nature of reality. True reality is beyond thought; It is ineffable and silent. Silent and unmoving, It is the source of all things. Do not be distracted by worldly affairs; Do not be entangled in delusions. Cut off all attachments, And you will attain peace and joy. Peace and joy are the Way; The Way is peace and joy. Do not wait for the future; Do not hope for the past. In the present moment, The Way is manifest. Manifest yet ungraspable, It is the ultimate truth. Ultimate truth is beyond speech; It is realized only through practice. Practice with single-mindedness, And you will reach the goal. Do not be swayed by doubts; Do not be led astray by views. Non-dual and non-conceptual, This is the state of the Way. To dwell in this state, Is to dwell in the ultimate. The ultimate is ineffable; It cannot be described. To describe it is to miss it; To seek it is to lose it. Let go of seeking and describing, And you will find the Way. The Way is not far; It is right here. Right here, Do not hesitate. Does this mean that each person individually wears a separate robe and eats from their own pot? This is a partial view.
Do you know that the Buddhas of the three periods of time all wear a single robe together? Therefore, although Śākyamuni Buddha was sixteen feet tall, he left his *kāṣāya* to Maitreya. Maitreya...
The robe fits those who are a thousand feet tall exactly; why is this so? It is because for those with a long Dharma-body, it is long, and for those with a short Dharma-body, it is short.
Do you wish to understand this easily? The ancient Buddha intersects with the pillar; the Buddha Hall vies with the Heavenly King for the forehead.
If you do not understand this, you will suffer a single, heavy failure. Take care!
The Master ascended the hall and said: "Sometimes a single shout is used as nothing more than a shout; sometimes a single shout serves as a probing pole or a decoy blade of grass;

If it is the Vajra King’s precious sword, you must not look at it with your true eye; to look at it is to lose your life."
The Master then offered this verse:
"It was not forged by Ganjiang; What need is there for the four winds to blow? The green serpent roars within its scabbard;
Whenever a demon is encountered, wield it at will. If one can maintain total mastery, How could one fail to act at the critical moment?"
Vairocana was so startled that he fled; the great assembly all knit their brows and stood for a long time.

"Take care," said the Master as he ascended the hall. He addressed the assembly, saying: "Dagui received the Great Mallet from his predecessor; those who wander on the clouds and waters of the Five Lakes vie with one another to rush forward."
They vie with one another in their headlong rush; what gate is there for them? Striking the arrow, how could one know that the rotten wood remains?

That the rotten wood remains—within a single year, it has already seen spring twice. Spring coming twice—pearls are scattered from within the curtains for all to take. Pearls scattered for others—one reflects that this too is merely a longing for Xiqin. Be careful.
The Master ascended the hall and said: "In the past, a non-Buddhist asked the Buddha, 'I do not ask about words, nor do I ask about wordlessness.

The World-Honored One simply remained seated upon his mat. The non-Buddhist then said, 'The World-Honored One, in his great kindness and compassion, has cleared away my clouds of delusion and enabled me to enter.
[The Master continued: 'How great was this World-Honored One, yet he was thoroughly hoodwinked by that non-Buddhist! As for what the non-Buddhist said, "He has cleared away my..."'"
"The clouds of delusion have allowed me to enter. But tell me, have you entered yet? Do you wish to understand? You have never seen it even in a dream.

The Master ascended the hall and said: A monk asked the Abbot of Fenzhou, "What is the phrase for receiving a beginner?

[He replied,] "Bringing it from a thousand miles away to present one's old face. "What is the phrase for establishing heaven and earth? [He replied,] "North Kuru."
"In the continent of Jambudvīpa, there grows long-grain non-glutinous rice; those who eat it have neither greed nor caution.

The Master then said, "I shall use these four lines of verse to test the monks of the world. Consider them carefully! Before long, the monks of the world all scrutinized these four lines of verse and were simultaneously exposed. Take care!

The Master ascended the hall. Hearing the sound of the bell, he said: "Those who enter through the Gate of Avalokiteśvara are like shrimp, frogs, and earthworms; they assist you in triggering the awakening. Those who enter through the Gate of Samantabhadra arrive without moving a step. Is there anyone here now who has arrived? After a long silence, as no one responded, he struck the meditation seat once with his staff and uttered this verse:

The gate of Avalokiteśvara Is the realm of shrimp, frogs, and earthworms. The gate of Samantabhadra Reaches here without moving a foot. If you can pass through both gates, Then you are truly a person of the Way. If you cannot pass through both gates, You are merely a fellow of the common crowd. At the moment of hearing the bell, If you can suddenly leap up— This is called the Great Matter.
If you do not understand, You will surely fall into the pit of birth and death. Do you understand? If you do not understand, I strike you once more! Thus he struck again.
A single strike rings out with crystalline clarity, Resounding through the vast expanse of the universe. The one who understands merely tilts their ear;
Xiang Yu has crossed over to the east of the River.

"Which one is the sutra? After a long silence, he said, "The subsequent text is lengthy; it shall be entrusted to a future day. Then he gave a shout and descended from his seat.
Entering the hall, he held up his staff and said, "The Buddhas of the past, the Buddhas of the present, and the Buddhas of the future... [West]...
The twenty-eight patriarchs of India, the six patriarchs of the Tang land, and all the elder monks under heaven—these have all been transformed into Nan-yuan’s staff.
Where, you people, will you find a place to settle your body and establish your life? Look!
This staff has already pierced through the skulls of you all. Is there anyone here who recognizes its pain and itch? If there is, come forth.

He looked around the assembly with a mischievous glance. "If there were none, Nan-yuan would have lost face today. He let out a shout, struck his staff once on the ground, and descended from the seat.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The true nature of ignorance is itself Buddha-nature; the illusory, empty body is itself the Dharma-body.

O worthy ones, if you can believe this, it will not fail to save you effort. This may be called Sudhana entering Maitreya’s pavilion, where all boundless Dharma-gates are fully encompassed, attaining great non-obstruction, and is termed the 'Patience of the Non-arising of Dharmas' (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti). Therefore it is said: Boundless..."
The realms of all lands are not separated from one another by so much as a hair’s tip; the ten ages of past and present, from beginning to end, do not depart from this very moment of thought.
Now I ask you all: which of these is your "present moment of thought"? Do you wish to understand?

It is simply the nature of your current ignorance that is itself the nature of fundamental enlightenment and wondrous clarity. Because you fail to realize the root source of birth and death, you cling to the delusory as...

Indeed, by following along with delusions, one falls into saṃsāra and undergoes all manner of suffering. If one can turn the light back to reflect upon oneself and realize for oneself that the original true nature is neither born nor extinguished, it is said: "The actual nature of ignorance is itself Buddha-nature;
the illusory, empty body is itself the Dharma-body. Just as this impure body composed of the four elements and five aggregates has no substantial reality whatsoever, so it is.
Dreams are like illusions, like shadows, and like echoes. Since immeasurable kalpas past, we have wandered through birth and death, driven by craving and attachment without a moment’s rest.
Emerging from here and entering there, the bones we have accumulated would equal Mount Vipula, and the milk of our mothers we have drunk would equal the waters of the four great oceans.
Why is this? It is because we lack wisdom and are unable to realize that the five aggregates are fundamentally empty and entirely devoid of reality.
Meaning: Following after sense objects, one gives rise to craving and becomes ensnared by the net of desire, losing all autonomy.
Therefore, the World-Honored One taught that the cause of all suffering is rooted in greed; if greed is extinguished, there is nothing upon which to rely.

If you can understand that this illusory body is false and fundamentally empty and quiescent, then various views will not arise, and views such as self, person, or sentient being will cease to exist. All...

All phenomena are thusness; therefore it is said that the illusory, empty body is itself the Dharma-body (*dharmakāya*). The Dharma-body is fully awakened and realizes there is not a single thing; there is only hearing the Dharma and preaching the Dharma.
This is the profound and mysterious Great Way, the unattached True Doctrine. Therefore it is said: "The fundamental source and original nature are the natural, true Buddha.

The five aggregates (*pañca-skandha*) are like floating clouds, coming and going in emptiness; the three poisons are like bubbles on water, vainly appearing and disappearing. If one is thus, [one is a Buddha].
This is called crossing over all suffering and calamity. Even unto the immeasurable and boundless afflictions, their knowledge and understanding are entirely purified;

this is termed the Pure Dharma-body (*viśuddha-dharmakāya*). If one reaches this state, whether emerging from here or entering there, casting off this body or receiving another, whether in hell or heaven, or within this world and its lands—there is freedom to move vertically and horizontally, floating or sinking at will, responding to things as they arise.

which one is the original dharma? After a long silence, he said: "Wherever there is a path to ascend, even those higher than others will walk it.
He gave a shout, struck the ground with his staff, and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Dharma-body is formless; it manifests forms in response to things. Holding up his staff, he said:

"This is Dao-wu’s staff. Which one is the Dharma-body? Let us set aside this entanglement for a moment. It has already entered through the nostrils of all of you in the Sangha hall and the Buddha hall.
The waters of the four great oceans are upon your heads, and the Dragon King is there."
"Do you feel it upon your fingernails? If you do feel it, you will travel three thousand miles by day and eight hundred by night;
smoke will rise from beneath your feet and fire will blaze from your head. If you do not feel it, then when hunger comes you eat, and when weariness comes you sleep. He let out a shout.
He descended from his seat. Entering the hall, he said: "All Buddhas distinguish themselves by means of the unconditioned dharma (*asaṃskṛta-dharma*).

That which is in front is Mount An; that which is behind is Mount Zhu. Which one is the unconditioned dharma? After a long silence, he said: "The text below is extensive; it is entrusted to those who come."
[The Master] says, "Day! He lets out a shout and descends from his seat. A monk asks, "I do not ask about the Buddha’s command or the Patriarch’s command;
what is the True Command? The Master says, "A golden phoenix plunges off a cliff. The monk shouts. The Master also shouts.
He strikes his staff once, and the monk spits behind him. Then he addresses the assembly: The Master says, "I take pity on you because you are the host of this dharma assembly."

Ascending the hall, he said: "The sky has already brightened; the drum has already sounded; the holy assembly has arrived; all join their palms together. Is there anyone here now who does not join their palms?
If there is, Nirgrantha will rejoice; if there is none, Gautama will be displeased. Having stood for a long time, take care."
A monk asked, "You have polished a three-foot sword to transform those who are unjust; what is your intention, Master?
The Master said, "Go well. The monk said, "Understood. The Master said, "Watch! The monk clapped his hands once and returned to the assembly.
The Master said, "Finished."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Samādhi of the World-Honored One, Ānanda did not know. The Samādhi of Ānanda, Śāṇakavāsin did not know.
The Samādhis of all the sages from antiquity do not know one another. He then took up his staff, drew a circle in the air, and asked, "What is this?
Is there anyone who can say? After a long silence, he said, "When meeting a swordsman on the road, you must..."
Presenting his sword: "If you are not a poet, do not offer a poem. With a shout, he descends from his seat. Ascending the hall, he says:
"The path to Nirvana has no divergent ways; the skillful means have many gates. He picks up his staff and says: "This here is Dao-wu’s staff;
which one is the gate of Nirvana? After a long silence, he says: "When you see the moon, cease looking at the finger; return home."
He ceased questioning Cheng, gave a shout, and descended from his seat.
Entering the hall, he said: "Now, those who preach the Dharma must respond to the proper time and season; if they do not respond to the time, it is all untimely speech."

There is still someone who ought to attain it. If you "ought," then you have already attained it. But tell me, where does it land? (He lets out a shout and descends from the seat. Ascending the hall, he said:
"When Daowu beats the drum, those in the four great continents are fellow practitioners. When the staff is held horizontally, it sweeps across the heavens."
The earth is the great ground. The alms bowl turns over, overturning worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. I ask you all:
where do you establish yourselves and sustain your lives? If you know the direction, you will eat porridge and rice in the continent of Uttarakuru.
If you do not know, then speak of Daowu’s transgression. Take care.
Ascending the hall, a monk came forward to prostrate. As he rose, he gave a shout. The Master said, "What is this? The monk shouted again.
The Master said, "Blind! The monk prostrated. The Master said, "Thirty blows! Wait until another time, and I will give them to you.
A monk asked, "Regarding the ancients facing the wall—what was their intent? The Master said, "He had years but no virtue."
Ascending the hall, he said: "North Mountain is south; South Mountain is north. Sun and moon shine together, yet heaven and earth are dark.
The great ocean and all rivers emit light. When encountering Avalokiteśvara, one asks about Maitreya. Take care."

The Master was residing at Shishuang. On the day he ascended the hall, a monk asked: "Vimalakīrti’s single silence and Linji’s praise of the teacher's tradition—when the staff and the shout are applied together, those in the middle current are at a loss.
For this assembly today, we pray that the Master will provide a skillful means. The Master said: "At Shidi, spring arrives and grows long;
the frost-flower asks toward the sun. The monk stepped forward and said: "If it is thus, then the sun-bird warbles its speech, and after the rain falls, the hundred [flowers]..."
Huaxin said: "If it were not for the fisherman’s guidance, how would one know the depth of the water? The monk said: "In steep waters, the current flows swiftly;
when the clouds part, they reveal the azure sky. The Master said: "I am walking through the wild weeds, and you have entered deep into the village.
The monk responded with an "Amen" (Ām) and said: "Your Excellency does not spare me a needle; let me ask one more question. What is the meaning of your intent? The Master [remained silent].
[The Master] said, "I grant you thirty blows; it will not be until thirty years hence that you will finally know what pain and itching are.
The monk twirled his sleeves and withdrew. The Master said, "A dream. [The monk] asked, "What is it like when a square piece of wood is tuned as a string?
The Master said, "A banner pole, one foot two inches. [The monk] pressed further, "In that case, does the Master's hand produce the present age? The Master said, "A kick with the foot."
Fobong said, "Do not say you do not recognize the sound. The Master said, "In thirty years, it is uncertain whether you will realize it.
A monk asked, "What is it like when there is reason that cannot be fully expressed? The Master said, "Bitter.
The monk pressed further, "If so, then the tongue is pressed against the upper palate. The Master then sighed repeatedly. The monk said, "I thought the beard was red. The Master [remained silent].
[The Master] said: "I dreamed of Nanyuan’s heels. A question was asked: "What is it like when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished?
The Master said: "Silla beats the drum. He further asked: "What is it like after it has been polished? The Master said: "India performs a dance."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The blue lotus blinks its eyes with excessive frequency; Kāśyapa’s faint smile is but self-deception. Sitting at Shaoshi, he clung to folly and had his arm cut off;
at Huangmei, he presented various kinds of verses as his understanding. Through the eight gates of staff and shout, layer upon layer of error occurs;

regarding the supreme vehicle of the ancestral lineage, one carves out one's own flesh. When you examine what is already established, who would feel shame? Kaian’s 'Aha! and the 'cracking' and 'pecking' are laughed at by bystanders. (1)
Sujue came to realize it was a mistake; he did not say that his teacher was without reason. Every man possesses the ambition to pierce the heavens;
they look back at the North Star from the face of the Southern Dipper.
Verse: In Response to the Sangha’s Request for Clarification on the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials, Verse One:
The First Mystery How could the Buddhas of the three periods of time proclaim it?
Bestowing compassion while dreaming is to become frivolous; Sitting upright still results in falling into the extreme of nihilism.
The Second Mystery: The keen eye of the *sramana* is not yet clear;
even knowing the spark of flint or the flash of lightning is dull. Raising an eyebrow or blinking an eye, one traverses the mountain passes.
The Third Mystery: The myriad phenomena are dense and vast, the universe is wide and open.
Clouds disperse into the empty caverns, the mountains and peaks are still; Falling blossoms fill the flowing waters of the long river.
This is the primary requirement. How could one speak of the wondrousness of the holy and the ordinary? To deliberate is to travel a long road;
to lift the eyes is to fall into seven perversions.
The Second Essential: Striking the Peak Summit with a Summoning Call; Supernatural powers come freely as one arrives, calling at the gate of the Gate of Much Learning.
The Third Essential: Arising and falling cause people to laugh; Within the palm, one grasps the universe.

A thousand differences are all illumined at once to inform you, O Master of the Profound Mystery; The staff and the shout must be applied according to the occasion. If you clearly understand the essential meaning, the sun will shine even in the middle of the night.
At the request of the assembly, Linji’s two hall heads both let out a shout; this verse praises the mechanism of "the peck and the hatch.
The arrow meets the blade in a flash, and guest and host are distinguished at that moment.
The Master, pitying all beings, bestows [this teaching] upon both the ordained and the laity; In the north, the Yellow River runs turbid to its very depths.
In response to a request for further instruction regarding the story of Huichao, Master [Linji] spoke in verse:
A monk asked, "What is Buddha? The Master said, "You are Huichao.
Huichao prostrated himself, then stepped forward with palms joined. To deliberate upon this is ten thousand miles of distance.
Because the assembly requested instruction on Yunmen’s discourse on "transcending Buddhas and patriarchs," [the Master] declared:
"How does one transcend Buddhas and patriarchs? When Xuan-chong served rice cakes at the vegetarian feast, he ate them to his heart's content;
when the monk from Hunan spread out his bowl, the man from Silla bit into it; the Persian merchant at the great rock asked for a ferryboat."
In response to the monks' request for further instruction, he composed three verses on the Three Secrets.
The First Secret: The great earth, mountains, and rivers leak forth; Vimalakīrti remained silent, while Mañjuśrī spoke at length.
The Second Secret: When you unfold and examine the timing, how could speech and silence interfere with one another?
It is like the autumn moon at midnight.
The Third Secret: The distant road is difficult to traverse; it is like rowing a boat upon dry land.
The first line of the three-line verse, "The sun and moon are hidden within the eyes":
even those in the heavens or other directions are utterly at a loss.
The various inverted arguments of Kūla are manifold; the towering [peak] has not yet reached the Nyagrodha tree.
In the second line: Linji and Deshan traverse the road;
before even reaching Silla, they brandish their staffs. The one who attains realization points wildly along the way.
Third Verse: Vimalakīrti manifests illness; Mañjuśrī engages in profound dialogue.
A single silence shakes heaven and earth. Even until this very day, it serves as a source of laughter.
At the request of the monks, there are verses on the Five Ranks.
The partial within the absolute center: at midnight, the black hen crows within the chamber;
the world is like a lamp-light shining from the bottom of the sea, and flowers grow upon stones with long branches and spirit.
The absolute center within the partial: as the sun sets behind the western mountains, one beholds strange shadows.
The distinct images reveal the vehicle of the school; do not mistake the head for the moon in the well.
Coming from the very center, the wooden horse gives birth to a child that fills the nine realms.
Advancing and retreating, one follows the bird-path at will; how could this compare to dwelling in a nest within the confines of the mundane world?
Simultaneous Arrival: Each of those great officers fully maintains their spirit;
the crossbows interlock without their points meeting. Expanding and contracting, moving vertically and horizontally, they remain inseparable.
Simultaneous Reaching: Before black and white have appeared, cease all fabrication.
One must clearly understand that the pillar has not yet given birth to a child; do not mistake wild words for the path and wander astray.
This entire verse returns from the partial to the correct, reaching the utmost mystery: when the correct and mysterious emerge from the partial, principle and phenomena are complete.
One must know that true establishment is beyond verbal expression; Faint signs belong to the realm of conditions.
When both past and future exert wondrous functions, What further need is there to pursue verbal explanations?
Arising and ceasing cannot encompass the entire world; Vast and unattached, the Bird Path is profound.

Because the Sangha requested instruction on the "Buddha's Talk on the Wind Caves," [I spoke of] the "Bamboo Sinew Whip" beneath Mount Zhaglin. There are myriads upon myriads of Chan practitioners from the north and south;
do not be surprised that we meet and I do not dismount from my horse—each of you has your own path ahead in the east and west.
To Li, the Prince of the Imperial Household:
Dividing yourself into thousands, tens of thousands, and hundreds of millions, Your compassion, wisdom, and vows are inexhaustible. Amidst the secular world you follow the ways of the world;
Dwelling in the palace, you accord with the life of the palace. In every step, you provide great protection; In every place, you manifest spiritual powers.
Precious indeed is our school’s fortune, Many are able to establish the ancient style. Furthermore,
gazing upward at the single orb of the sun upon the horizon, How many times has its pure radiance risen from the four quarters?
The Great Being with Disheveled Hair asks Master Zhigong: A Commentary on the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā* by Upādhyāya Du Shun’s Verses:
“A buffalo in Huai Prefecture eats the grain” (the world-systems as numerous as the sands of the Ganges); “A horse in Yi Prefecture has a bloated belly” (ants carry off a bowl).
The world summons physicians who have donkey heads and horse horns; they cauterize the left shoulder of a pig (like painting a tiger and ending up with a wildcat).
The cowherd and the oxherd are truly happy; barefoot and clad in rain-cloaks, their hair is gathered in twin tufts.
Lying across upon the ox, facing the sky, he sings a song. When people ask what he is doing, he turns his face to look back:
The level fields are vast; he lets the ox roam in all four directions, Ceasing to restrain it within a pen.
With no constraints from any of the eight directions, it wanders at will. If you wish to bring it back, simply pinch its nose.
Little calf, comb the hair with the grain; Your strength is not yet sufficient to lift you up.
For now, let us leave you on this small slope; Fearing that upon the solitary peak your four hooves might slip.
The sun is already high; do not graze. Pick up the end of the rope—there is neither young nor old.
All at once they are led into the pen to sleep; Mixing with the mud, watch them fall east and west—A-he-he!
Excellent, yet excellent! Leisurely blowing the short flute with the wind, It shakes the five lakes, mountains, peaks, and islands. Riding the ox backward, he takes off his tattered robe.
Those who know the sound need not seek it on the road; If you ask where the cowherd dwells, he points east and west with his whip—there is not a single treasure.
In winter, there are no human affairs.

The forest trees on the eastern mountains are tall; how many years have they stood, and how many times has it rained? On the southern ridge, the pine branches are slender; stones grow from the soil at their sides.

Seeing the golden-hued Gautama, [the Master] composed a verse based on the ancient song of the twelve periods of the day, requested by the monks for further instruction. It reads: The eastern mountain’s forest trees are tall; How many years, how many cycles of rain? On the southern ridge, pine branches are lean; Stones grow from the earth beside the rocks.
Seeing the Golden One, Gautama, He versified the ancient song of the twelve periods of the day, as requested by the monks.
At the hour of Chou (1–3 a.m.), when the cock crows, one encounters people in dreams amidst a vast and chaotic blur.
At the hour of Yin (3–5 a.m.), at the break of dawn, one awakens and plays with the spirit upon the road.
At the hour of Mao (5–7 a.m.), as the sun rises, one sits within the shadow of magnificent radiance.
The hour of eating: when one is full, one knows it to be the cause of illness.
The hours of Wuyong and Si: buying and selling, weighing and measuring, entering the marketplace.
Midday, the sun at its zenith: the myriad phenomena clearly become objects of laughter.
Before the sun has turned its shadow west, Zhang drinks his wine while Li is already drunk;
at the hour of Bu (15–17) and Shen (17–19), he reflects and sits upright, yet remains in a state of intoxication;
when the sun sets at You (19–21), he props up his thatched hut and bamboo door with stubborn persistence.
At the hour of Xu (7–9 p.m.), twilight falls; as the sun sets behind the western mountains, foxes and demons emerge.
At the hour of Hai (9–11 p.m.), the rat forms its ranks at the head of the bed.
At the hour of Zi (11 p.m.–1 a.m.), the full moon shines—Sūkhali!
When Chan Master Huijue of Mount Langya in Chuzhou first ascended the hall, after he had finished offering incense, a monk asked:
"Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does the lineage follow? The Master said: "I leave it entirely to you to probe the tortoise shell and strike the tiles.
The monk pressed further: "If that is so, then Fengyang’s single arrow has shot straight through to Langya. The Master said: "Finished."
Question: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "The remaining candle before the courtyard has faded.
Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "The yellow-faced bhikṣu. The questioner followed up: "Is it not this very one? The Master said:
"Wisdom has no weight in grains."
Chan Master Xiaoyu of Longhua Monastery in Huangmei, Qizhou, was traveling on pilgrimage to consult with the Fifth Patriarch.
Chan Master Jie asked him, "How do you speak that single phrase which does not fall within the range of lips and tongue?
The Master said, "Old and decrepit as I am, I have not even looked after my own meditation topic. Jie gave a shout. The Master also shouted. Jie raised his staff; the Master then—
As he clapped his hands, the Preceptor called out, "Acarya, wait! The teaching remains.
The Master placed his sitting cloth upon his shoulder and departed without looking back.
When Chan Master Zhìyuán of Lóngtán in Tángzhōu first opened the hall for his inaugural sermon, a monk asked: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does he succeed?
The Master said: "The waters at Fényáng are swift; white waves surge to the heavens. The monk pressed further:
"Does this allow a student to set foot [upon the path]? The Master said: "Roll! A monk asked: "I have heard it said in the teachings: 'This is true diligence.'"
"This is called the true offering of Dharma. "How is this the true Dharma? The Master said: "Gathering at night and dispersing at dawn. Question: "What is the Dragon Pond sword?
The Master said: "It cannot be touched. He further asked: "What about one who is exhausted? The Master said:
"White bones stretching across the mountains. Question: "I have long heard of the Dragon Pond; why is it that when I arrive, the dragon does not appear?"
The Master said, "The water is deep; its bottom cannot be seen. [The student] asked, "What is it like before and after?
The Master said, "A groundless cause for sorrow. Chan Master Guangpu of Yongqing Monastery in Guozhou was originally in the assembly of Chan Master Cizhao Cong at Shimen. Early on...
[Chan Master] Can (Shanshan) entered. The Master asked, "I have heard an ancient saying: 'In the Hall of Great Compassion there is a meal. What is the meaning of this?
Shimen said, "When the sun rises, he sits in the shade; when the weather is cold, he does not raise his head. He then descended from the seat.

Later, the Master followed him into the inner quarters. Shimen asked, "How do you understand the causal conditions just now? The Master said, "To understand them is to consume them on the journey. "No," [Shimen replied].
This was immediately circulated as a conventional truth. Shimen said, "Not yet; say more. The Master shook his sleeves and departed.
On the day the Master opened the hall, a monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master replied, "The land of Shu produces bing-iron."
A monk asked Chan Master Huiling of Shouning Monastery in Guizhou, "When both light and objects have vanished, where does the Way return?
The Master said, "At the head of the street, at the tail of the market. The monk pressed further, "What about the matter right now?
The Master said, "Dragging through mud and carrying water. A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "A little, not much."
The student said, "A guest arrives from the East; with what will you receive him? The Master said, "On the long benches, venison soup and plain rice.
Chan Master Liaotong, the sixth patriarch of Shimen Mountain in Xiangzhou, said: "Just now, before the bell in the hall had even rung—"
When it is time for the bell to ring, the senior monks (upādhyāyas) should naturally know the proper moment. Why must you come forward, clenching your fists against your chests?
It is truly a matter of excessive solemnity. O worthy ones, even so, it is as if one were scattering sand into the eyes of the senior monks.
The Buddhas of the three periods of time turn the Great Dharma Wheel upon the bridge of your noses. Look, look! After a long silence, he said: "Winter practicing Spring."
"Take care. A monk asked, "What is the phoenix mechanism? The Master said, "I have shown it clearly to you, *ācārya*.
The monk further asked, "If one suddenly encounters a traveler seeking to join with it, what then? The Master said, "For now, receive my words.
Another monk asked, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? The Master then took up a pure pitcher and made the gesture of pouring out water.
The student said, "I do not yet understand the meaning of this. The Master said, "The arrow has already passed beyond Silla.
A questioner asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Walking alone, departing from India."
On the day Chan Master Faxian of Zhuyuan Mountain in Jingnan Prefecture ascended the hall, a monk asked: "Master, having ascended the precious seat, what Dharma will you preach?
The Master said: "Where the incense smoke rises, the assembly gathers like clouds. The student said: "In that case, within the midst of the red flames, no trace is to be seen.
The Master said: "Heaven and earth leave no path for penetration. The monk asked: "What is [the Way]?"
The Master said, "A skilled hand cannot paint it. Question: "What is the Way? The Master said, "Intersecting at a crossroads.
Question: "What is one who is on the Way? The Master said, "Often they do not recognize one another."
Question: "What is this extraordinary matter? The Master drew a line with his staff. The monk then shouted.
The Master struck the meditation bench once. The monk prostrated. The Master then struck him. Question: "I have heard it said in the teachings:
'Stop, stop! There is no need to speak; my Dharma is subtle and inconceivable. What is meant by 'stop, stop! There is no need to speak'?"
The Master said, "Too much. The student asked, "How is it that my Dharma is wondrous and inconceivable?
The Master said, "It would be better for you to quickly prostrate three times."
Chan Master Yanzhao of Yongfu Monastery in Pengzhou ascended the hall. A monk asked, "The Master has mounted the precious throne; the Imperial Envoy has arrived.
We pray that you will proclaim the ultimate pivot of the teaching. The Master said, "The lunar disc grinds through the crystal shell;
the Dragon Kings within the seas smile and nod their heads. The monk pressed further, "If it is so, then delusion and awakening do not depend upon a teacher. The Master—
The Master said: "Rarely do we encounter those who pierce their ears; frequently do we meet those who wait by the stump. A questioner asked: "What is the realm of Pengzhou? The Master said:
"Men and horses are jumbled together. The questioner pressed: "What is it like to be within that realm? The Master then gave a shout.
The monk made a gesture with his hands as if drawing a bow. The Master then raised his staff; as the monk hesitated, the Master struck him.
A monk asked, "An ancient worthy said: 'All over the body sweat flows in a mountain-demon's cave; the *kāṣāya* covers the face in a village of ghosts and spirits. What is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "From the great face of Qingcheng, a worthy man emerges. As the monk hesitated, the Master [struck him].
"Ho! On the day Chan Master Dezun of Dacheng Mountain in Tangzhou first opened the hall for formal teaching, a monk asked:

"When a Buddha appeared in the West, the earth was spread with yellow gold. Today you have appeared in the world—what auspicious signs are there? The Master said: "The Real One within a tattered rag."
Zhuzhen said, "If it is so, then the Perfect Fusion (yuanrong) below has its light penetrating through the Sahā world. The Master said, "A donkey's mouth in a blue cloth bag.
He asked, "Please, Master, speak a phrase regarding the perfect fusion of the world. The Master said, "A perfect sphere, more than seven feet in circumference.
He asked, "What is the Great Vehicle Mountain? The Master said, "The stream water flows toward the east. Zhuzhen continued.
[The monk] asked, "What is it like to be a person among the mountains? The Master said, "Brows like deer, eyes as white.
[The monk] asked, "What is the matter regarding Linji’s one shout? The Master said, "I, this mountain monk, cannot say it. The monk then shouted. The Master said, "A fine shout!
The monk shouted again. The Master said, "I do not yet believe you. The monk said, "Blind! The Master [said], "Blind!"
[The Master] raised his staff and struck [the monk].
The Master ascended the hall and said:
"The Ancient Buddhas transmitted the Mind-Seal; The Lamp of Prajñā is ever-burning. Such is the profound and wondrous intent of Caoxi."
Master Mazu’s Legacy: Treading upon the moon in the waves, how many among them can transcend the lofty style of our school?
Coming and going with spontaneous ease, a monk once asked:
"I have heard your words, Master; what is the lofty style beyond our school? The Master said: "A laugh."
Pointing with his finger toward the setting sun casting shadows into the dark room, he said: "Treading upon Vairocana, the oceans and mountains collapse. The student asked:
"What is it like to come and go in a state of natural ease? The Master said: "A hunting dog bites a bone and licks its own muzzle in vain; its belly hangs empty while its back is covered in dust."
When Master Jusu first ascended the seat at Jingqing Chan Monastery in Huzhou, the Rector struck the gavel and said:

"In this Dharma assembly, you dragon-like and elephant-like multitudes should contemplate the primary principle. The Master said: "To clearly understand within the primary principle is still like covering one's ears while stealing a bell.
To succeed in the station of immovability is inevitably subject to the criticisms and denigrations of others. Even if one were to manifest a transcendence that surpasses the elephants..."

Externally, you remain silent and withdraw from the sharp points of verbal debate; yet internally, you have not forgotten the sentiments of grasping and rejecting—how could such a state possibly overcome the affliction of existence and non-existence?

A view such as this is enough to make others laugh to death. Nevertheless, though it be so, the official does not begrudge a needle, nor does he refuse to let carriages and horses pass through his gate.

If you have doubts, please ask. A monk asked: "The patriarchs transmit to one another the seal of the patriarchs; to whom did the Master transmit the Dharma? The Master said: "He who can ride a white ox through the blue heavens."
The Master said: "By the side of the Pool of Carved Teeth, I once stayed in victory; at the edge of Dao’an’s Cliff, I walked freely along the path. Jin said:
"If that is so, then the flowers of Tiger Creek bloom again from days of old, and the moon over Lake Xia is freshly renewed this very day.
The Master said: "A thousand bamboos stand aged and green; a single path through pine and ivy grows deep. A question was asked: "What is the pure realm? The Master said: "Rain."
A person crossing the bridge over the stream hesitated to pass. The Master said, "How is it with one within the realm?
The monk said, "The light of the moon-cold toad—how can it be beheld? Another asked, "From afar I have come to seek refuge with you, Master;

I beg you for a reception. The Master said, "A man from Silla beats the drum. The student asked, "How should I understand this? The Master said, "I have never met the captain of the ship. The monk [departed].
Question: I have heard the Master say, "The Son of Heaven issues his edicts within the realm; the General issues his orders beyond the frontier.
What is the General’s order beyond the frontier? Master: [He] lifts [his robe]. Disciple: What is the matter therein?
Master: [He] kicks [him]. Disciple: Is this not the very point where the Master benefits others? Master: Snaps his fingers once.
Question: "What is the final phrase? The Master said: "Beneath the Diamond Tree. The student asked:
"What is the ultimate phrase? The Master said: "Beside the City of Kuśinagara. The student asked:
"Is there anything further beyond this? The Master said: "There is. The student asked: "What is that which is further beyond? The Master said: [Silence].
Pabao clapped his hands and laughed "he-he. Kāśyapa raised his head, not recognizing the man.
(The following phrases were recorded separately by Li Zunxu, the Prince Consort and Regional Commander of Zhenguojun.
Master Huìyuè of Cùfēng Chan Monastery on Mount Dōngtíng in Sūzhōu ascended the seat and said: "If one discusses the Patriarchs..."
The Mind-Seal—how could it be contained within the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*)? Not only the ultimate truth, but even the three essentials cannot encompass it;
how then could the four propositions (*catuṣkoṭi*) include it? Even if one were to claim that it is realized prior to words, one would still be halfway there.

The Master said, "On what day shall there be a time of rest? Question: "What is it to not abandon a single dharma within the gate of Buddha-activity?
The Master said, "Letting go of one and seizing another. Question: "What is it like when the path of words is cut off? The Master said: [Silence].
“This is not yet the ultimate point. The student asked, “What is the ultimate point? The Master said, “After winter, the first yang arises.

One morning, the Master ascended the hall for the formal lecture and said, “I have a phrase to hand over directly to you face-to-face. If you do not understand it, the four heavens [will bear witness].”
[The Master] was in the eastern lands. After a long silence, he said: "If one can directly take responsibility in this very way with little effort, one is already a person who has missed the point.
[I have] stood for a long time. A monk asked: "What is it like when one sits firmly atop the crown of Vairocana and does not receive instruction from Śākyamuni?
The Master said: "This old monk takes a leap of three thousand li; you are right there within the nostrils and the eyelashes."
"What do you say to this? The student said, "How can you, Master, act so arbitrarily? The Master said, "Give me back the head of the phrase.
The monk was speechless. The Master struck him. A monk asked, "What is the primary meaning? The Master said, "Which meaning is that which asks?
The student said, "I have come specifically to request instruction. The Master said, "I take it for granted that you are from the West..."
Tianlai asked, "In the teachings it is said: 'Stop, stop! There is no need to speak; my Dharma is subtle and difficult to conceive. What is this matter that is difficult to conceive?
The Master said, "If it were not you, Master, asking, even I would not know. The student asked, "How can one receive and uphold it?
The Master said, "In the morning, observe the beauty of the clouds and mists; in the evening, listen to the coolness of the mountain stream."
Question: "What is the matter beneath the patched robe? The Master said: "A thousand mountains where the drifting clouds have vanished.
Question: "What is the path that leads upward? The Master said: "Sometimes advancing, sometimes retreating.

The Master said: "His mouth hangs on the eastern wall.

Accumulations are naturally perfected; why must one falsely seek among the various realms day and night? If I were to say to you practitioners of Chan right now that there is nothing to do, you would already be lost in oblivion;
how much more so with many paths, which only serve to increase your afflictions. This is the case within the school of the patched-robed monks.
"How do you bring them together? Is there anyone who understands? Come forth and speak before the assembly! At that time, a monk came forward and bowed.

The direct son of Yunmen; the true great-grandson of Xueling. The Master said: "Even if you were to memorize it by force, Zhu would certainly not be your own kin.
The student said: "What of the great assembly? The Master said: "You see only the sharpness of the chisel's tip;
how can you know the squareness of the chisel's head? Question: "What is the newly opened realm? The Master said: "Look within Lake Dongting."
Jinge asked, "What is it like to be a person within the realm? The Master said, "Holding hands by the walls of Yueyang City.
He asked, "How is it when a Buddha appears in the world? The Master said, "Joining palms while reciting the name of Avalokiteśvara.

Question: "How was it before Oxhead had seen the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said: "He wore a hat that reached toward heaven and donned a robe with four sleeves.
The questioner asked: "How was it after he saw him? The Master said: "In hand he held a dragon-tusk staff, striking out the mechanism of the extraordinary man.
Question: "I do not ask about the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings; what is the meaning of the Master’s One [Vehicle]?"
The Master drew a line in front of him with his staff. As the student hesitated, the Master said, "Give me back a phrase.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Mount Nanyue.

"The bridge has been broken into two sections. What do you say to this? The monk was speechless. The Master said, "Go and join the assembly.

A monk remained silent. The Master struck him and said, "Do you know where you have fallen?

The Master remained silent and then struck him. He asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from?

"Go to the hall.

The Master said, "The mountains are green and the waters are clear. The monk asked, "What is the non-duality of form and mind? The Master said, "The words you have spoken are profound."
Biandao asked, "What is the very first phrase? The Master said, "Lifted up, it is clear.

The monk asked, "Is this not the very phrase used for receiving people? The Master said, "Later generations will find it difficult to encounter.
