The Master said, "The Yellow River clears itself only once every three thousand years."
A monk asked Chan Master Hai of Nantianwang in Luzhou, “What is the ‘hair-blistering sword’? The Master said, “The walls crumble and the ice melts.
The monk pressed further, “And what of one who uses it? The Master said, “Drag it out! A monk asked, “What is the True Suchness of the One Body?
The Master said, “The iron ball in Wulang’s hand. A monk asked, “What is the West? The Master said, “The Eastern Peak.”
Regarding the intent of the question: The Master said, "It startles heaven and shakes the earth. The questioner asked, "When one speaks ten times and rests nine times, what is it like?
The Master said, "Thorns grow upon the lips. The questioner pressed further, "How can one avoid this fault?
The Master said, "It is best to withdraw halfway."
A monk asked Chan Master Weian of Beitian in Luzhou, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "It needlessly makes people sorrowful. The monk pressed further, "Why is it so? The Master struck him. [The monk] asked again.
"What is it that is secretly transmitted from east to west? The Master said, "People of past and present have been at a loss. Question:
"What was the subject of the dialogue between Mañjuśrī and Vimalakīrti? The Master said, "Listen. The student said, "I do not yet understand;
how can one attain intimacy? The Master said, "An echo. Question: "What is the Great Canon of Teachings? The Master said, "The high seat."
[The monk] asked, "Before ascending [the hall], how was it? The Master said, "After ascending, how was it? The Master said, "The three sections are not the same.
A monk asked Zen Master Huangbo of Mount Huangbo in Junzhou, "What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "I serve as a model for all people under heaven. He asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Thick eyebrows and large eyes."
Question: What is the primordial body? The Master said: Lying upon thorns, not dependent on others.
Question: What is the first phrase? The Master said: Smash through Damsanguan; turn back on foot with bare feet.
Chan Master Juehua Puzhao of Guizhou ascended the hall and addressed the assembly, saying: "A single word cuts it off; heaven and earth are fully dissected.
A hundred thousand wondrous gates converge simultaneously. All you Chan practitioners, you need not use thought to know, nor deliberation to understand.
If you attempt to take another step forward, you will further lose all connection. Nevertheless, though it is thus, the wind does not come, and the tree—"
"Unmoving. Is there anyone among this assembly who has long been a veteran practitioner? Let us deliberate on this before the assembly.
At that time, a monk asked, "The Tathāgata expounds the Dharma with a single voice; I wonder, Master, what Dharma do you show to people?
The Master said, "White clouds have no fixed abode; they appear and vanish within the great void. The monk pressed further, "If that is so, then [you are in] the Hall of Good Dharma."
[This was] the previous lion’s roar. The Master said, "Step back; you are obstructing others from asking.

A questioner asked, "For several days we have not heard the lion’s roar. What is the nature of its majestic and powerful sound? The Master said, "The dragon sings in the deep caverns and heaven and earth are still;

the tiger roars before the crags and auspicious clouds arise. A questioner asked, "People already understand your ordinary means (*pingchang ji*). What about the words that transcend [the ordinary]? (*shangxiang yan*)...
Fengyi asked, "How is it? The Master said, "Look directly. The student asked, "What is it? The Master struck him.
The Master then said, "What end will there ever be to this questioning and answering? If you take mere words and sounds as your own self, you will never find it."
What business is there here? Even if one were to pose hundreds or thousands of difficult questions, it would only serve to exhaust oneself further.

Within the gate of the patch-robed monks, if there is a single word of accord, then all the myriad distinctions and thousandfold differences are rendered superfluous; they are merely self-made. As for the matter that has come down from of old—how should one approach it?
If you can realize it right here, you have already reached the point of "two heads and three tops. To attempt further paths is to move further away from the Way.
[The Master] said, "Far away! In these present days of peace and tranquility, the royal law is somewhat strict. I have stood for a long time; take care.

The Master ascended the hall and said, "The golden crow’s cry has not yet ceased; the jade hare again uncovers its brow. If you are a seeker of the Way, do not trouble yourself further by leaking the mechanism [of the mind].
I have stood for a long time; take care. A monk asked, "If one kills father and mother, one repents before the Buddha. What about killing..."
“Buddha killed his patriarch. Where does one repent? The Master said: “The dawn light has not yet parted, yet all gaze;
when the sky breaks into day, it is as usual. Question: “I have heard an ancient saying: ‘From antiquity to now, nothing has fallen away; it is clearly before one’s eyes.
I do not know what thing this is. The Master said: “The scenery is vast and expansive, with a thousand points of difference; the sound of the river—”
"It is the same as the four seasons. The student asked, "Why can one not turn over within the great trichiliocosm?
The Master said, "Who is obstructing you, O *jialuo*? The student pressed, "What can be done about the fact that one cannot turn over? The Master said, "It is of no use."
Question: How can one penetrate the two characters "sound" and "form"? The Master said: "Empty space undergoes no change;
the sun and moon divide their own paths. Question: What is true suchness and nirvana? The Master said: "The sound of the autumn wind rustles."
The sound of the flowing water was a murmuring *chan-chan*. A questioner asked, "The entire world cannot speak of it; please, Master, speak of it.

The Master said, "It would silence the mouths of all people in the world. The questioner pressed further, "If that is so, then we thank you for your compassion. The Master said, "This mountain monk is at fault.
A questioner asked, "Before a single thought has arisen, how does one distinguish between this side and that side? The Master said, "Full."
The eyes are all crossroads; throughout one's life, there is no coming or going.

The Master ascended the hall and said: "If everyone were like today, the Old Barbarian (the Buddha) would have cause for hope; yet even Dīpaṃkara Buddha was not equal to you, O Ācārya. He further said:
"If it were as it is today, the Old Barbarian would be without hope; you, O Ācārya, would not be equal to Dīpaṃkara Buddha. Understand this clearly herein.
The Buddhas as numerous as the atoms of the great earth, the twenty-eight patriarchs of the Western Heaven, the six patriarchs of the Tang land, and the elder masters of the world—
all at once brought forth upon the tip of this mountain monk’s staff, they turn the wondrous Wheel of Dharma. If you cannot understand this,
hundreds of thousands of Buddhas will pierce your nostrils, and the twenty-eight patriarchs of the Western Heaven will pass through your skull.
"Do you understand? If you do not, I, the superior monk, shall point it out for you. After a long silence, he said: "What fault is there in the mountains, rivers, and the great earth?
He stood for a long time and said, "Take care. A monk asked: "You have resided at Shaoshi for a long time; why is it that the waters of Li are so fragrant?
The Master said: "A single moon over a thousand households; there is nowhere it does not shine. The monk bowed, and the Master then [departed].
[The Master] struck [the student]. He asked: "When Shaolin sat facing the wall, who was the man standing in the snow?
The Master said: "A single phrase before the blade transcends the Tamer of Men; what more could one find anywhere that is not sharp and new? He asked:

"In the teachings it is said, 'The fragrant wind blows away the withered flowers, and rain falls upon the fresh and beautiful. What is the meaning of this? The Master said: "Can you say it, O Ajari? [The student] stepped forward.
[The monk] said, "If that is so, then I thank the Master for his instruction. The Master said, "This mountain monk is at fault. A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "The pines are high and the ravines are deep; the road is long and the horse complains of the distance.
The Master asked a monk, "With your staff trailing clouds, from where did you depart this morning? The monk said, "I recently left Dongyuan. The Master said, "Come here."
At that time, he saw the ancient Śākyamuni again. The monk said, “I do not understand. The Master said, “Sit for a moment and drink some tea.
The Master asked a newly arrived monk, “Upon entering the gate, there is the lion’s roar; how do you respond with a single phrase at the point of encounter?
The monk said, “Painting on a diamond wall. The Master said, “That is merely following local custom. The monk said, “Master...”
“Why do you not grasp the meaning of this statement? The Master said, “When shooting a tiger, one does not encounter a man; one draws back a crossbow capable of launching a thousand-jin bolt.
Then he said, “Go to the hall. Chan Master Jue of Tiectang in Yizhou ascended the hall and said: “The True Dharma is wordless; why trouble oneself with names and forms? If one were to discuss it...”
"Mind itself is Buddha. This is very much like not knowing the proper time. To further say, "Neither mind nor Buddha," is exactly like cutting off one's head and seeking life thereby.
Venerable elders, you carry your bags and alms bowls, wandering north and south—what is your intention?
Do not see those old masters from all quarters sitting upon crooked wooden seats, opening their two flaps of skin and making a great clamor, and then you immediately say, "This is it."
Zen is the Way; it is true suchness and liberation. Do not misunderstand this!
Although I, this mountain monk, now speak to you in this way out of necessity, I am already burying you. Nevertheless, one must be a person of such caliber to truly attain it.
"What matters is this very moment; come forth and let us deliberate. At that time, a monk asked, "Since ancient times, the masters of old have transmitted mind through mind.
From whom did you, Master, receive the Dharma? The Master said: "As soon as the single sound is split open, boundless limits vanish;
the brilliant sun rises, casting its radiance across heaven and earth. The monk pressed further: "If that is so, then today I have received it directly."
The Master’s countenance departed. The Master said: "Flowers flourish toward the end of spring; birds cry out with their voices through the four seasons. Question:
"The Way transcends the discourse of existence and non-existence; the Dharma is free from talk of going and staying. How do you express the ancestral house style? The Master said:
"A single wheel stamps out the reflection in the cold pond; ten thousand phenomena simultaneously share the brilliance of the Patriarchal Way. Question: "How is it?"
"This is where the Upādhyāya came from. The Master said, "Heaven does not weary him; hell never tires him. Question:
"How does one practice throughout the twelve periods of the day? The Master said, "Shave the head clean; wash the bowl pure.
[The student] said, "If that is so, then I thank you for your instruction. The Master said, "You see only the sharpness of the tip of the awl."
The Master ascended the hall and said: "The true does not conceal the false; the crooked does not hide the straight. He further said:
"The Patriarchs and Ancestors left behind a single sandal, which has been causing a clamor until the present day. How, O monks, do you understand this?

If there is anyone who can understand this moment, it will be no small matter; they will not be deceived by others, but will pass their days according to conditions and spend their time as they please."

Do not trouble your mind with needless hardship or force yourself to stand out. Throughout the twelve periods of the day, whether putting on clothes or eating food, you will naturally be free from obstruction.

Question: "When one speaks of the ultimate reality (*dharmatā*) without destroying conventional designations (*prajñapti*), how is it? The Master said: "The green mountains do not move their feet; the sun and moon are free to roam. Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "Mixing mud and blending water. The student pressed further: "Ultimately, what is it? The Master said: "Seizing and grasping at raw thunder. Question: "Why is the delicious nectar of *amṛta* [called] *tīrtha*? The Master said: "Because it is the ultimate flavor. The student asked: "What is the ultimate flavor? The Master said: "It is like a person who has lost his way. The student asked: "What is it like for one who has lost his way? The Master said: "He does not know where he is going. The student asked: "How can he find his way back? The Master said: "He must rely on a good friend. The student asked: "What is a good friend? The Master said: "One who points out the path. The student asked: "How does one recognize such a person? The Master said: "By observing their conduct. The student asked: "What is conduct? The Master said: "Not being deluded by appearances. The student asked: "What is meant by 'not being deluded by appearances'? The Master said: "To see the mind as it truly is. The student asked: "What is the mind as it truly is? The Master said: "Empty and still, without a single thing. The student asked: "If there is nothing at all, how can there be liberation? The Master said: "Liberation is precisely this very state of having nothing. The student asked: "If there is nothing, how can one attain Buddhahood? The Master said: "Buddhahood is attained when one realizes that there is nothing to attain. The student asked: "If there is nothing to attain, why do people seek it? The Master said: "Because they are deluded by their own ignorance. The student asked: "How can one cut through this ignorance? The Master said: "By relying on the Dharma of the Buddhas. The student asked: "What is the Dharma of the Buddhas? The Master said: "The Dharma that is beyond words and thought. The student asked: "How can one enter into this Dharma? The Master said: "By letting go of all attachments. The student asked: "What is meant by 'letting go of all attachments'? The Master said: "To realize that the self and phenomena are originally empty. The student asked: "If everything is empty, how can there be cause and effect? The Master said: "Cause and effect are like reflections in a mirror; though they appear, they have no substance. The student asked: "If they have no substance, how can one experience the fruits of practice? The Master said: "The fruits of practice are like dreams; though they arise, they leave no trace. The student asked: "If there is no trace, how can one benefit sentient beings? The Master said: "Benefiting sentient beings is like the moon reflected in water; it appears everywhere yet is nowhere real. The student asked: "If it is not real, how can one manifest various forms? The Master said: "Manifesting forms is like an echo in the valley; it responds to conditions yet has no origin. The student asked: "If it has no origin, how can one preach the Dharma? The Master said: "Preaching the Dharma is like the wind blowing through the trees; it produces sound yet has no speaker. The student asked: "If there is no speaker, how can the teaching be heard? The Master said: "Hearing the teaching is like the ear perceiving sound; it arises from conditions yet has no hearer. The student asked: "If there is no hearer, how can one attain awakening? The Master said: "Awakening is like the dawn breaking; it illuminates all things yet has no subject. The student asked: "If there is no subject, how can one turn the wheel of the Dharma? The Master said: "Turning the wheel of the Dharma is like the turning of the great earth; it moves all beings yet has no mover. The student asked: "If there is no mover, how can one enter Nirvana? The Master said: "Entering Nirvana is like the extinguishing of a lamp; the light fades, yet its essence remains. The student asked: "If its essence remains, how can one say it is 'extinguished'? The Master said: "Extinction means that there is no longer any delusion. The student asked: "What is non-delusion? The Master said: "To see the nature of the mind as it is. The student asked: "What is the nature of the mind? The Master said: "It is neither existent nor non-existent, neither born nor destroyed. The student asked: "If it is neither born nor destroyed, how can one speak of birth and death? The Master said: "Birth and death are like clouds passing across the sky; they come and go, yet the sky remains unchanged. The student asked: "If the sky remains unchanged, how can one speak of samsara? The Master said: "Samsara is like a dream within a dream; it is vast and boundless, yet ultimately unreal. The student asked: "If it is unreal, how can one escape suffering? The Master said: "Escaping suffering is like waking from a dream; once awake, there is no more sorrow. The student asked: "Once one is awake, what is there to do? The Master said: "There is nothing to do but rest in the natural state. The student asked: "What is the natural state? The Master said: "It is the state of total stillness, free from all conceptualization. The student asked: "How can one abide in this state? The Master said: "By letting go of all striving and remaining in non-action. The student asked: "What is non-action? The Master said: "It is to act without acting, to speak without speaking. The student asked: "How can one speak without speaking? The Master said: "By using words to point beyond words. The student asked: "How can one act without acting? The Master said: "By moving the body while remaining unmoved in spirit. The student asked: "What is meant by 'remaining unmoved in spirit'? The Master said: "To be like a mountain in the midst of a storm; the wind may blow, but the mountain does not shake. The student asked: "If the mountain does not shake, how can it support all beings? The Master said: "Supporting all beings is like the earth holding up the world; it sustains all without discrimination. The student asked: "If it sustains all without discrimination, how can one distinguish between right and wrong? The Master said: "Right and wrong are like the two sides of a coin; they appear distinct, yet they are of one substance. The student asked: "If they are of one substance, how can one cultivate the path? The Master said: "Cultivating the path is like polishing a mirror; the dust is removed, yet the brightness was always there. The student asked: "If the brightness was always there, why did the dust obscure it? The Master said: "The dust of ignorance arose from deluded thoughts. The student asked: "How can one remove these thoughts? The Master said: "By realizing that thoughts are originally empty. The student asked: "If thoughts are empty, how can one produce wisdom? The Master said: "Wisdom is produced when one realizes the emptiness of thoughts. The student asked: "What is the emptiness of thoughts? The Master said: "It is the absence of a self in thoughts. The student asked: "If there is no self, who is it that experiences the fruits of practice? The Master said: "The experiencer is like a phantom; it appears, yet has no reality. The student asked: "If it has no reality, how can one speak of liberation? The Master said: "Liberation is the realization that there is no one to be liberated. The student asked: "If there is no one to be liberated, who is it that attains Buddhahood? The Master said: "The one who attains Buddhahood is like a reflection in the water; it arises from causes and conditions, yet has no substance. The student asked: "If it has no substance, how can one transmit the Dharma? The Master said: "Transmitting the Dharma is like handing over a torch; the flame passes from one to another, yet the wood is different each time. The student asked: "If the wood is different, how can the flame remain the same? The Master said: "The flame remains the same because the nature of fire is constant. The student asked: "What is the nature of fire? The Master said: "It is hot and bright,

He pressed further, "And how was it after he appeared in the world? The Master said, "An edict before Kāśyapa’s platform; a command atop the White Cloud Pavilion.
He asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "It cannot be borne. He pressed further.
[The student] asked, "Why can it not be carried? The Master said, "The meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West.

[The student] asked, "What was it like before Niu-tou saw the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "A high question met with a low answer. [The student] further asked, "What was it like after he saw him?
The Master said, "The wind whistles; the rain falls in torrents."

The Master ascended the hall and said: A monk asked, "Master, you have personally sung the 'One Melody of Yunmen. As for the matter of the Northern Dipper concealing its body, what is it? The Master said, "Discern the field from the sprouts. The student said, "I do not understand;

I specifically request your further instruction. The Master said: *Note: This is a classic *gong'an* (public case) exchange. The "One Melody of Yunmen" refers to the famous verse attributed to Yunmen Wenyan. The "Northern Dipper concealing its body" refers to a kōan concerning the limits of perception and the nature of reality.*
"Whose fault is this? The Master then said, "Excellent, you venerable elders! You who carry your bags and bowls to travel east, west, south, and north—what is it for?
I, this mountain monk, now open my doors wide; I do not fear you coming out to snap my staff or overturn my meditation seat.
Yet, you are still not true adepts. He further said, "The gentleman applies himself to..."
"Fundamentality. When the foundation is established, the Way arises. The Master picked up his staff and said, "Now that it is standing, where is the foundation?
Is it on the tip of the staff? Or is it upon the eyebrows and eyelashes of you all?
He struck the meditation seat once with the staff and said, "Be careful. A monk asked, "Linji would shout as soon as he entered the gate; Deshan..."
As soon as he entered, [the Master] struck him with a staff. The student asked, "How do you guide people here, Preceptor? The Master said, "It is not appropriate.
The student asked, "Why is it not appropriate? The Master then struck him.
The Master ascended the hall and said: "An ancient said, 'Nirvāṇa contains the four virtues; only I realize the direct permanence.
He held up his staff and said, 'Is this not the four virtues? What, then, is true permanence? Do you all understand?
If you do not understand, I, Zuofeng, shall bestow it upon you. He then said, 'The staff pierces through true permanence; true permanence [is the staff itself].'"
"Passing through the four virtues—do you understand? Master Zufeng has untied his sack and emptied it all out at once.
Do any of you have an understanding? Come forward and speak! If you can speak, Zufeng will bear witness for you."
"If you cannot speak, I shall knock off your nostrils and pull out your eyebrows. With these words, he struck the incense altar with his staff and descended from the seat.
The Master then ascended the hall and said: "Look, look! The Tathāgata Sumerudīparāja has finished turning the Great Dharma Wheel upon my staff."
[The Master] entered [the light] into the space between the eyebrows of the various senior monks. "Do you see it yet? If you do not see it, where is your eye?
He struck the meditation seat with his staff and then descended from the seat. A monk asked, "Even the sword Mo-he-yue (Molixie) is dull when cutting iron;

what is the matter regarding 'biting the tip' while facing the front-line? The Master said, "Try using it and see. The monk stepped forward and said, "In that case, I present this to the Han Emperor."
"High King. The Master said, "What principle have you seen? He replied, "The suffering is deep.
The Master said, "The head is in my hands; do as you please, even if you leap about."
The Master ascended the hall and said: "We gather together every morning; the seasons are the same for all. Even so, what should we do?
Have you not seen it said in the teachings: 'All Buddhas, past and present, all emerge from this sutra'?
The Master picked up his staff and said: "Is this not the sutra? Which one here is the Buddha? If you see him, come forth and meet with Zupeng!"
"Listen! If you do not perceive this meaning, the text is too long, so I shall leave it for another day.

Take care. The Master ascended the hall. A monk asked, "Your fame resounds throughout the universe; we have known your mastery for a long time. May we briefly catch a glimpse of the ancestral style of Yunling?
The Master said, "Say more. The monk extended his hands. The Master struck him. The Master then held up his staff and said:
"Is the great assembly present? Once spoken, it shall not be repeated; once commanded, there shall be no second performance. With these words, he descended from his seat.
The Master ascended the hall, picked up his staff, and said: "Maitreya is at the vanguard, Śākyamuni is in the rear;
all are upon the tip of this Patriarchal Peak staff. Do you all see them? He further said: "I contemplate the Dharma of the Dharma-King; the Dharma of the Dharma-King..."
"Is it so? Do you understand? If you do, come forth and speak. If you do not, I shall respectfully await your response.
[The Master] struck the incense altar with his staff and descended from the seat.
The Master ascended the hall. As soon as the assembly had gathered, the Master said: "The bells and drums urge one another; for what purpose are they struck? The former worthies were thus;

how do you, the later followers, understand this? He then raised his staff and said: "The Great Master of old said: 'The root is real, yet the branches differ. For long it has leaned against the cold crags.
It stirs the great ocean and strikes the dragon palace. This mountain monk, too, does not stir the great ocean nor strike the dragon palace."
[The Master] struck the eyebrows and eyelashes of the various senior monks, tapped the incense stand once with his staff, and then descended from his seat.
A monk asked, "In a lion’s den there are no other beasts; right now, please manifest your full majesty.
The Master said, "Try to manifest it yourself. The monk stepped forward and said, "If that is so, then devas and dragons will pay you homage. Thereupon, the Master—
[The Master] struck [the gong]. The Master ascended the hall and said: "Master Yunmen said: 'The Dharma-body has three kinds of illnesses and two kinds of radiance.
Once you have emerged from the thicket of thorns, there are countless dead people upon the pure ground. Is there anyone who can speak of this? Come forth and give it to me!'"
Zufeng said, "Look! If you cannot say it, I shall entrust it to Deshan and Linji. He struck the incense stand once with his staff and then descended from the seat.

The Master ascended the hall, held up his staff, and said: "All Buddhas and the *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* of all Buddhas emerge from this very sutra. Is this staff not the sutra? How do you all understand it?
Old Śākyamuni comes forth from the tip of this staff to preach the Buddha-dharma for you all until you are utterly exhausted."
"I see that you do not understand; rather, you must enter through the tip of the staff. "As for going out, let it be as you say; but how do you explain the principle of entering?
[The Master] struck the incense altar once with the staff and then descended from his seat. Later, the Master addressed the assembly, saying:
"The true Dharma-body of the Buddha is like empty space; responding to things and manifesting forms is like the moon reflected in water."
The Master picked up his staff and said, "This is the staff; where is the moon?
He then continued, "A three-year-old child can say it all, yet a centenarian cannot walk it. He struck the incense stand once with the staff and descended from his seat.
The Master ascended the hall and said: "An ancient said, 'When the four attachments are gone, the hundred negations are all dispelled.
How do you all understand these four attachments? It is like when Puyan was in samādhi at the Buddha’s assembly, observing the lands within a single mote of dust, yet he could not see Samantabhadra.
He then addressed the World-Honored One, saying: 'I have searched everywhere throughout the lands within a single mote of dust for Samantabhadra, but I cannot find him.'"
"You will be able to see him. The World-Honored One said, "If you simply give rise to a single thought within the Pure Samādhi, you will immediately see Samantabhadra.
At that time, Universal Eye suddenly gave rise to a single thought within the Pure Samādhi and immediately saw Samantabhadra riding a six-tusked white elephant toward the sky.
The Master said, "Everyone in the assembly was looking up at this. Samantabhadra, I do not ask about you."
You, tell me: where does the eye of Universal Vision (Samantacakṣus) rest? Take care!
Verse: Yunmen’s Dharmakāya—Yunmen penetrates the Dharmakāya; He cuts off Śākyamuni’s voice, And Mañjuśrī need no longer lament.
Puxian’s "Eulogy on the Prohibitions Regarding Medicines" from the *Manchen Yin*:
"The origins of the prohibitions regarding medicines are examined by masters; Showing his disciples intimately, their ailments are as numerous as hemp."
All the spiritual friends of the ten directions and three periods of time— Like the sun blazing bright amidst thunder and lightning.
Ascending the hall on the first day of the New Year, there is this verse:
"Today is the first day of the first month; The past and the future are both fully revealed."
The wise of the world laugh heartily; who knows, who knows the style of this great house?
On the first day of the first month, one pays homage to Maitreya within the Hall of Avalokiteśvara; Mañjuśrī holds the writing-brush of Samantabhadra in his hand.
In response to a monk’s question regarding Yunmen’s “Withdrawing the Gaze,” Yunmen said: “The patch-robed monk’s eyelids are heavy; the eyelids are heavy.
Seven or eight measures [of weight], a thundering chariot cannot move them; it cannot move them.”
While drawing lots and reciting the name of Amitābha three or five times, may the deceased Li Hu-zǐ of East Village be reborn on Mount Tiānshān;
may Meng Bā-láng remain strong and healthy.
A poor child cries out within Futian Monastery, begging for a single *dàguāng* coin.
A monk asked Zhaozhou about the cypress tree; the Master then composed a verse.
The Chan masters of the world gnaw on Shaolin; Zhaozhou has a saying: "The cypress tree in the courtyard, the cypress tree in the courtyard.
This decrepit old Chan master’s eyes are bloodshot;
unable to distinguish east from west, he has lost the source. He reduces my Avalokiteśvara to a barbarian guest.

Chan Master Yìn of Mount Sijuzu in Qízhōu ascended the hall and said: "The entire universe, all the Buddhas of the three periods of time, and all the old monks of the world—today I have cut them off completely. There is no place for you to show your heads.
Even if you were able to show your heads, you would still be nothing but a spirit of bamboo or wood. Nevertheless, even so, you cannot escape carrying [the burden]."
[The Master] adjudicated the case. He stood for a long time. "Take care. A monk asked, "What is the realm of the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said, "Thousand-year-old pines, cedars, and cypresses; forever green through the four seasons. The monk further asked, "What is one within the realm?
The Master said, "The true portrait of the Patriarch remains for all years; travelers and visitors bow their heads in reverence. [The monk] asked, "What is..."
The Master said, “It is Śākyamuni in the Great Hall. The student asked, “Is it not he? The Master said, “Do not mistake the markings on the scale.
A student asked, “What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, “There are no guests to dine in the kitchen.
The student asked, “When a guest arrives, with what will you entertain them? The Master said, “When a guest comes, one must look upon them.”
Question: What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? The Master said: "On the many-year-old pine tree, the old skin is wrinkled.
[The questioner] said: "I do not ask about picking at the branches and leaves; what is the direct source? The Master said:
"The Buddha’s head is not far from the scale. Question: Regarding Kāśyapa’s upper robe, who is worthy to wear it? The Master said: "Dayu Pass."
"At the mountain pass, it cannot be lifted up; only then do you know that I am not one of your kind. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "One person transmits what is false; ten thousand people transmit what is real. A monk asked, "When the leaves fall and return to the root, what then?
The Master said, "Year by year, there is withering and flourishing."
Chan Master Huaizhi of Guangjiao in Qizhou ascended the hall and said: "When the command is raised and the guiding principle is upheld, the local demons vanish from their tracks.
When the ancestral seal is fully brandished, the ten directions are cut off. At such a time as this, even if the Old Barbarian were to appear, he would have to beg for his life."
“If there are those among you who are true masters, I hope for your discerning insight. At that time, a monk asked, “What is it that has been transmitted from the ancestors?
What should we discuss? The Master said, “The command. The monk pressed further, “If that is so, then people will retreat when they encounter this word.
The Master said, “Heh! Heh! A monk asked, “What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, “How much have you memorized?”
At that time, Jin said, "The student does not understand. How can one attain its practical application? The Master said, "The words are still ringing in my ears.
Jin asked, "What is the matter concerning the ancestral lineage? The Master said, "You have expressed it very clearly. Jin said, "If that is so, then this student prostrates.
The Master said, "I thought you were truly so. Jin asked, "What is this? The Master said, "It is right here before you."
"What thing? Why does the student not understand? The Master said, "I was born in Jizhou.
A monk asked, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharmakāya? The Master answered with a verse.
The Northern Dipper’s phrase for concealing the body—few are those who can meet it head-on. Even when the opportunity is seized, the profound realization remains beyond the reach of the unknowing.
Beyond the green cliffs, the cry of the ape resounds; through the mountain ravines, the tiger’s roar pierces.
The great bell comes to announce the dawn; the cock crows toward the fifth watch.
Chan Master Xinghua Fenneng of Xiangzhou ascended the hall and said: "The moment a single word is uttered, a thousand differences follow the same track.
This is the Transformation Body (nirmāṇakāya) preaching the Dharma; the Reward Body (saṃbhogakāya) does not preach the Dharma. He further asked: "Why does the Reward Body not preach the Dharma?"
He had his own hall and screen. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Vulture Peak? The Master said, "The wind blows through the willows on both banks;
the waves stir the lotuses in the pond. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said, "The Vairocana Buddha in the Great Hall;
the monks from all quarters in the shrine room. The monk asked, "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind do you succeed? The Master said, [silence].
The Master said, "Before Kāśyapa’s Terrace, there is a pagoda of clouds and water. A monk asked, "What is the pivot of Vulture Peak?
The Master said, "Do not move your chopsticks. The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "I told you not to move them."
[The Master] shouted. The monk shouted again, and the Master struck him. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha?

The Master said, "Long hair; the monk's appearance is ugly. A monk asked, "Setting aside the staff and shout for the moment as they are expedients used according to the occasion, what is the pivotal mechanism of Vulture Peak?
The Master said, "Setting aside the pivotal mechanism of Vulture Peak for now, how is it with your own self?"
The student said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Give me back the pivot.
Later, the Master ascended the hall and showed the assembly a verse, saying:
"I ask you, you monks from all ten directions, What is the meaning of coming from the south and going to the north?"
A thousand differences meet the eye, yet there is no divergent path; the stone man snaps his tongue as he recites Amitābha’s name.
Among the essential tenets of the school, nothing is more perilous than the edge of a sword; from this point on, the Patriarch established the fundamental principles.
Gù Jiàn does not know where he has gone; beneath a thousand pine trees, an old man with white hair.
Chan Master Chìmǎn of Tiānmù Mountain in Tānzhōu ascends the hall and addresses the assembly: "Kāśyapa received it in person; it is the secret seal of the Tathāgata.
Dànmó came from the West—much talk, little substance. If we discuss this matter, for the time being let us provisionally take the servant for the master. He spoke thus.
The Buddha spoke of the Patriarchs; carving flesh to form a sore—though this directly clarifies the matter, it is not yet the livelihood of a patch-robed monk.
What, then, is the livelihood of a patch-robed monk? Why do you not test him before the assembly? At that time, a monk prostrated himself.
The Master said, "If you were a traveler from Xiantuo, I would not even wait for you to raise an eyebrow. The monk said, "Yes. The Master said, "Jinzhou."
On the road, two by two and three by three, they asked: "When the Master ascends the lion’s throne and displays his full majestic power, at the peak of Kāśyapa, whom does the Master now serve?
The Master said: "Last night the wind and frost were fierce; this morning the cold cuts to the bone. He further asked:
"If that is so, then you have truly followed the single arrow toward the sun. The Master said: "Calamity!"
"Not acting alone. Question: "When a fish leaps through the waves at the Dragon Gate, its whole body soars and flies.
What is this like? The Master said: "In the third month, thunder and rain stir; a clap of lightning strikes with full majesty. Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: [Silence].
[Taohé] of Duōnián asked: "I do not yet understand the meaning of this; how is it? The Master said: "Break open the person within. [He] asked:
"Regarding the samādhis of all the sages, who is it that should know them? The Master said: "Right now. [He] asked:
"Is it not just this very thing? The Master said: "Clouds rise on the southern mountain; rain falls on the northern mountain. [He] asked: "If..."
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Every three years there is an intercalary month. The student asked, "What should we discuss?
The Master said, "The ninth month is the Double Ninth Festival."
Chan Master Jian Fuzhi Tong of Ezhou ascended the hall and said: "Even if you were to kick it clear and understand it with perfect clarity in a single phrase, you would already have missed the mark;
you would have been defiled by it. What would you do? [I shall] take my leave for a long while. Be well. A monk asked:
"Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said: "The mountains are lofty and the ridges are steep."
The student said, "If that is so, then it is not the same [as before]. The Master said, "The waves of Dongze are clear.
The student asked, "What is the one phrase by which the Master benefits people? The Master said, "A rough recognition of good and evil. The student asked, "What is the direct phrase of Mañjuśrī?
The Master said, "A snap of the fingers reaches Qingliang. The student asked, "Dharmas have no duality; the mind has no duality."
[The student asked: "What is the mind? The Master said: "A thousand differences, ten thousand distinctions. [The student] asked:
"Ascending to Tuṣita at night and descending to Jambudvīpa by day—what kind of realm is this? The Master said: "It is not anyone else's. [The student] asked: "What is the Buddha? The Master said:
"His nose is like a cut bamboo tube. [The student] asked: "Regarding 'the Northern Dipper concealing its body,' what is the meaning?"
The Master said: "The myna bird yearns for Western Qin. Thereupon he offered this verse:
Yunmen penetrates the Dharma-body; As for the Dharma-body, what kind of person is it? When the wild geese return to the desert passes, The myna bird yearns for Western Qin.
Chan Master Chongshan of Fuchang Chan Monastery in Jiangling Prefecture ascended the hall. A monk asked, “What is the Eye of the True Dharma?
The Master said, “Observe the celestial bodies at night. The student said, “I do not understand; what is the meaning of this? The Master said:

"Looking at the mountains in the daylight. [The student] asked, "What is the meaning of 'Chengchang's realm'? The Master said, "Gazing from the Pine Peak Pavilion, it does not level with the white clouds.
[The student] further asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said, "In the morning one sees golden scales leaping; in the evening one hears the cuckoo cry.
[The student] asked, "Are the intent of the Patriarchs and the intent of the Teachings the same or different? The Master... [responded].
[The Master] said: "Nests know the wind; burrows know the rain. [The student] asked: "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said: "In the east, jia-yi is wood. [The student] further said: "If that is so, then I shall grind my bones and shatter my body [to follow it]. The Master said: [Silence].
It is easy to open the mouth at the beginning and end, but difficult to preserve the heart through the cold of winter. Question: “What is Mount Fuchang? The Master said:
“Where birds fly, they cannot pass. [The student] further asked: “What is it like for one within the mountains? The Master said: “The four seas and five lakes. Question:
“Amidst this vast expanse, how does one distinguish the master? The Master said: “The Son of Heaven in Chang’an; beyond the frontier walls.”
The General advanced and said, "If that is so, then power is held firmly in one's hand. The Master said, "One does not execute those who are innocent.
[The General] asked, "What is the dharma that does not transmigrate? The Master said, "A dead person does not sit on a spirit-seat. [The General] further asked, "The student does not understand;
what is the meaning of this? The Master said, "The Nāga is always in samādhi. [The General] asked, "Apart from swallowing..."
[The student] purses his lips at the throat and says, "Please, Master, speak quickly! The Master says, "Fuchang’s mouth is narrow. [The student] asks, "Why, Master, is your mouth narrow?
The Master says, "Give me back the words you just spoke. [The student] asks, "What is the phrase that transcends the trap and the snare?
The Master says, "The head is large, but the hat is small. The student says, "I do not understand; what is the meaning?"

The Master said, "For a long time, my feet have been turned sideways as I wear these boots. A question was asked: "When the golden crow surges from the east and the jade hare sinks in the west, what is the state of affairs?
The Master said, "A scholar does not ride a donkey. The questioner pressed further: "If that is so, then I thank you for your guidance.
The Master said, "You must still be more careful. A question was asked: "What was it like before Oxhead saw the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "..."
[The Master holds] a rosary of *huazi* seeds. The attendant says, “What is it like after seeing [this]? The Master says, “An iron chime, O practitioner.
A student asks, “What is it like when one enters the battlefield before having yet displayed martial skill? The Master says, “This old monk beats the drum of retreat.
The student says, “In that case, the battle lines are deployed and the banners are unfurled. The Master says, “May you enjoy the offering.”
The Master ascended the hall and said, "All the Buddhas of the dust motes throughout the entire universe and great earth are entirely within this Fuchang.
He raised his staff, drew a line on the ground, and said, "Whether it be preaching the Buddhas or preaching the Dharma—if you Zen masters understand this, come forth and I will bear witness for you.
If you do not understand, the flowers must bloom through the night; do not wait for the morning breeze to blow. [He stood] for a long time. Adieu.
[Recorded] at Shuzhou Longmen Mountain, Chan Master Renyong ascended the hall and said: "The verbal explanations of the Buddhas have 'stopping the crying' as their meaning.
The mind-seal of the Patriarchs is beyond all discussion. As for the one path that transcends [all], who would dare set foot upon it? If you can realize it directly here and now—"
“Too early; you have not yet hit the mark. I have stood here for a long time. Take care. A monk asked, “The patriarchs have transmitted it from one to another;
I wonder what it is they transmit? The Master said, “Deshan’s staff. The monk stepped forward and said, “If that is so, then one has attained its subtlety.
The Master struck him. A monk asked, “What is the road to Longmen? The Master said, “Perilous. The monk stepped forward and said, “Why is that so?”
This master said: "He turns back with his forehead marked. [The student] asked: "What is the dragon within the Dragon Gate Mountains?
The master said: "Thunder shakes the azure heavens. [The student] further asked: "What if a golden-winged bird suddenly encounters it? The master said: [Silence].
He overturned the valleys and toppled the mountains. A monk asked, "What is the robe of the Patriarchs? The Master said, "At Mount Dayu, it could not be lifted.
A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Rarely have I encountered such a question."
When Chan Master Zongben of Yanqing in Xiangzhou first opened the hall, he addressed the assembly, saying: "The mountains spread out like shattered jade; the trees hang with silver strands.
At the edge of the Daoan crag, I proclaim the Dharma-vehicle. This is the tradition of Kāśyapa’s gate: if you have any doubts, please ask.
At that time, a monk asked: "The True Dharma is wordless; we pray that the Master will proclaim it. The Master said: "Right now is the very day! The monk stepped forward.
The student said, "If it is so, then one has met the Master. The Master said, "A total embarrassment. The student said, "Truly so.
The Master said, "I grant you twenty blows of the staff. A student asked, "What is it like when the fish has not yet leaped over the Dragon Gate?
The Master said, "Waving his hand, he enters Chang'an. The student pressed further, "And after he has leaped over it? The Master said, "Chang'an."
[The Master] said, "Though joyful. [The student] asked, "What is Fengshan? The Master said, "A natural bearing bestowed by Heaven.
[The student] further asked, "What is one who dwells among the mountains? The Master said, "Ancient in appearance, no one recognizes him.

[The student] asked, "What is the Master’s single phrase for benefiting others? The Master said, "Severing the Fenglin Pass. [The student] further asked, "If that is so, then [the Master] extends his hand."
"I have not met anyone," [the monk said]. The Master then struck him.
When Chan Master Huixun of Mount Fuan in Tangzhou first ascended the seat for his inaugural hall-opening ceremony, a monk asked: "Whose song does the Master sing?
Whose lineage of the ancestral wind do you succeed? The Master said: "The ancient hall reaches the clouds and waters. [The monk] further asked: "In that case..."
He was the direct descendant of Shao Yang and the legitimate son of Longju. The Master said, "When words are repeated, they should not be taken literally.
A monk asked, "When our Buddha appeared in the world, he shook the palaces of the Māras. When you, Preceptor, appear in the world, what auspicious signs will there be?
The Master said, "The water of Bi flows straight south. When the Master first accepted the invitation to Tangzhou, a monk asked him, "If you arrive at Biyang, suddenly—"
"Whether they be officials or private persons, men or women—let each person pose one question, and let each question be distinct. How do you respond?
The Master said, "After spring, the first yang arises. [The student] asked, "If that is so, then today is a small departure meeting with a great encounter.
The Master took up his sitting cloth (*zuoju*) and spread it out directly in front of him. He then asked, "What was the intention of the Patriarch in coming to this land?"
"What is the essential meaning? The Master said, "Direct. The monk asked, "When the Human King and the Dharma King meet, what then? The Master said, "A dispatch.
The monk asked, "Before leaving Tuṣita Heaven, he has already descended into the royal palace; before emerging from his mother's womb, he has already finished saving sentient beings—what then?
The Master said, "It is not that one does not know this good matter."
Chan Master Byeonghyeon of Dae龙山 (Dae-ryong-san) in Dingzhou ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Dae-ryong?
The Master said, "A mound of earth before the hall, towering and leaning against half the sky. The monk pressed further, "What is the person within the realm?
The Master said, "Sweeping the ground before the gate clean, welcoming guests from the five lakes. [The monk] asked, "What is..."
The Master said: "Piercing through the clouds, he does not cross the waters; treading his feet down, he descends to Jambudvīpa. Question:
"Regarding the words of the former master in the past, how does one penetrate the Dharma-body? The Master said: "The phrase before the ten-thousand-fathom peak does not level with the white clouds."

Question: "What is the phrase that moves heaven and earth? The Verse on the Fish Drum: A single blow causes the ocean waves to surge and boil; The light of heaven reflects back, blinding the eyes with its glare. Xuansha heard the mention and awakened within it; At once he said, "I cannot guarantee that [the one who spoke] is him. The fish drum resonates through the void; The golden cock crows at the edge of the sky. The great matter is not found in words; How could it be grasped by the mind? The fish drum beats, the golden cock crows; The whole world is filled with their sound. If you can hear it here and now, You will know the source of the Way. If you do not hear it here and now, You will wander lost in the six realms. Do not seek it in the past or the future; Seek it directly within your own mind. If you can see it clearly right now, You will transcend birth and death. If you cannot see it clearly right now, You will remain trapped in the cycle of rebirth. Do not rely on external conditions; Rely instead on your own internal realization. If you can realize it yourself, You will attain liberation. If you cannot realize it yourself, You will remain bound by delusion. Do not seek it in scriptures or commentaries; Seek it in the silence before speech. If you can enter this silence, You will find the true path. If you cannot enter this silence, You will remain lost in confusion. Do not seek it in the mountains or the forests; Seek it in the midst of daily life. If you can see it in daily life, You will be free from attachment. If you cannot see it in daily life, You will remain bound by worldly concerns. Do not seek it in the past or the future; Seek it in the present moment. If you can grasp it in the present moment, You will attain the ultimate truth. If you cannot grasp it in the present moment, You will remain caught in the flow of time. Do not seek it in the north or the south; Seek it in the center of your being. If you can find it in the center of your being, You will realize your original nature. If you cannot find it in the center of your being, You will remain obscured by ignorance. Do not seek it in the heavens or the earth; Seek it in the space between your eyebrows. If you can look there with clarity, You will see the Buddha-nature. If you cannot look there with clarity, You will remain blind to reality. Do not seek it in the east or the west; Seek it in the direction of your own mind. If you can turn your mind inward, You will find the source of all things. If you cannot turn your mind inward, You will remain lost in the external world. Do not seek it in the beginning or the end; Seek it in the middle of the path. If you can walk the middle way, You will avoid extremes. If you cannot walk the middle way, You will fall into bias. Do not seek it in the high or the low; Seek it in the equality of all things. If you can perceive this equality, You will transcend discrimination. If you cannot perceive this equality, You will remain mired in dualism. Do not seek it in the self or the other; Seek it in the non-duality of subject and object. If you can realize this non-duality, You will attain the Great Peace. If you cannot realize this non-duality, You will remain subject to conflict. Do not seek it in the known or the unknown; Seek it in the state beyond knowing. If you can dwell in the state beyond knowing, You will be free from thought. If you cannot dwell in the state beyond knowing, You will remain bound by concepts. Do not seek it in the past or the future; Seek it in the eternal now. If you can abide in the eternal now, You will be at peace. If you cannot abide in the eternal now, You will remain restless. The Master said, "I cannot say any more to you. [The student] stepped forward and said, "If that is so, then the fragrant breeze rises across the earth, and the Patriarchal Sun renews throughout the heavens.
The Master said, "That too is merely the sound of a bowl ringing. [The student] asked, "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does he inherit?
The Master said, "A thousand-fathom snow on Qingcheng Mountain; ten thousand layers of peaks beyond the clouds."
The student said, "In that case, the waters of the Jin River branch out, and the fragrant groves divide their boughs. The Master said, "Friends fill the world, but how many truly know my heart?
A question was asked: "The ancestral lamp continues its flame; the Grand Marshal presides at the banquet. What is the principle beyond this?"
"Please, Master, grant us your instruction. The Master said, "The entire assembly sees it clearly. The student stepped forward and said, "If that is so, then the clouds disperse and the waters flow.
The Master said, "Quickly, prostrate three times. A question was asked: "The teachings of the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the scriptures are expedient means tailored to the times.

The student said, "If that is so, then there is no continuity. The Master said, "Quickly, prostrate yourself!
The Master ascended the hall, looked around left and right, and said, "Is there anyone who is a true master? Come forth and resolve this before the assembly. After a long silence...

A monk asked, "The teachings of the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the canon merely serve to stop a child's crying while manifesting the principle. Setting aside the throat, lips, and mouth, I ask the Master to speak.

Question: “A Bodhisattva of the Ten Grounds perceives the nature as if through fine gauze. What exactly does a Bodhisattva of the First Ground perceive as being veiled?
The Master said: “Mount Sumeru. Questioner: “How can one penetrate it? Master: “Three lifetimes, sixty kalpas. Question:

A Verse on the Essential Lineage: The essential point is not found in words or phrases; It is not something that can be grasped by the mind. If you seek it through conceptual thought, you will be lost; If you try to measure it with the intellect, you will fail. Do not mistake the finger for the moon; Do not mistake the boat for the shore. If you understand this principle, you will see clearly; If you do not, you remain mired in delusion. The ancient sages have transmitted it directly; They did not rely on books or scriptures. If you wish to enter the gate of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, You must first sever the root of doubt. Do not seek outside yourself; Do not look within. When the mind is empty and still, the Way appears; When thoughts cease, reality is revealed. This is the true lineage of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; It is the ultimate secret of the ancestral teachers. Do not let your efforts be in vain; Do not waste your time in idle talk. If you can realize this right now, You will transcend birth and death. This is the Great Matter; It is not something to be taken lightly. If you encounter a true teacher, You will receive the direct transmission. Do not rely on secondary explanations; Do not follow the traces of others. Awaken to your own original face; Realize your inherent nature. This is the heart of the Dharma; This is the source of liberation. All phenomena are but one mind; All teachings are but one truth. Do not be confused by appearances; Do not be distracted by forms. Maintain a single-minded focus; Be steadfast and unwavering. Then you will attain the great peace; Then you will realize the ultimate freedom. This is the final word of the ancestral school; This is the legacy of the patriarchs. May all who hear this verse Attain awakening immediately. Thus ends the verse on the essential lineage.

The sky is clear as the roof is thatched; The grain is harvested under the canopy of heaven. Having paid the king’s taxes early, I sing a song with a full belly. A verse on the Bathing of the Buddha: When the world was first formed, The Buddha appeared in the world. He manifested in the human realm To preach the Dharma for all beings. His body was like pure gold, His marks and signs complete. With a compassionate heart, He brought peace to the world. The great earth shook six times, And the heavens rained down flowers. The gods and humans rejoiced, As they bathed the World-Honored One. The fragrance of incense filled the air, And music resounded through the ten directions. All who saw him were moved to faith, As he taught the path of liberation. May all sentient beings Attain the fruit of Buddhahood. Through this merit, May all be reborn in the Pure Land. May the Three Jewels endure forever, And the Dharma wheel turn eternally. May all living beings Together realize the Way.
On the eighth day of the fourth month, the Buddha’s birthday, he pointed to heaven and earth, declaring himself the foremost;
nine dragons sprayed water to bathe his golden body. *Mahāprajñāpāramitā*.
A verse by Master Bimbara holding a staff.
Weeds overgrow the fields and he is old and decrepit; his eyes grow increasingly dim. Unable to save himself, he has no remedy, yet still holds a fork.
When the hunters of Lingnan saw him at that time, they struck him dead with a single blow—thus one realizes the house of Māra.
One day, feeling unwell, he ascended the hall to take leave of the assembly. On the morning of the seventh day, he passed away. At the time of the midday meal, he returned once more.
He then recited a verse on the Dharmakāya for the assembly:
"In practicing Chan and studying the Way, do not be in such a hurry; Question through until the Dharmakāya is revealed within the Northern Dipper.
I am now old, decrepit, and extremely frail; Seeing others, I lack the strength to engage in discussion."

Chan Master Faguang of Gaoyang Mountain in汝州 (Ruzhou) ascended the hall. A monk asked, "Among the three bodies, which one is the primary body?
The Master said, "The bird-path is profound and mysterious, without obstruction; the stone man’s eyes do not distinguish flowers.
The monk pressed further, "In that case, every place is the true trace; penetrating the depths, it does not continue with the dust of the world. The Master said, "Transverse."
The body is beyond the three realms; it dwells everywhere, never hidden. Question: When Niutou had not yet met the Fourth Patriarch, why did the hundred birds bring flowers to offer him?
Master: "The spring warmth brings forth life without obstruction; the vast, enlightened source is revered by all species. Questioner:

"Riding an ox, he does not enter the grass. Question: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "Nine years facing the wall—hard for others to discern.
A single phrase of the clear flow—matters cannot be peered into. Question: "The assembly is about to take their meal; we request the Master [to speak]."
The Master raised his voice and said: "A single sound produces phrases as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; the vast and empty spiritual source responds to ten thousand occasions.
Question: "What is the great compassion of the thousand hands and eyes? The Master said: "Falling into pits and ditches according to one's path.
Question: "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said: "A single word, free from private bias, awaits only the guests from the five lakes. Question: [Unfinished]
"What is the Way? The Master said, "It is not far from here to Xiangzhou. The student asked, "What is one who is on the Way?
The Master said, "Traveling south and traveling north."
Master Jiecheng of Shishuang Mountain in Tanzhou ascended the hall. A monk asked, "I have heard it said of old: 'Before one's eyes are green mountains with not an inch of tree;
looking out to the horizon, there is clear water with no waves. I wonder, what then is the Buddha Hall and the Sangha Hall?
The Master said, "The wind strikes the treetops and waves arise; at midnight, the stone man rows his boat home."

The flowers and trees are exquisite throughout the four seasons. Question: Who is the person within the realm? The Master said: [He] is... (text ends).
Facing the white clouds at their source. He asked: "I have heard it said of old: 'Rolling up the curtain to face the bright day; shifting the mat to face the green mountains.

"A precious sword as sharp as frost. The student asked, "How does one comprehend this? The Master said, "The golden armor resembles fish scales; the vermilion banners are like flames of fire.

This morning a wildfire broke out.

If an ordinary person comes, I strike them. If a sage comes, I strike them. If they come in this way, I strike them;

The Master said: "The great earth, mountains, and rivers leave no path for penetration; the worlds of the ten directions are all accommodated at once. A student asked: "What is the pure *dharmakāya*?
The Master said: "A barbarian’s leather bag filled with things. The student asked: "How does one comprehend this? The Master said:

"Offerings are beyond discussion. A student asked: "What is the urgent matter of the ancients? The Master said: "A barbarian’s leather bag filled with things. The student asked: "How does one comprehend this? The Master said: "Offerings are beyond discussion."
The Master said: "When his hair was spread upon the mud, it was as if tears were falling in the courtyard. A student asked: "How does one maintain this within the midst of time?

The student asked, "When the Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū sat at the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas, why did he not attain the Way of Buddhahood? The Master said, "He was greedily gazing at the moon in the sky."

[The Master] withdrew the pearl from his palm. A question was asked: "Regarding the moon painted on Mount Ling, what is its intended meaning? The Master said: "It cannot be grasped at the bottom of the water;
it may be buried beneath the earth. A question was asked: "What is it like when military affairs are urgent? The Master said: [He withdrew the pearl from his palm.]
[The Master] said, "Dust covers his face at the crossroads. The student asked, "Why is it so? The Master said, "Knowing it, one deliberately commits it. A question was asked:
"What is it like when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished? The Master said, "It illuminates heaven and earth. The student pressed further.
[The student] asked, "What is it like after being ground down? The Master said, "Not even a hair's breadth remains. [The student] asked, "What is the discourse on the unconditioned?
The Master said, "The stone rams and stone tigers chatter away. [The student] asked, "What kind of teaching is this? The Master said, [silence].
The prose would not suffice to record it all; the short verses have ceased to be heard by men. Question: "What is the one phrase of great function?
The Master said: "Heaven and earth are pitch black. The student asked: "How is it when it is not being used? The Master said: "The boundaries of the world are brilliantly clear. Question:
"How is it when the precious sword has not yet been polished? The Master said: "Its radiance pierces the Northern Dipper. [The student] advanced.
[The student] asked: "After polishing, what is it like? The Master said: "Entering the water, silent and without sound. [The student] asked:
"Before clarifying the wisdom of differentiation, how can one attain freedom from doubt? The Master said: "Creating wind and dust yourself, you act as a lowly guest;
failing to recognize true gold, you labor in vain. [The student] asked: "Throughout the twelve periods of the day, how does one cultivate progress? The Master said: "Do not seek it within the water."
The Moon: A single orb touches the eyes; how can students not see it? The Master said: "It pierces through your skull. Question:
What were Mañjuśrī and Vimalakīrti discussing when they conversed? The Master said: "A sweet rain falls at night; the stone woman lights a lamp at night. Question:
When one applies the mind with the mind, what is it like? The Master said: "The Northern Miao Mountains."
"Several times a guest on the mountain; years uncounted aboard a ship in the South Sea.
The Master ascended the hall and said, "Virtuous Chan practitioners: those who study the Way must possess the eye of a patch-robed monk before they can succeed.

If you possess the eye of a divine monk, you will not be obstructed by Buddhas, obstructed by patriarchs, or obstructed by Bodhi and Nirvana. You will then attain freedom wherever you go and enter [the Way]."
Water cannot drown him; fire cannot burn him. He walks upon the earth as if on water; he walks upon water as if on earth. After a long while, he said, "What is the eye of a patch-robed monk?
Let anyone come forward and demonstrate it before the assembly; I will grant that your study of the Way is complete.
If there is no one, you have been thoroughly deceived by the Buddhas, the Patriarchs, Bodhi, and Nirvana. The Master struck the meditation seat once and descended from his seat.
A monk asked, "What is the single phrase for the moment of encounter? The Master said, "An arrow released from the bowstring leaves no trace;
one wearing boots and a hat wanders in the sea. A monk asked, "What is Bodhi as it meets the eye? The Master said, "A cold wind blows across the face until it cracks;
upon the snow, frost is added once more. A monk asked, "What is the Immovable Honored One? The Master said, "Luminous clarity."
The enlightened person does not recognize it; those who offer worship lack anyone to understand them. Question: "All phenomena return to the One. To what does the One return? The Master said:
"Before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion, a hundred acrobatic feats are displayed; beneath a thousand pine trees, the birds sing. Question:
"It is said that making offerings to hundreds of thousands of Buddhas is not as good as making offerings to a single mindless man of the Way. What fault do the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas have?"
"What virtues does a man of the Way who is without mind possess? The Master said: "When the yang energy arises, there is no hard ground;
when the ice melts and the snow is exhausted, all at once it ceases. Question: "When a phrase is cut off, clarity manifests; when names and words are touched upon, they penetrate everywhere.
How is this so? The Master said: "The golden body is not produced; entering the water, it is silent and makes no sound. Question: "When the single truth contains the dharma-realm..."
"How is it? The Master said, "A single drop of unconditioned water flows day and night through a thousand rivers.
Question: "What is the lion within the site of enlightenment (dojō)? The Master said, "With one roar, heaven and earth merge; throughout the ten directions of the world, no witness remains.
Question: "How is it when two blades cross in combat? The Master said, "At midnight, the son is especially close."
The student asked, "How is it when the sky breaks into dawn? The Master said, "Leave it to you to speculate. A question was asked: "What is the sword of Mañjuśrī?
The Master said, "Three feet of snowy radiance beyond the azure heavens; the dust and shadows of the four quarters have ceased, and the halberds are laid down.
A question was asked: "When traveling alone within the ocean of the Flower Treasury, what then? The Master said, "The seashore."
In a place of solitary isolation, one stands majestic, yet no one knows it. The student asked: "After knowing this, what then? The Master said:
"Only then do you see your original body. The student asked: "How far apart are the Way of Kings and the Way of Dharma?

The Master said: "Clouds move and rain falls thickly; water flows swiftly and waves arise. The student did not understand and asked: "I do not yet comprehend this; how is it so? The Master said: "The water flows."
Returning to the sea. A man lies amidst a thousand peaks. Question: "What is the functioning of *prajñā*? The Master said: "The celestial Māras’ gall blisters;
the heretics’ hearts crumble. Question: "What is the place where a student establishes themselves? The Master said: "At the crossroads, people do not look back;

[The Master] brandishes his sword. The student says, "The seven stars’ radiance turns through the Milky Way; it cuts off the waves of Vairocana’s market town.
The Master asks, "Is this not so? The student says, "No. The Master says, "Like a person blind from birth, it cannot be known. The student bows. The Master sighs.
The student asks, "What is the mechanism that cuts people? The Master says, "A crossroads."
The path’s head is clearly revealed; with a single mind, there is no difference and no deviation. The student said, “Is this not it?

The Master said, “If you conceive of it in your mind, you are separated by a thousand miles; look at the profound mystery as it naturally is. The student said, “If that is so, then...”

"If you cannot speak, your entire life will have passed in vain. After a long silence, he struck the meditation seat once and then descended from it.

Wei-guo ultimately returns to the West with a single sandal."

At that time, a monk asked, "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style does he succeed? The Master said, "Fortunately, I have never raised my feet in praise;
people insist on saying they see the sands of the Ganges. The monk pressed further, "Coming as you have done, I beg the Master for the definitive truth.

What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "Why do you not ask about your own meaning?"

Flute. The rustic elder sings unevenly by the streamside. The Master then said: "In the past, Subhūti sat in meditative repose within a cave.
Brahmā rained down flowers in praise. Subhūti asked, 'Who is this person praising from the air?
Brahmā replied, 'I am Brahmā. Subhūti asked, 'How do you praise? Brahmā said, 'I see that the Venerable One has spoken well.'"
Regarding "Prajñā," [Huai]tiyun said: "As for Prajñā, I have never uttered a single word. He added: "In Sanskrit it is said: 'The Venerable One has nothing to say;
I, therefore, have nothing to hear. That there is nothing to say and nothing to hear—this is the true teaching of Prajñā.
The Master said: "When Brahmā speaks thus, does it accord with Subhūti’s intent? It is simply a state of no words and no speech, not involving sight or hearing."
This is still but a high embankment to Nirvana and a deep pit of liberation. If it were Yaoshan, it would be otherwise:

when Mañjuśrī brandishes his sword, the stone man’s gall blanches and the wooden woman’s heart trembles. You venerable elders and masters who have long lingered among the various offices—please take care of yourselves.

you shall not appear in the world. Thereafter, the Master withdrew from public view. He was constantly devoted to seated meditation and shaved his head during all four seasons.

[The Master] ate but one meal a day. A monk asked, "In the twelve hours of the day, what do you take as your seat? The Master said, "Where have you seen him? [Another] asked, "To where has the late master Liangshan departed after his passing?

The Master said: *Note: The original Chinese text provided is incomplete at the end. The response to the second question is typically recorded as "He has returned to the place from which he came" (歸本處), though this specific phrasing was not included in the source fragment.*

He smashed the dull chicken’s egg; the phoenix fled away. The student asked, “Ultimately, where does it return? The Master said, “The green mountains are ever towering; the flowing waters are naturally vast.

A questioner asked, “I beg the Master for instruction on the point of intimacy. The Master said, “This old monk was originally a man from Guangnan. One day, the Master composed a verse and posted it: Smashing the dull chicken’s egg, The phoenix soars away.

Upon the wall of the Dharma Hall:

Regarding the elder brother, Master Jia Shan: when the Master first visited Qing Lin, he asked, "Do the various sages of the past have a share for a student like me?
Qing Lin remained seated as before. After the Master had sat in silence for a long while, Qing Lin asked, "Do you understand? The Master [remained silent].

Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A cool breeze blows, chilling the person;
how long can a bubble float upon the water? He was asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Good brother! Solitary beyond all things."
Riding a thousand-li elephant, he strikes a full bell beneath ten-thousand-year-old pines. A monk asked, "What is the true master of Jia Shan?

Riding a fine steed, galloping atop a high tower; with an iron whip, pointing the way for all the Hu people. Later, King Ma invited the Master from the Green Forest.
