The Master said, "A man waiting for a ferry by the riverbank, while the old fisherman on the shore calls out repeatedly."
[The Master] beckons with his hand. He asks, "The land is peaceful and clear; who acts as its ruler? The Master says, "He waves his hand, and the universe trembles.
The student says, "And what of the Way of Kings? The Master says, "Fine grain forms ears together; the village elders sing songs of joy.
The student says, "Is there still a further place for clear understanding beyond this? The Master says, "There is. The student steps forward and says, "Such as..."
"What is this matter that transcends [the mundane]? The Master said: "Even Yao and Shun did not hold court beneath the forest; they washed their ears by the river and drank while tending cattle.
[The student] asked: "A crescent moon falls upon the empty mountain; where has the single sandal gone? The Master said: "Clouds and mist gather on the Western Mountain;
when the moon shines bright on the Eastern Ridge. [The student] further asked: "When a student raises his hand in this manner, what then?"
The Master said: "A single wheel covers the entire earth; ten thousand phenomena gaze upon it together.
Chan Master Zhidu of Guangdeshan in Xiangzhou ascended the hall. A monk asked, "Where have all the sages of the past gone? The Master said:
"The imperial carriage does not travel through the Golden World; with a bamboo hat in hand, he asks the way from an old farmer."
Question: "How was it before Niutou had seen the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said: "He put on his robes and ate his meals.
The questioner asked: "How was it after he saw him? The Master said: "He put on his robes and ate his meals. Question: "What is Guangdeshan? The Master said: "In the sun, flowers bloom easily;
in the shade, snow is hard to melt. The questioner asked: "What is the mountain? The Master said: "He put on his robes and ate his meals."
The Master said: "If the morning glow does not appear at the gate, the evening glow travels a thousand miles.
Chan Master Xian of Beichan Monastery in Tanzhou had a monk ask him: "When you visited Shimen, what did you obtain?
The Master said: "The golden flower contains the jade bud; it blooms amidst the snow in the desolate fields. [The monk] asked: "What is True Suchness-Buddha?"
The Master said: "Flowing with the current, there is no obstruction; wherever it is applied, it is the truth. The student asked: "The wanderer has returned home;
there is no other name for it. The Master said: "At every point, do not extend your hand; in every thing, do not labor in vain. [The student] asked:
"What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "A single wheel faces the universe; everywhere it shines with brilliance.
The student asked further, "If a guest suddenly arrives, how do you receive and attend to them? The Master said, "Every thing is entirely without toil;
every point requires no device of the cowherd."
Chan Master Yunyu of Taoyuan Mountain in Cizhou ascended the seat for the opening of the hall. He said, "The wondrous intent of the West-facing [Bodhidharma] is difficult to encounter face-to-face.
A thousand mechanisms flash like lightning; there is no need to labor over deliberation. If there is anyone who has achieved something, please come forward to meet me.
At that time, a monk stepped forward and bowed. The Master said, "Your feet have already missed the mark. As the monk rose from his bow, intending to ask a question, the Master—

[The Master] said, "Once the four horses have galloped away, they are difficult to pursue. A question was asked: "The Phoenix’s One Song—Master, please sing it yourself; we pray you will reveal its profound mystery with a single sound.
The Master said, "This great resonance does not accord with the melodies of the human world. It issues directly from the azure heavens; can you harmonize with it?

He stepped forward and said, "If that is so, then the voice of wisdom cannot be harmonized. The Master said, "Frost and ice fill his mouth, chilling to the very marrow of his bones. Beneath the cliff..."
The stone man smiled and nodded his head. A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Water flows down the ravine;
clouds emerge from the mountain peaks.
At Beichan Temple in Tanzhou, Chan Master Huigan had a monk ask, "What is that which all the sages use to benefit people?"
The Master said, “The crimson sun faces ten thousand households; its light illuminates all below without partiality.
The student asked, “What is the phrase by which you, the Master, benefit others? The Master said, “The golden hook mingles with the jade waves; how would a swimming fish dare swallow it?
The student said, “In that case, I shall return home empty-handed. The Master said, “Whom do you blame? [The student] asked, “What is...? (The question is left unfinished).
The Master said: "An inch may be short, but a cun may be long.
Shuzhou Simenshan Baolin Chan Master had a monk ask him, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master replied, "The mountains are cold and the ice is freezing. The Master asked a monk in charge of construction: "Since it is fundamentally perfected of itself, why must you open it up?"
Zhaozuo said, "I have brought my chains and my record of offenses. The Master said, "Not yet. Speak further.
Zhaozuo said, "A double case. The Master raised his staff; as Zhaozuo hesitated, the Master struck him.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "From Shuzhou. The Master said, "You have fallen right into the hands of the Four Sides. The monk was speechless.
The Master said, "Sit for a moment and drink tea.
A Verse on the Staff:
A single staff extends in all four directions; It tests dragons and elephants when the occasion arises; Their horns and crests slightly rise and fall.
When the lightning-flash descended upon his back at Guangde Mountain in Xiangzhou, Chan Master Zhongzhi was asked by a monk: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does he succeed?
The Master said: "White clouds drift over Fengling; the whole world sings of peace. He was further asked: "What of this Guangde?"

The Master [Daowu] personally cited the precedent: "What was the meaning beneath the Phoenix Rock? The Master said, "A single stream from the numinous source flows differently, responding to ten thousand occasions.
Question: "What is the phrase for being in accord with the season? The Master said, "When it is cold, turn toward the fire.
The student said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "When it is hot, seek the cool."
A monk asked Chan Master Yicheng of Qingfeng Mountain in Fengxiang Prefecture: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style does he inherit? The Master said:
"For ten years I roamed the Han River; now I have shed a phoenix feather. The monk asked: "What is the house style of Qingfeng? The Master said:
"Facing the fire while eating sweet melons. The monk asked: "The non-arising of the three periods is..."
"What is the realm? The Master said, "White clouds at Lotus Snow Mountain; the bright moon blends with the fishhook.
The student asked, "I wonder, is there anything further beyond this? The Master said, "There is. The student asked, "What is the matter beyond this?
The Master said, "The numinous light pierces through the color of lapis lazuli; when the great earth is illuminated, all traces of blemish vanish. [Question: "As for this..."
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "A stone ox blocks the ancient road; a wooden horse gallops atop the high tower.
Chan Master Zhen of Jingde Monastery in Yongkang Commandery had a monk ask: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind do you succeed? The Master said:
"Under the rootless tree, the direct entrustment was given; who else could testify to this at the bottom of the well?"
The student said, "Although I have received the Master’s instruction on the spirit of our school, what is it like at this very assembly today?
The Master said, "The golden dragon emerges from its cave as auspicious light gathers; the phoenix spreads its wings as wild clouds fly. The student asked, "What is the Way?
The Master said, "Though there are a thousand differences, the single moon shines without partiality. The student asked, "What is the Way within the Way?"
The Master said: "To travel the profound without lifting a foot; let the Bird Path pass as it will. Question: "What is before all Buddhas?
The Master said: "A flake of snow locks the cold crag. He pressed further: "What is after all Buddhas? The Master said:
"Dripping—there is nothing like it."
A monk asked Chan Master Shaorong of Guangjiao Monastery in Xingyuan Prefecture, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "Rice from Mount Dou; water-moss from River Rang. The monk asked, "What is the matter transmitted from of old?
The Master said, "A sliver of the moon flows with its radiance, containing the myriad phenomena within its light. The monk pressed further, "As for the matter right now..."
"Furthermore, how is it? The Master said, "The drum that shakes heaven and earth is struck, yet those in their dreams are not yet startled.
Chan Master Yiqin of Chengtian Monastery in Jiazhou had a monk ask, "What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "Not worth half a penny. The monk pressed further, "If a guest suddenly arrives, with what will you receive them? The Master—
[The Master] said: "The entire platter is displayed, yet nothing can be brought forth; those who arrive must know the proper time. Question: "What are words of ultimate truth?
The Master said: "A black dot on a white cloth."
Dharma Master Fahua of Raoyi Temple in Tongzhou went on pilgrimage to the assembly of Chan Master Cheshi at Shimen in Xiangzhou.
One morning, he went to pay his respects. Cheshi said, "The sky has been overcast for several days; where has the sun gone?
The Master remained silent for a long while and said, "I cannot say. Cheshi said, "You ask, and I will give it to you."
Dàoshī then asked, "For several days the sky has been overcast; where has the sun gone? Chè replied, "In the kitchen, there is the sound of the rafters creaking.
The Master said, "I understand. Chè asked, "What principle have you perceived? The Master said, "In the kitchen, there is the sound of the rafters creaking.
Because of this, the Master attained awakening. He returned to his own temple and, although he did not appear in the world again, [he remained there].
The assembly in the Yun-tang hall was always full of over a hundred practitioners. The Master also vowed never to leave the monastery and constantly recited the Lotus Sutra.
Once, when a monk was about to depart for Shimen, the Master sent him a question. When the monk arrived at Shimen, he asked: "What is it like when the golden phoenix pierces through the white clouds?
Cheng (the master of Shimen) said: "The full moon of Haizhou appears; its brilliance fills the ends of the earth. Cheng then said: [The Master’s original question].
"Stop! This question was self-initiated. Someone taught you it. If it was self-initiated, you must explain how.
If you cannot explain it, you shall receive a beating and leave the monastery. The monk said, "This was asked by Fahu of Raoyi Temple in the same prefecture;
he instructed me to ask. Changche said, "I knew from the start that this was not your own question. Later, Master Changche repeatedly sent people to fetch [the monk] and command him [to come].
While staying at Shimen, the Master firmly declined [the invitation].
He then sent a poem in the style of a moon ode: Through vast eons it rolls across the long sky; The scenery of mountains and rivers is fresh and clear.
A thousand households hold auspicious luster; A single orb hangs over ten thousand miles. It illuminates the shadows of all that exists; Impartially, it pervades the great trichiliocosm.
The great void cannot be retained; how could it be covered by drifting white clouds?
Entering the hall, he said: "Destroy the Hu seed! Destroy the Hu seed!
The Head Seat Jūn of Shimen Mountain in Xiangzhou received his formal training at Jincang Monastery in Taiyuan. Since entering here..."
For over thirty years at Mount [Name], every time he had finished his midday meal, he would shoulder a hoe and part the brambles, planting pears and chestnuts by hand throughout the mountain fields.

He shared his remaining provisions with the assembly, and his noble conduct was such that the monastic communities admired him. Though he was invited three times by both the ordained and the laity to take charge of a monastery, he did not accept.
One day, while tea was being served at the request of a monk, the monk asked: "What is the Head? (or "What is the First?")
"Take a seat. The Master said, "I still remember you from just now. The monk said, "And how is it right now?
The Master said, "Sit well. Tea is being served. Once, while the Master was carrying a hoe into the garden, a monk asked, "Among the three bodies (trikāya), which one goes to perform manual labor?
The Master stood with the hoe propped against him. The monk said, "Do not take this as the ultimate truth."
Without a teacher, he took up his hoe and departed.
A monk asked Chan Master Qianian of Beichen Temple in Tanzhou, "What is the source of the Great Way?
The Master said, "The myriad streams cannot be mixed. The monk pressed further, "How is it when one is uniquely liberated? The Master said, "It pierces the clouds and penetrates [the mountains]."
Shi asked, "What is the phrase that does not fall into the past or present? The Master said, "The fifteenth and the sixteenth;
the sun and moon pursue one another.
Zhaozhou Shishi, the third-generation abbot of Liangshan in Dingzhou, ascended the hall and said: "Day after day, the bells are struck and the drums beaten."

Originally, one is not deluded; why then seek awakening? All you venerable elders, before you have even reached the pavilion at Liangshan Bridge, you already possess thirty kinds of coarse distinctions.
Now that you have come up here, what are you looking for? Take care! A monk asked, "When one brushes away the dust and sees the Buddha, what then?
The Master said, "Do not let your eyes grow dim. The monk asked, "At what time did the Master become a Buddha? The Master said:
"Furthermore, do not suppress the worthy to make them base. A student asked, "Why, Master, do you refuse to accept [the responsibility]?
The Master said, "Better that good things be non-existent. The Master then cited the case of Zen Master Luzu, who would simply face the wall whenever a monk approached.
There is a verse that says:
"Lu Zu’s samādhi is most effortless: As soon as he sees a monk approach, he turns his back to the wall.
If one is a person who knows the heart and reaches the Way, It is not necessary to raise an eyebrow for them to understand."
Because a monk was possessed of afflictions, the Master composed a verse, saying:
"If a person’s mind is set upon the Way, Afflictions will naturally vanish. It is not that there is no mind;
The Dharma is originally as vast as empty space."
The Cowherd’s Verses:
A Water Buffalo of Liangshan Has never had nostrils—how could it ever be caught?
If it should attempt to damage another's crops morning or night, A single shout shall cause it to turn its head back.
Turning my head back, I see not a single thing; Spontaneous joy arises, and I am free from sorrow.
From this, I have realized the method of tending the ox: Without selecting fertile fields, one attains freedom.
Chan Master Qichong of Guyin Mountain in Xiangzhou was asked by a monk: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?"
The Master said: "The Fan people wear skins and furs; the Hu people put them on. The student asked: "I do not understand this principle.
What is it? The Master said: "A deaf person leans his ear; a mute person sings."
A monk asked Chan Master Fahui of Guyin Mountain in Xiangzhou: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style do you succeed? The Master said:
"The stone sprout puts forth shoots in the midwinter spring. The monk pressed further: "If that is so, then you are the true son of Huxi.
The Master said: "Do not speak recklessly. The monk asked: "What is the Dharma? The Master said: "Mountains and rivers."
Daji Jin asked, "Is this not the very point where the Master acts for others? The Master said, "Why must it be so?
Chan Master Kaixie Shan Chongmin of Xiangzhou had a monk ask him, "I have heard it said in the teachings: 'It cannot be known by wisdom;
it cannot be recognized by consciousness. What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "A whisk made of tortoise hair is used according to the occasion."
"The rabbit's horns clearly respond to ten thousand occasions. The student said, "I do not yet understand; I beg the Master for a skillful means.
The Master said, "The stone man knows how to sing the song of longevity; the jade maiden can distinguish the eight-character eyebrows.
The student asked, "What is the student’s own self? The Master said, "Ask people everywhere. The student said, "I beg the Master for a skillful means. The Master—
[The Master] said: "What can be done?
Chan Master Huaijian of Jialing Monastery in Xiangzhou had a monk ask him: "There is nothing more perilous than the edge of a sword-blade.
What is the edge of a sword-blade? The Master said: "It is not within your realm. The monk pressed further: "Advancing is it; retreating is it..."
The Master said, "Both are wrong. A monk asked, "What is it like when there is neither advancing nor retreating? The Master shouted.
On the day the summer retreat ended, a monk asked, "In the Western Heaven, a wax man was used as a test.
I wonder, what is used as a test here in this land? The Master said, "The thief’s heart is empty. The monk pressed further, "If that is so, then today is the sixteenth, and tomorrow..."
17. The Master said, "I grant you twenty blows. A questioner asked, "The drum has just finished sounding and the assembly has gathered like clouds;
as a student I have come before you—what is your intention, Master? The Master said, "Eat the blows. The questioner pressed further, "How should a student set foot [in the Way]?
The Master said, "The offense shall not be punished with excessive severity."
Chan Master Shoufang of Guangji Monastery in Dengzhou previously resided at Yanshou Monastery in Tanzhou.
On the day he ascended the hall, a monk asked, "Master, what did you attain that you have now retired? The Master said, "Ever since I bit through the iron pastry."
"Up until now, the five flavors have been complete. A question was asked: "What is the realm of Yan-shou? The Master said:
"The waters of Shu-hu are as clear as a mirror; they reflect the hearts of ten thousand people. He further asked: "Who is the person within that realm? The Master said: [Silence].
Shoufang was forty-nine years old this year. A questioner asked, "How was it before Niutou had seen the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said, "A rooster crowing at dawn with snow upon its head. The questioner followed up, "And how was it after he saw him?

The Master said, "The snow has dispersed, the rooster has flown away, and no trace remains. A questioner asked, "How was it when the ancient mirror had not yet been polished? The Master said, "Its radiance is brilliant."
He (Hè) asked, “After polishing, what is it like? The Master said, “Black as lacquer.
Chan Master Chongbao of Huguo Monastery in Suizhou had a monk ask him: “Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does he succeed?
The Master said, “It beats the sounding drum; it raises the phoenix song. [The monk] asked: “The heavens and the multitudes...”
All living beings receive this power of grace. What is this power of grace? The Master said: "The wind is high, the moon chants.
Chan Master Jiàn of Yúndǐng in Huá’ān Commandery had a monk ask: "Whose song do you sing, Master? Whose lineage of the patriarchal wind do you succeed? The Master said:
"When the stone drum is struck, heaven and earth shake; the wooden man blows the flute amidst the flames. [The monk] asked:
"What is the realm of Yunjing? The Master said, "A thousand-year withered tree puts forth flowers once more; for ten thousand kalpas, Mount Panta remains forever upon the ancient peak.
[The student] asked further, "What is the person within the realm? The Master held up his whisk and said, "Do you see it? The student said, "I see it.
The Master said, "If you see it, you have not reached such an old ground."
A monk asked Chan Master Qi Chuan of Daowu Mountain in Tanzhou: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose lineage of the Dharma wind do you succeed?
The Master said: "On Phoenix Ridge there is no biased melody; today it is transmitted throughout the world. The monk asked: "What is the realm of Daowu?
The Master said: "Ravine flowers hold the jade dew; court fruits fall upon the golden terrace. [The monk] further asked: "How about..."
"What is it that is within this realm? The Master said: "Embracing the brazier while wearing ancient robes; basking in the sun while resting one's head against the mountain root.
Question: "How was it before Niu-tou had seen the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said: "A blue fly on a jade ornament.
He continued: "And after he saw him? The Master said: "Ice within the flames of a red furnace."
A monk asked Chan Master Huiyuan of Guangde Mountain in Xiangzhou, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "A branch of auspicious grass flows to the Eastern Land; its six petals are fragrant throughout ancient and modern times.
The monk asked, "What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas? The Master said, "The stone man strikes the jar, and the wooden man listens. The monk asked, "What is... [the text here is incomplete].
The Zen Master said, "After a long drought, the reeds flower and snow fills the sky. The student asked, "Is it not simply this very thing?
The Master said, "If it were, it would be far too extraordinary."
A monk asked Chan Master Shànlái of Chéngshān in Lǐzhōu, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Three *lǐ* from here to Shímén County.
The monk pressed further, "What is one who is on the Way? The Master said, "Zhāng Sān and Lǐ Sì.
[Another] asked, "What is the meaning of 'a tortoise contained within a cloth bag'? The Master said, "The name of a thousand sages does not [apply]."
[The Master] emerged. How could his entire being be hindered by the triggering of a kōan?
*Tiansheng Guangdeng Lu*, Scroll Twenty-Four; *Tiansheng Guangdeng Lu*, Scroll Twenty-Five. [Song Dynasty Stele Inscription]
Chan Master Zhuanhai of Mount Sizhu in Qizhou ascended the hall and said: "If you wish for immediate resonance, there is only the teaching of non-duality.
How do you explain this principle of non-duality? Indeed, everyone knows it exists, yet for the most part, it does not continue.
How can it be made to continue? After a long silence, he said: "Simply conceal the traces within your own mind; let the words pass."
Floating clouds. Take care. A monk asked, "What is the ancestral style of the ancient Buddhas? The Master said, "The secret deployment of the numinous barrier is unique;
a thousand mechanisms are not alike. On the first day of the New Year, a monk asked, "The times have shifted and the fortunes of the age have changed—everyone knows this."
"How is it when one does not fall into the four seasonal occasions? The Master said: "Throughout kalpas, one is never deluded regarding the affairs of today.
A single wheel rolls through and shatters the four seasonal occasions. The student asked: "And what of the affairs of today? The Master said: "Mist and fog coalesce in the thin air;
rewards are bestowed without partiality once again for another year."
On the day of Master Qingpou’s opening of the hall at Mount Xingyang in Yingzhou, he ascended the seat and said: "The Great Way from the West transcends the hundred negations of principle;
to apply the mind within the confines of words is entirely contrary to the sublime intent. To stop here and not proceed further would be a disservice to the Patriarchs;

how much less need one speak of tedious elaboration—what benefit could it possibly have? Nevertheless, although this is so, matters are never absolute. For now, let us address the gate of proclaiming the Way."
[The Master] said: "A single thread penetrates all people. Everyone, come forward and deliberate. At that time, a monk asked:

"Before Bodhidharma transmitted the seal beneath his heart, and before Śākyamuni untied the pearl within his topknot—if one were to ask about the meaning of the West at such a time, would there still be a 'meaning of the West' or not?
The Master said: "Extraordinary grasses flourish in midwinter; they do not wait for the thunder of the Five Indias. The student said: [I do not understand.]
If one does not come forward to pose this question, how can one discern the pivot of the Dharma King?
The Master said: "A wild goose flying high in the north loses its wings and its body. The student asked: "I know that you have wondrously attained the intent of the Sovereign of Emptiness;

as for the matter at this assembly today, what is it? The Master said: "Vast and boundless, it is not something to be acquired; expansive and open, it turns back toward the ends of the earth. The student pressed further: "Wondrous!"
"How is it when the function is employed? The Master said: "The Imperial Net is layered upon layer without interruption;

its interlacing radiance is arrayed as the pivot before one's eyes. Question: "When the *Bhagavatī* emerges from the sea, heaven and earth tremble. When presented face-to-face, what is the matter? The Master said:
"When the *Garuḍa* spreads its wings, it encompasses the universe. Who among them is the one who puts forth his head? He further asked: "If one suddenly encounters..."
"What about when you emerge? The Master said, "It is like a *tígǒu* bird that has not yet awakened; it is only at the front of the imperial palace that one knows the truth.

The Second Generation Chan Master Rujing of Qishan in Lizhou ascended the hall and said: "Now, wondrous sound must rely upon a wondrous finger.
If one obtains the wondrous finger, the wondrous sound vibrates of itself. All you venerable ones, what is this wondrous sound? Do you understand?
If you do not yet understand, I, Qishan, shall press my finger for you. He then clapped his hands once.
He then returned to his quarters. A monk asked, "What was it like before the Patriarch had not yet arrived? The Master said, "Above is heaven; below is earth.
The monk pressed further, "And what was it like after he had arrived? The Master said, "Below is earth; above is heaven."
Question: "What is it like when a fish has not yet become a dragon? The Master said: "It holds its head high and wears horns. The questioner continued:
"What is it like after it has become a dragon? The Master said: "It leaps and frolics in rivers and lakes."
The Chan Master Baozhao Zhengjue of Chengtian Monastery in Jiangling Prefecture was invited to succeed to the abbacy by Provincial Governor Zhang Qixian.
As soon as the Master ascended the seat, he said: "This seat is high and vast; I cannot ascend it. Nevertheless, 'Each of those great men is just like me.
At that time, a monk asked: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style do you follow?"
The Master said: "To the west of the city of Yunxi, the twin peaks are majestic; by the side of the marshy pond, auspicious vapors disperse.
A monk from Xiangzhou, who was the Sangha Rectifier (Sengzheng), asked: "In the past, at the eastern edge of the city of Jue, the Dharma-eye was entrusted to Kāśyapa.
I wonder, Reverend Sir, whose dharma heir are you? The Master said: "When you arrive in Xiangzhou, do not speak erroneously. The monk pressed further: "If that is so..."
The Master said, "Do not speak in confusion. A monk asked, "What is the pure Dharma-body?
The Master said, "A bird flies beyond the clouds seeking its kin; a fish leaps in the deep pool exhaling azure waves. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "The *svastika* is emblazoned upon his chest. The student said, "I do not understand. I beg the Master for further instruction."
The Master said, "His feet tread upon a thousand wheels. Question: "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "When a fish swims, the water becomes turbid;
when a bird flies, its feathers fall."
The Master ascended the hall. A monk asked, "Is one blow and one shout the Buddha-dharma or not? The Master said, "Where did you get this news?
The monk then shouted. The Master then struck him. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Perfectly identical to the great void. The monk said, "Why is it not..."
The Master said, "What is there not to see?
Chan Master Haosheng of Lingquan Temple on Mount Qingju in Guozhou ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha within the mountains of Qingju?
The Master said, "In looking up, there is no error. The student said, "Why is it that one does not see him?"
The Master said, "Not seeing what? Question: "What is this great matter of causal conditions? The Master said, "A kitchen with five rafters.
Zen Master Juyou of Linxi Mountain Xingjiao Monastery in Yingzhou ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is that which penetrates through?"
[Question on] the Phrase of the Dharma-body. The Master said: "Beside the Stone Bridge at Mount Nanyue. The student asked: "Why do you go about in such a manner?
The Master said: "It is not within your realm. [Question: "What is Chan? The Master said:
"Sleeping in bed after autumn. The student pressed further: "What is the Patriarch? The Master said: "Face-to-face, yet not seen."
Chan Master Dexian of Kaifu Monastery in Jiangling Prefecture ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the mani-jewel?
The Master said, "Blue, yellow, red, and white. The monk asked, "What color does it take on?
The Master said, "I will tell you when it has a color. The monk asked, "Why do you not say? The Master said, "It is not within your realm."
Question: "What is the student's own self? The Master held up one finger.
The monk said, "Is this not it? The Master said, "Wrong."
Chan Master Zhigui of Chongsheng Monastery in Yuanzhou ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "It covers every mountain and every ridge.
The monk said, "Why is it not seen? The Master said, "What is there not to see?
The monk said, "What is one who is on the Way? The Master said, "Coming in thousands, going in tens of thousands. [The monk] asked, "What is..."
Song of Returning to the Homeland. The Master said: "A foreign monk cannot sing it. The student asked:
"Why can he not sing it? The Master said: "Because you are too sharp-witted."
Chan Master Siqing of Yanxi Monastery at Huanglong Mountain in Ezhou ascended the hall.
A monk asked, "Since it is Huanglong, why is it that upon arriving one does not see it? The Master said, "The eyes are not open. The student said, "What is it like after seeing it?
The Master said, "Try to say it yourself. A monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "The single signpost at every five li."
Ten *li* away, at the Yunquan Monastery of Jia Shan in Liuzhou, Chan Master Shengzong ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the true master of Jia Shan?
The Master said, "There is no obstruction. The monk pressed further, "When a student comes here, why does he not see him?"
The Master said, "If you see, then rest. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The spiral topknot towers over a thousand peaks.
Chan Master Wuxian of Zhangfayuan in Jiangling Prefecture ascended the hall. A monk asked, "Since it is 'Zhangfa' (Manifesting the Dharma), what is that which is manifested?"
"What is the Dharma? The Master said, "Every single thing is manifest. The student asked, "Why does the student not see it?
The Master said, "Having eyes, yet as if without them. Question: "What is the newly risen moon?
The Master said, "Crooked head and willow-shaped legs. Question: "What is the path to Bodhi? The Master said, "The green grass flourishes on the South Mountain; the North Ridge..."
Ten thousand pine trees.

At Lingquan Monastery in Jia Shan, Liuzhou, Chan Master Renshou was asked by a monk: "What is the pivotal function of all Buddhas?"

Chan Master Yongchun of Lingquan Monastery in Lizhou ascends the hall. A monk asks: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind do you succeed?
The Master says: "Night travel is not permitted; you must arrive by dawn. The monk asks: "What is the realm of Lingquan? The Master says:
"A thousand rivers flow without ceasing; ten thousand streams vie in clamor. The monk steps forward and asks: "How about this?"

"The bright moon shines upon the shadowless tree; crooked and straight, long and short—none are alike."
When Chan Master Congxiao of Longtan in Tangzhou first opened the hall for teaching, a monk asked:

Yangshan replied, 'From Guangnan. The Abbot said, 'I have heard it said that Guangnan possesses the "Taming Pearl. Is this true? Yangshan replied, 'It is. The Abbot asked, 'What is its shape?
Yangshan replied, 'In the bright moon it is hidden; in the dark moon it appears. The Abbot asked, 'Can you bring it here?'"
Yangshan said, "I have brought it here. Guishan said, "Why do you not present it to this old monk? Yangshan said, "Yesterday I arrived at Mount Mui, and he too asked for this pearl.
I was left with no words to respond and no reason to offer. Guishan said, "This old monk is advanced in years and has not seen Mount Mui.
You are the son of Mount Mui; you are like a tiny gnat living within the eye-lashes of a mosquito."
He built a nest and cried out for injustice at the crossroads. The land was vast and the people few; those who encountered him were rare. The Master took up the case, saying:
"Among the assembly, this is called the 'Story of Presenting the Pearl. But what is the place where the pearl is presented?
Today, I shall provide a commentary for the great assembly: Do not casually stand by the riverbank; take care that cold ashes do not burn you to death."
The Master asked a newly arrived monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk said, "From Dongjing.
The Master said, "In Dongjing there is a person who has no surname and no name; do you recognize him? The monk said, "I do not recognize him.
The Master said, "If that is so, then you have not come from Dongjing. The monk said, "Yes, yes," and then departed. The Master then ordered his attendant...
The Master said, "Just now, when you responded with a 'nyo-ho,' did you accept me, the old monk, or did you reject me? The monk had no reply.
The Master said, "I should have let it pass," and he struck him.

An ancient saying goes: "In my own house, there is a matter of shared wind. Though none comes from a thousand miles away, I am willing to accept him.
What is this matter of shared wind? The Master said, "Who would not be willing? Question: "When the path of the mind has not yet been traversed, what is it like?

The Master said, "What thing is obstructing you? Question: "I have received the teaching that says: 'Prajñā is like a great mass of fire. What is the principle of this? The Master said, "Who would dare to approach it?"
A student asked, "How can one not be attached to even a hair’s breadth? The Master said, "There is not even a hair's breadth upon which you may set foot. A student asked, "What is empty space?
The Master said, "There is no place for you to set your hands or feet. A student asked, "What is the lion’s roar? The Master said, "Do not disturb others."
Question: “The great assembly has gathered and the disciples have taken their seats. From the perspective of the supreme vehicle (*parama-yāna*), we request the Master to proclaim it.
The Master said: “Why did you not ask sooner? The Master then said:

“Venerable elders, as for what I just said to him—‘Why did you not ask sooner’—was it to reproach him for asking late, or was there another principle behind it? Those who have already attained [the truth] testify to one another.”
"Clear! How do you, my junior brothers of later learning, understand this? I urge all of you: you must investigate this with all haste;
time does not wait for man. Master Fayan said: 'Returning, one is not separated by the intermediate state,' yet it was only after twenty years that he knew what was good and what was bad.
Now, seeing him exerting effort in idle matters while paying no attention whatsoever to his own fundamental nature—why is this so?"
Look at what our ancients said: "You all—where do you establish yourselves and find your livelihood throughout the twelve periods of the day?
If you do not investigate in this manner, Venerable One, there is nowhere else for you to apply your calculations;
you will simply say, "Only the Buddha’s Bodhi is the true place of refuge. Now, let me ask you, Venerable One: as for that Buddha’s Bodhi...
"How do you return to the source? Take care. [The Master] ascended the hall.
A monk asked: "You may come within the white clouds; I shall teach you the song of the purple灵芝 (zhī) mushroom. What is the song of the purple灵芝?"
The Master clapped his hands and faced him. He asked, “What is the master’s house style? The Master said, “There is nothing else in the mountains.
He asked, “When there are no clouds ten thousand miles away, what then? The Master said, “From where does this single point arise?
He asked, “When a deaf person listens to the Dharma, what then? The Master said, “There is nothing to be distinguished. He asked, “As for taking... [text fragment]
To offer this body and mind to every dust-mote world is what is called repaying the Buddha’s kindness. [The student asked: “What is the mind that offers to every dust-mote world?
The Master said: “Only then does one repay the Buddha’s kindness. [The student] asked: “What is the Prince’s precious sword? The Master said:

"Not easily seen. [The student] asked: "One may take it up within the sound of the bell; yet when the drum sounds, one immediately falls into inversion. I do not know what the intent of the ancients was.
The Master said: "It is you who are inverted. [The student] asked: "Master, you have carried the patriarchal seal back to Jiangzhe, alone presiding over Mount Taibai by the Qín River.
Today, fortunately, you have ascended the seat of fearlessness; we pray that you will employ skillful means to manifest perfect penetration."
The Master said, "What more can I teach you to say? The Master continued, "Right now, in the presence of all of you, there is truly no place for a word to be uttered.
Why is this so? Because each of you possesses your own fundamental matter, which renders everything else unnecessary.
Observe how our former patriarchs, when they appeared in the world, spent twenty-one days in contemplation."
Regarding such matters, he said: "I would rather not preach the Dharma; I shall quickly enter nirvana. Based on his saying this, infinite gates of expedient means have already been opened.
Why do you not investigate it in this way? People nowadays only desire a profusion of words; this will not suffice for the task.
It merely increases discursive thought and does not lead one into true wisdom. Later, Muzhou [said]:...
Furthermore, as soon as a monk enters the gate, you see a ready-made public case (gong'an) and I would give you thirty blows.
Master Yunmen said, "At such a time, everyone in the entire world must wear a cangue and be bound with chains. All you venerable seniors!
When the ancients spoke thus, what was their intention? How clearly they revealed it!
Now, if you step forward further and chatter on with your mouths, when will you ever attain resonance? [This has been] a long standing; take care.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "Master Quanzhao asks the Master: When the true mind is vast and empty, what is it like?
The Master said, "Your name is Quanzhao. The monk asked, "What is this great matter of causal conditions? The Master said, "It is no small matter."
Question: "When one seeks it but does not find it, what then? The Master said: "What is the use of seeking?
He asked further: "How then can it be found? The Master said: "Since when have you lost it? Question: "When the myriad dharmas do not arise, what then? The Master said:
"From where would the myriad dharmas come to exist? Question: "What is the one dharma? The Master said: "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth."
[The Master] said, "The ground. [The student] asked, "What is the 'tree-stump of Xuansha'? The Master said, "As for the ground, to whom does it belong?
[The student] asked, "I have heard an ancient saying: 'One who does not take the myriad dharmas as a companion. I wonder, who is this person? The Master said, "Who says such a thing?
[The student] asked, "What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas? The Master said, "I certainly will not tell you that it is a wall."
The walls and rubble are it.
The Master ascended the hall and addressed the assembly, saying: "It is fundamentally perfected of itself; there is no need for laborious effort.
Take care. He ascended the hall again. A monk asked: "The World-Honored One arose from samādhi with composure and dignity; I wonder from what samādhi did the Patriarch arise?"

[The student] rose. The Master said, "Thank you for reporting this to me. [The student] asked, "Diligently seeking the accumulation of supreme merit, one’s principle accords with that of the ancients.
I wonder, what was the intent of the ancients? The Master said, "A pine by a mountain stream in a northwest wind. [The student] asked, "I have received the teaching that says:
'Transcending all expedient means, one achieves the Ten Powers. But how can one transcend expedient means? The Master said...
[The Master] said, "Grasp the expedient means. A question was asked: "When words do not touch the tongue, what then? The Master said, "How can you be liberated? A question was asked:
"What did the Buddha say during his forty-nine years of teaching? The Master said, "He spoke of a dream. A question was asked:
"How should one travel through the twelve hours of the day? The Master said, "Do not see that there are twelve hours."

"What is the realm of the meritorious official? The Master said, "I only fear it cannot be painted.
Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Who does not look up to him? Question: "What is the student’s own self? The Master said, "This time, stop asking others.
Question: "The spirit is ever-unclouded; its clarity is always aware. Why is it that the student does not [perceive this]?"

Master Wuzhuo said, "This will make the great assembly laugh to death. A monk asked, "I have heard it said in the teachings that the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas were all exhorted and inspired by Mañjuśrī.
I wonder, who was this Mañjuśrī that exhorted them? The Master said, "Do you recognize Mañjuśrī yet?
The monk replied, "How should one understand this if one has not yet awakened? The Master said, "I told you just now."
"What? [The student] asked. "Before Bodhidharma transmitted the mind, he was already welcomed; before Śākyamuni understood the jewel in his topknot, it was already there.

If one were to ask about the meaning of the 'coming from the West' at such a time, would there still be a 'meaning of coming from the West' or not? The Master said: "Where did you get this news? [The student] asked:
"What is the家风 (family style/tradition) of the meritorious official? The Master said: "How could we dare hope for praise from all quarters?"
[The Master] sighed. A question was asked: "What is the meaning within the secret chamber?
The Master said: "Do not leak the mechanism. Question: "What is the Dharma-gate of the mind-ground? The Master said: "How many people cannot grasp it? Question:
"The old year has already passed and the new year is about to arrive. What is the meaning of non-transmigration? The Master said: "What is the business of the new year?"

Question: What is the original source of Buddha-nature? The Master said: "It requires careful scrutiny. Question: What is the bright moon jewel? The Master said: "How could those who act with haste ever see it? Question: What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas? The Master said: "All living beings sigh that they cannot reach it. Question: The Patriarch was not on either the eastern or western mountain; where has he gone? The Master said: "He has returned to his own home. Question: Where is the place where the Patriarch resides? The Master said: "He is right here before you. Question: How does one enter the gate of the Buddhas and Patriarchs? The Master said: "If you wish to enter, you must first leave behind all traces. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "He came to transmit the Dharma-eye treasury. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s leaving for the East? The Master said: "He went to spread the teaching throughout the world. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s sitting in silence? The Master said: "He was manifesting the Way through non-action. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s speaking of the Dharma? The Master said: "He was responding to the capacity of sentient beings. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s not speaking of the Dharma? The Master said: "He was protecting the true essence of the mind. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s holding up a flower? The Master said: "He was pointing directly at the source. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s smiling? The Master said: "He was revealing the ultimate truth. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s transmitting the robe and bowl? The Master said: "He was entrusting the Dharma to a successor. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s not transmitting the robe and bowl? The Master said: "He was ensuring the Dharma would not be lost. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s ascending the hall? The Master said: "He was addressing the assembly. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s descending from the hall? The Master said: "He was returning to his quarters. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s preaching the Dharma? The Master said: "He was guiding sentient beings according to their needs. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s not preaching the Dharma? The Master said: "He was letting the Dharma speak for itself. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s entering the room? The Master said: "He was attending to the affairs of the monastery. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s not entering the room? The Master said: "He was resting in the state of non-duality. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s eating? The Master said: "He was sustaining his life-force. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s sleeping? The Master said: "He was entering the realm of great stillness. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s walking? The Master said: "He was practicing the Way in daily activity. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s sitting? The Master said: "He was cultivating the mind in meditation. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s standing? The Master said: "He was maintaining mindfulness in every posture. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s lying down? The Master said: "He was returning to the source of rest. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s rising? The Master said: "He was emerging from the state of stillness. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s looking? The Master said: "He was observing the nature of phenomena. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s listening? The Master said: "He was hearing the sound of the Dharma. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s smelling? The Master said: "He was perceiving the fragrance of liberation. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s tasting? The Master said: "He was experiencing the flavor of the Way. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s touching? The Master said: "He was realizing the reality of the body. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s thinking? The Master said: "He was contemplating the ultimate truth. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s not thinking? The Master said: "He was transcending the realm of conceptualization. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s being born? The Master said: "He appeared in response to the world. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s passing away? The Master said: "He returned to the source of non-arising. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s life? The Master said: "It is the manifestation of the eternal Dharma-body. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s death? The Master said: "It is the realization of the unconditioned Nirvana. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s body? The Master said: "It is the formless Dharma-realm. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s mind? The Master said: "It is the luminous, unobstructed wisdom. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s speech? The Master said: "It is the spontaneous expression of the Dharma. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s silence? The Master said: "It is the ineffable truth beyond words. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s action? The Master said: "It is the functioning of the Great Compassion. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s inaction? The Master said: "It is the state of non-activity in the midst of activity. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s virtue? The Master said: "It is the perfection of the six paramitas. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s wisdom? The Master said: "It is the penetration of the ultimate reality. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s liberation? The Master said: "It is the freedom from all attachments. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s enlightenment? The Master said: "It is the awakening to the nature of the mind. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s ignorance? The Master said: "It is the delusion regarding the true self. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s afflictions? The Master said: "They are the illusions of the unreal mind. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s purity? The Master said: "It is the stainlessness of the original nature. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s impurity? The Master said: "It is the defilement of false thoughts. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s good? The Master said: "It is the cultivation of wholesome roots. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s evil? The Master said: "It is the indulgence in unwholesome deeds. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s cause? The Master said: "It is the seeds planted in past lives. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s effect? The Master said: "It is the fruit ripened in the present life. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s condition? The Master said: "It is the external environment that supports existence. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s result? The Master said: "It is the attainment of Buddhahood. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s emptiness? The Master said: "It is the absence of inherent existence. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s form? The Master said: "It is the manifestation of the empty nature. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s perception? The Master said: "It is the discrimination of objects. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s volition? The Master said: "It is the movement of the mind toward objects. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s consciousness? The Master said: "It is the awareness of the six sense-fields. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s aggregates? The Master said: "They are the accumulation of suffering. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s elements? The Master said: "They are the constituents of the physical body. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s sense bases? The Master said: "They are the meeting places of subject and object. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s dependent origination? The Master said
[The student] asked, "Where exactly does it reside? The Master said, "Go find out for yourself. [The student] asked, "What is samādhi everywhere? The Master said, "It is of no use here.
[The student] asked, "Since I have recognized the path of Caoxi, I know that birth and death are not mutually involved.
What is the path of Caoxi? The Master said, "You have not yet even stepped upon it. [The student] asked, "As for opening one's mouth..."
When one cannot attain the Way, what then? The Master said, "It makes people laugh to death. Question: When one comes without bringing a single thing, what then?
The Master said, "How would I dare hope to show it to you? Question: In the past, the Second Patriarch performed three prostrations and remained upright in his place;
what was the meaning of this? The Master said, "I suspect you have not yet attained succession. Question: Regarding the four-way crossroads...

In truth, this thoroughly illuminates both the present and the past, encompassing as many things as there are grains of sand in the Ganges. Sentient and insentient beings alike are entirely empty and quiescent.

Furthermore, fearing that you, O benevolent ones, might not yet believe this, I employ metaphors such as reflections in a mirror or the moon in water. Although I speak thus, there are many who misunderstand.
Now, let me ask you, venerable elders: how many images are there within a mirror? How many moons are there in the water? If...
If the Way departs without form, its radiance remains vividly present. If the Way were to depart with form, it would be like losing one's head while chasing after a shadow.
Setting aside for a moment the questions of existence and non-existence, venerable elders, have you yet recognized the moon in the mirror?

If you have recognized the moon in the mirror, you may freely allow length and shortness to respond as they may, and let curvature and straightness each manifest their own brilliance. If you have not yet recognized the mirror and have not yet clarified the moon, you may be said to be lost among the myriad phenomena.
Moving forward or backward, you encounter obstacles at every turn. At this time, in the midst of the evening, how can you attain peace and happiness?
If you wish to exert less effort now, do you understand? Each of you should turn the light inward and reflect; cease further hesitation. Take care.

This must be attained by one who is truly extraordinary. Suppose one has never possessed the seed-nature (*gotra*) of the Mahāyāna from the outset and their power of faith is slight;

[The Master] had already arrived at the Snow Peak (Xuedou) Dharma-assembly. On this day, high officials attended the gathering and requested him to preach the Dharma.
The Master said, "Keep this well in mind. A question was asked: "What is the realm of Xuedou? The Master said: "In the crevices of stone, a thousand years' snow is hidden;

The monk replied, "In that case, when one sees the moon, one no longer gazes at the finger [pointing to it]. The Master said, "Where have you been for all this time?"
Question: "On this day, as you carry your precious sword, we pray that you will employ skillful means to determine who is the hero and who is the coward.
The Master said: "Prize your head well. The questioner continued: "If it is so, then within the vast expanse of heaven and earth, all heresies are severed and the multitudes are stilled.
The Master said: "You have still not yet prized your life and nature. Question: "The incense smoke in the burner curls and drifts; the assembly of the sea of followers stands in dense rows."
Bian specifically asked about the meaning of the Westward Journey, relying on the Master to point it out for him. The Master said, "Do not seek it to the east.
Bian further said, "If that is so, then the lion’s roar in the Hall of Good Dharma will be heard all at once throughout the great trichiliocosm.
The Master said, "What have you heard?"
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "Master Baima usually says he is 'happy,' yet when ill he says he is 'suffering. What is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "By whom was this established? The Master then said, "Master Baima usually cries out, 'Happy!
Happy! One day, when he fell ill, he cried out, 'Suffering! Suffering! The temple administrator said, 'Master, you were always happy.'"
Now, why does he instead cry out in suffering? Bai Ma said, "Tell me, was it right then, or is it right now?
Later, Chan Master Fayan spoke on his behalf, saying, "At that time, he simply covered his ears and went out. What is the meaning of this? Is it that he approves of him?

"Go out! Now tell me: is this present moment suffering or bliss? Try to determine it for yourself. Take care. [The Master] ascends the hall.

Regarding the Dharma: how do you understand the Real? If you do not understand the Real, it becomes the false, and you will enter onto the path of error.

[Song Dynasty Stele] Master Jiuqu Qingxiang of Hangzhou was surnamed Shen by secular name. He was a native of Qiantang. At the age of six, in his home prefecture...
He entered the monastic order at Mount Longshan Qianfo Temple at the age of eleven. He received full ordination at Mile Temple and began his study of the Vinaya-piṭaka.
At that time, there was a monk named Wenguang, who was renowned for his reputation; he consequently took him as his teacher. Having read through a case once, he could memorize it entirely;

contemporaries remarked that he possessed the eloquence of Avalokiteśvara. One day, he sighed and said: "Regarding the Dharma for transcending the world, I pray that I may encounter a supreme person. Thereupon...
He went directly to the gate of Chan Master Fazong of Mount Tiantai. The Master was eight feet tall, with hands that reached below his knees.
Upon seeing him, Fazong regarded him as extraordinary. A monk then asked, "What is it like at the place where all news and signs are cut off? Fazong replied, "Thank you for pointing it out."
Upon hearing this, the Master attained great enlightenment. Later, when he returned to his native province, the kingdoms of Wu and Yue were flourishing.

They admired the Master’s reputation and constructed the Qianguangwang Chan Monastery within the city, inviting him to reside there. He declined their repeated requests and returned instead to his former dwelling at Jiugqu.
That place bordered a lake; whenever the spring rains made the evenings dark, the croaking of frogs and the chirping of earthworms were quite clamorous.

[The Master] was interrupted. The Master said, "This meditative stillness of mine ought to be pure and quiet. Thereupon, he cut off [the conversation], and from then on, the monks were able to dwell in peace.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Your question comes too late.
The monk asked again, "In the midst of a perilous and evil path, what serves as the bridge and ferry? The Master said, "This very thing serves as the bridge and ferry."
The student asked: "What is this? The Master said: "It strikes right at your nostrils. The student asked:
"Where does one plant the rootless tree? The Master said: "From where did you get that? The student asked: "The garden is profoundly bright;
I ask the Master for a decisive word. The Master said: "A vast lake ten li wide, a single wheel of autumn moon. The student said: "If that is so, then..."
This is the Master’s instruction on the pointing-gesture (mudrā). The Master said: "Dharma-heir Mengzhao meets the pillar.
The Master passed away on the seventh day of the eighth month in the Wuxu year. After his cremation, his relics were collected and a stupa was erected. His secular age was sixty-five;
his monastic seniority was fifty-four.
Chan Master Hongsu of Jiaojisi in Hangzhou was surnamed Cao by birth. He was born in Qiantang in the first year of the Kaiyun era (the Jiachen year) of the Later Jin Emperor Houzhu.
Before he had reached the age of twenty, he petitioned his parents earnestly to allow him to renounce the household life, and they granted his request.

He paid homage to Zen Master Langzhi of Tiantong Temple as his teacher, shaved his head, and received full ordination. He traveled extensively among the lecture halls to investigate the Vinaya in depth.
Later, he visited National Teacher Yao of Mount Tiantai. One day, while performing manual labor to carry firewood, he dropped a bundle;
thereupon, he composed a verse:
"What falls is not another thing; / Laid out horizontally and vertically, it is not dust. / Mountains, rivers, and the great earth—/ The entire body of the Dharma King is revealed.
National Teacher Nanyue approved this. He then returned to his native village at Daci Mountain, where he thatched together grass to build a hermitage. This was during the Dazhong Xiangfu era.
