A Verse for the Old Gardener.
Sprouts do not necessarily grow through bitter striving; why toil so hard without knowing when to cease?
When one’s efforts are exhausted, the garden becomes vast and open; the mountain colors remain ever new while the person turns white-haired.
*Verse on Xuefeng’s Ancient Mirror*
Every person possesses a mirror on their face; what Dharma gate is not fully revealed therein?
The eminent practitioner of the profound mystery is lost in his head; the old woman mending thread suddenly attains enlightenment.
A monk recites a verse on the ancient masters' staff and shout.
The ancient masters’ single blow and single shout encompass the wondrous voices of the sands of the Ganges;
at the point of the shout, one can distinguish the holy from the ordinary, and under the blow, one immediately knows life and death.
The eyes of humanity and heaven are opened wide, and the delusions of past and present are instantly shattered.
At that time, Old Man Deshan directly revealed that there was not even a hair’s breadth of anything further;
the nature of the Dharma-realm is perfectly luminous and manifest— there is no need for forced cultivation, and neither ordinary beings nor sages can increase or diminish it.

Awakening and delusion have no fixed location; one cannot discard them, nor can they be discarded. Even if one were to seek them for hundreds of thousands of millions of Tathāgatas, they would not be found.
Master Cheng entered through this gate and resided there for five years.
He then announced his retirement and dwelt in the upper chamber. On the twentieth day of the third month in the first year of the Qianxing era (Renxu), he passed away.
He sat upright and entered nirvana. His worldly age was seventy-nine, and his monastic seniority was sixty-two.
The local people cremated him with incense and tea, collected his relics, and erected a stupa on the site of his former hermitage.
Chan Master Daoyuan of Chengtian Yongan Temple in Suzhou ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Shoo! You outcaste!
The monk stepped forward and said, "I am a beginner; I beg the Master for a skillful means. The Master asked, "What are you asking?
The student said, "I am asking about the Buddha. The Master said, "Shoo! You outcaste! He spoke thus again.
A monk asked, "What is the principle of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Drawing legs on a snake.
The monk followed up, saying, "Does this also repay the debt of gratitude to the state? The Master said, "Not only do you fail the state, but you also slander me."
Again, a monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Questioners are as numerous as cow-hairs.
The monk pressed, "I ask the Master to answer this question of the cow-hairs. The Master said, "A lion bites a man; it does not chase after clods of earth.
The monk said, "If that is so, then students are acting with haste. The Master said, "In the same field of study, those who are rare are few indeed."
The Disciple asked, "When the lotus has not yet emerged from the water, what is it like? The Master said, "Its fragrance and buds.
The Disciple further asked, "After it has emerged from the water, what is it like? The Master said, "All news is cut off. The Disciple asked, "What is the student's own self?
The Master said, "One cannot find it at the crossroads; one must ask the boatman beneath the pavilion by the river."
The student said, "If that is so, then everything is it. The Master said, "Yaññadatta’s madness was not yet true madness.
The student asked, "I have heard an ancient saying: 'The path beyond is not transmitted by the thousand sages.
What is this path beyond? The Master said, "Panshan was far too indiscreet. The student asked, "I wonder, did the thousand sages still extend their compassion?"
Wu-shi said, "This is not much different from Pan-shan.
Zen Master Xing-ming of Kaihua Temple on Longshan in Hangzhou ascended the seat and said, "Assembly, there is no need to come forward."
If you say that the Buddha-dharma exists here where it has come from, how could it not exist where it has not yet come?
If you say it does not exist, then there is a limitation. If you say it does exist, what is the principle of its existence?

If you realize its essence while it is yet to come, only then will you have a point of understanding upon arriving here. Therefore, the Patriarch said: "Every dharma is originally the Dharma; there is no..."
In the Dharma there is no non-Dharma. Why, within a single dharma, would there be both dharma and non-dharma? The ancient sages attained great enlightenment through the wind and the banner;

some saw their nature beneath a shout, others achieved the Way beneath a staff. In seeing, hearing, knowing, and perceiving; in bowing, looking up, turning, and moving—where is there that is not the appearance of the Buddhas in the world?
When the Patriarch came from the West, he pointed directly to the human mind, so that by seeing one's nature one becomes a Buddha, without using a single [word].
A hair’s breadth of mental effort—why do you not grasp it? And how would you go about grasping it? If you cannot grasp it, it is likewise not due to anyone else.
O assembly, why is this so? The ten realms are continuous; the four modes of birth are vibrant; there is not even a thread or a hair’s breadth of temporary contradiction between them.
Take care! A monk asked: "The Buddhas appear in the world for the sake of all sentient beings. Today, Master, [you act] like..."
The student asked, "What is shown to the assembly? The Master said, "Wait further for the response to the question.

The student said, "If that is so, then the Vulture Peak of old is the Nengren [Temple] of today. The Master said, "This is merely empty talk. A monk asked, "Having already ascended the Dharma seat, I request you to reveal the profound words.
The Master said, "Say what? In the fourth year of the Xianping era, the Master passed away without illness. The monk... [continued].
He was forty-five years old at his parinirvāṇa and seventy years of age at his passing. A stupa was erected for him on the mountain where he resided.

The Master Fêngyīn of Mount Xishan in Hangzhou was a native of Quántán; his secular surname was Lú. He left home to become a monk in his youth and received full ordination upon reaching the age of twenty.
While the Master was seated within his quarters, a monk asked: "The ancients inscribed verses for the quarters of Vimalakīrti—"
"No. "How is the meaning? The Master said, "Try to pose a question. The student said, "That person did not answer. The Master said, "Not answering is actually good. The student bowed.

The Master said, "You have come directly to the quarters of Vimalakīrti. He then composed a verse: The questioner asked, "What is the meaning? I replied, "It cannot be grasped. He said, "Try to pose a question. He did not answer—this is truly excellent. I prostrated myself; Thus I arrived at the hall of Vimalakīrti.
Vimalakīrti’s room of ten feet square was not of lofty dimensions; thirty-two thousand seats were not too narrow.
My present dwelling is far too spacious—it should surely be able to accommodate all you Chan practitioners.
One day, he said to the assembly: "All of you are already pitiable enough by nature; to try to make you believe [this] is already beyond me."
Duan. Why is this so? As Vimalakīrti said: "He has no wound himself; do not inflict one upon him.

On the fifteenth day of the ninth month in the third year of the Tiānshèng era, at the time of the midday meal, the Master sat in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*), formed the Maitreya-seal (*Mithu-yin*), and passed away.
His secular age was eighty, and his monastic seniority (*saṃgha-lak*) was sixty.
Chan Master Chengshi of Qixian Baojue Monastery on Mount Lu ascended the seat. A monk asked, "The imperial canopy has personally arrived before your seat;
we request the Master to employ skillful means to expound the vehicle of the school. The Master said, "Those present in the assembly shall bear witness.
The monk asked, "Today, the sword of wisdom is raised once more; we request the Master to let out a roar to settle who is the male and who is the female. The Master said, "Where is the sword?"
The student said, "In that case, within the vast expanse of heaven and earth, the wind passes through and carries all streams. The Master said, "Wild fox spirit!
The student asked, "Zhaozhou’s Stone Bridge carries donkeys and horses across; as for the Stone Bridge of the Three Gorges, whom does it carry across?
The Master said, "Shrimp and earthworms. The student said, "In that case, the hundred grasses are all bathed in grace."
The Master said, "You do not tread upon it. A question was asked: "What is the realm of Qixian? The Master said, "The clouds part, and all is newly revealed.
He further asked: "Who is within the realm? The Master said, "Having prostrated, withdraw. A question was asked:
"When Sudhana snapped his fingers, the gate of the pavilion opened. I wonder, how is it for you, Master, today? The Master said, "Examine."
Question: “I do not ask about the five elders’ profound and wondrous [encounter]. What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said: “How would you describe it to others? He replied: “In that case, it is entirely due to this question.
The Master said: “What connection is there? Let us stop this questioning for now. If we were to discuss the Buddha-dharma, it certainly would not be like this.”
Fengjing asked: "Right now, each of you says, 'The Elder has opened the hall; we have all come to hear the Dharma. But let me ask you all:
before the Elder had opened the hall, was there still Buddha-dharma? If you say there was not, how could it have reached this day?
Therefore, the former sage said: 'I guarantee this matter for you; it shall never be in vain. And how much more so..."
The Ultimate Way has no gate; those who see it do so in a mere instant. For all to attain it may take ten thousand kalpas in a single moment.

This is certainly not for those of the higher stream alone who can verify it through realization; as for those of middling or inferior capacity, they should provisionally grasp it according to their needs within the gates of expedient means.
Without waiting for the cultivation and verification of accumulated kalpas, they may suddenly transcend the stage of No-more-learning (*aśaikṣa*). What, then, is this "No-more-learning"?
"Study! You must quickly grasp this. I have stood here long enough; take care. Ascending the hall, a monk asked:
"Yesterday, at Xian-dong, you finished your teaching; today, at Xi-xian, you are invited to proclaim it. Master, what will you say tomorrow?
The Master said: "How will you ask then? The monk pressed further: "I do not yet understand how to comprehend this. The Master said: [Silence].
The arrow passed beyond Silla. [A monk] asked, "I have heard it said that you, Master, personally saw Baizhang; is this true? The Master said, "From whom did you hear this?
The monk pressed further, "I do not yet understand what it was like at that time. The Master said, "Just now, there was still a slight margin for improvement."
Question: The dragon has left the azure cave and already entered the clouds and mist. Regarding the supreme vehicle of the ultimate lineage, we request the Master to proclaim it.
The Master said: "Set aside another question and bring one forward. Question: We have received the teaching that says, "The Tathāgata comes from nowhere and goes nowhere;
therefore, he is called the Tathāgata. What is the Tathāgata? The Master said: "When you give alms to the assembly, for what purpose do you do so?"
[The assembly] presented their understanding. The Master spoke again, saying: "When you all gather here at once, you say, 'Let the Elder speak on Chan.
Yet the Elder does not speak of Bodhi and Nirvana, nor of True Suchness (Tathatā) and Liberation (Vimukti). What, then, do you all listen for? Bodhi and Nirvana?"
It is merely the prattle of a dream. These five thousand and forty-eight fascicles were likewise composed in a state of idle leisure.
Now I ask you all: with what do you listen? Do you listen with the body, or do you listen with the mind? Body and mind are each unaware of the other.
How do you all listen? This matter must also be personally witnessed before it can be attained. Therefore, within the skillful means, one must attain understanding according to what is appropriate;
only then will there be a slight degree of resonance. Even regarding the Buddha-dharma, it does not reach the mouth of Baojue (Precious Awakening) for him to speak.
If he were to speak, all people under heaven would be struck dumb by its wind, like iron hammers without holes. [The Master] stood for a long time. "珍" (Zhen—take care).
[The Master] ascends the hall. A monk asks: "The assembly has already gathered at the side of the seat; we pray that the Master will use skillful means to proclaim the Dharma for us.
The Master says: "Look after thirty years have passed. The monk steps forward and says: "In that case, the assembly shall hear what they have never heard before."
The Master said, "The assembly has not yet granted you permission to remain. The student stepped forward and said, "In the future, I shall specialize in being a master of circulation.

The Master said, "There is no need for idle talk. A question was asked: "Regarding the Five Peaks, the Master has finished his chanting; regarding the Three Gorges, something new and marvelous—please, Master, proclaim it!
The Master said, "What is the matter on those peaks? A question was asked: "I have received the teaching that says: 'Stop, stop! Do not speak.'"
"You must speak! My Dharma is subtle and difficult to conceive. "How is this Dharma difficult to conceive? The Master said, "O assembly, listen!
A monk asked, "If that is so, then the assembly has someone to rely upon. The Master said, "That is not your realm.
Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Zhang San and Li Si."
The Master said again: "Before leaving Xianju, I have already met all of you; as soon as I arrive at Shiqiao, I am already repeating the verse.
Now I ask you all: where is the place of meeting? Where is the place of repeating the verse?
Is it at this very moment that we meet? If you understand it in this way, you are tightly bound."
Straw sandals. Do not err in assigning names and phrases; take care. [The Master] ascends the hall. A monk asks:
"The Master has already raised the topic of 'Enlightening the Mind and Benefiting the World with the Sun'; how about 'Precious Awakening Benefiting Beings'? The Master says:
"Try raising 'Enlightening the Mind and Benefiting the World with the Sun' for me. The monk steps forward and says: "In that case, after thirty years..."
"For the sake of circulation. The Master said, "This will leave people utterly bewildered. The student asked, "I do not yet understand; where exactly does the fault lie?
The Master said, "Give me back the head of the dialogue!"
The Master spoke again: "Fortunately, there was nothing to do, yet I have been driven up here by the sound of the drum.
When I say I am visiting the Elder, do I visit him within the Dharma Hall, or do I visit him upon the Dharma Seat?
The Elder has never acted as a counterpart to this monk; this monk must investigate for himself. Therefore, Master Xuansha said: 'I am the same as Śākyamuni.'"
"Understand it thus: the teachers of the ten directions appear all at once before you. If you do not understand it thus, you betray the spirit of a true man.
[He stood for a long time. "Take care."
Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "I have heard the ancients say, 'The triple world is mind-only;
the myriad dharmas are consciousness-only. Are this consciousness and this mind one or two? The Master said: "It lacks what you would say. The monk stepped forward and asked:
"Having received your direct instruction from this point on, what about those who have not yet attained understanding? The Master said: "Go to a quiet place. The Master spoke again: "No..."
He cleared the ground and placed the refuse there, then returned to his quarters.

Upon ascending the hall for the discourse, a monk asked: "This is the place where one selects a Buddha; with an empty mind, one returns having passed the imperial examination. How may a student like me attain such a passing?
The Master said: "I am without talent; I respectfully withdraw. Another asked: "What was the intent behind the ancients' slaying of the snake?"
The Master said, "You still do not know pain or itch. A questioner asked, "This student has long been adrift in the waves of delusion;
I beg the Master to point directly to my original mind. The Master said, "Who would believe you? The student pressed further, "What about one who has not yet attained it?

The Master said, "You yourself carry the shackles and pass through the court of judgment. The student replied, "May the assembly bear witness," and as he stood by the seat, he prostrated himself to thank the Master.
The Master said, "Idle talk. He spoke again, saying, "Nowadays, when monks ask questions, they do so using printed manuals; every one of them is the same.
There is not a single person who asks a question from their own fundamental nature (*bon-bun*). Look at how Zen Master Zhuyou addressed the assembly: 'You people, do not [seek it]...'"
"Driving a stake into empty space. A monk came forward and said, "Empty space is the stake. Zuyou then struck him with his staff.
Tell me, when that monk came out and spoke thus, did he possess the eye of discernment or not?
Zuyou then struck him with his staff; tell me, where did he strike him? Everyone, examine this for yourselves! Take care!
Evening informal discourse in the hall. When the assembly had gathered, the Master said, "I did not meet with you all this morning;
tonight I must not remain silent. He then descended from his seat.

Ascending the hall, a monk asked, “When the Rishi Vyaghrapada took Mañjuśrī’s hand and saw the myriad Buddhas within a single mote of dust, what did he see before he had taken his hand? The Master said, “What do you see now?
A monk asked, “I do not ask about the Stone Bridge of the Three Gorges; what is the Master’s own house style? The Master said, “Why do you not ask?”
Regarding the matter of Shiqiao, the Master further said: "An elder must also not be summoned. If one does not summon him, the monastic community will become desolate.
Yet, if someone suddenly comes forward, you strike them with your staff—how can this be explained? If it were to reward them, what excellence would they have possessed?"
If he is to be punished, where does his fault lie? Is it that as soon as he comes out like this, he is at fault?
If you understand it in this way, you should look into the Buddha-dharma. Be careful.

Ascending the hall, he said: "When one speaks of knowing and seeing, both knowing and seeing are the mind. When the mind is present, it is knowing and seeing; knowing and seeing are right here and now.
This is the verse of the transmission of the Dharma by the Patriarchs. Furthermore, in the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, it is said: "To establish a knowing within knowing and seeing..."
This is precisely the root of ignorance. Furthermore, how can there be superiority or inferiority? Or can there not?

Is it not the case that only those who have long resided in the monastic community as senior monks (*upādhyāya*) are able to discern this? If you are beginners or late learners, do not point east and recognize west. [The Master] stood for a long time.
The Master ascended the hall. A monk asked, "Drops fall from the eaves; the tinkling is just right for listening. When the ancients said 'they have drawn it out,' what sound was it they drew out?
The Master said, "Why do you ask such a question? The monk pressed on, "In that case, one sees the moon and no longer looks at the finger;
having returned home, one stops asking about the journey. The Master said, "That too is forgetting the words. [The monk] asked again.
The warbling of orioles fills the valley, yet the flowers lack fragrance. "What is the place where the student gains strength? The Master said, "Are you afraid that others do not know?
The student further asked, "If so, then everything encountered is true. The Master said, "This too is merely exerting effort in a place of leisure.
The Master spoke again, saying, "Master Fayan said: 'On a clear spring day, the yellow oriole sings; the sun is warm.'"
The breeze is gentle and warm, and the moods of all things are at ease; listen further to the sound of the water falling over the cliff. When did the ancients speak thus?
Was it a word spoken in delusion, or a word spoken in awakening? Try to discern this for yourself. Be careful.

Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "Under the gate of Precious Enlightenment, are there those who have not passed the examination? The Master said: "At the Dragon Gate, there are no guests who remain overnight. The monk asked:
"Now that the drum has just ceased and the assembly has gathered like clouds, we beg the Master to grant us an instruction on the supreme vehicle of the ancestral school.
The Master said: "From where have you come? The monk stepped forward and said: "Those of superior capacity have already understood."
The student asked, "How can those of middling and inferior capacities distinguish [the truth]? The Master said, "You must first examine this closely.
The student asked, "Before Bodhidharma had not yet come to this land, was there already a Patriarch here? The Master said, "Do you even recognize the Patriarch?
The student asked, "I have heard it said in the teachings: 'If one says that the Tathāgata has preached any Dharma, that is to slander the Buddha.'"
"What do you think? The Master said, "You still have not yet attained faith. A question was asked: "An ancient said, 'All things are in flux;
this is the common nature of man. What is the meaning of 'non-transmigration'? The Master said, "The ancients, for the most part, never spoke of it."
Question: I have heard it said in the teachings that "one who does not uphold the precepts is called one who upholds the precepts. What is the intent of this teaching? The Master said:
"First, you must clearly remember this. The student further asked: "In that case, would it mean there is no self-nature? The Master said: "It lacks precisely what you have said."
The Master further said: "One who does not uphold the precepts is called one who upholds the precepts. Is there a precept to be upheld? Or is there no precept to be upheld?

Is this a natural precept (*prakṛti-śīla*) or a prohibitory precept (*pratikṣepaṇa-śīla*)? If this is not clearly understood, one will break them considerably throughout the twelve periods of the day.
Tell me, where exactly is the place of breaking? Those who have left the household life must clarify the Mahāyāna natural precepts. If you can clarify them,"
Mountains, rivers, and the great earth vanish all at once. [The Master] then descended from his seat.

Upon entering the hall for the discourse, a monk asked: "I have received the teaching that says: 'It is fundamentally pure and still. How is it that mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise?"
“I do not yet understand the meaning of this; how should I interpret it? The Master said, “What is it that you doubt? The student asked, “When seeking the Truth, the Truth is not found;
when exhausting delusion, delusion is fundamentally non-existent. When a student intends to rest, will you, Master, permit it or not?
The Master said, “The entire assembly has seen your question. The student pressed further, “Is there anything beyond this? The Master said, “Look closely at what precedes.”
The attendant stepped forward and said, "May the assembly bear witness. The student prostrated. The Master said, "Silla is not yet far away.
The Master ascended the hall and said, "O assembly! The Way of the King is peaceful and secure; one rain, one sun. He then descended from his seat. A monk asked:
"What is this natural matter? The Master said, "I simply keep watching. Question: "By what means did the sages of the past realize [enlightenment]?
The Master said, "By what means have you realized it? Question: "I have heard the former worthies say, 'Only the sage is one who takes all things as himself.
I do not know, however, what constitutes a 'thing'. The Master said, "Is it not clear?"
Jiwei (the sixth day of the sixth month). A student said, “I do not understand. The Master said, “Just now, you were still harboring doubts.
Ascending the hall, he said: “The Buddha-dharma is a matter of no concern. Everyone walks it together; everyone rests within it. Before one’s eyes are forms; before one’s ears are sounds.
The wondrous meaning of all Buddhas is clearly realized right here. Even if one must travel a thousand or ten thousand miles, one should return to the hall to find rest.”
Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "The assembly has already gathered before your seat; I beg the Master for a single phrase to point toward the source.
The Master said: "Take this clearly to heart. The monk continued: "If it is so, then seeing forms will not give rise to deluded attachment;
it is transparently one's own treasure from the very beginning. The Master said: "Do not be superficial. A monk asked: "Not coming from the prior limit, not going to the posterior..."
[The student] asked, "When the limit does not depart, what then? The Master said, "What is the matter with the middle?

[The student] further asked, "In that case, it is born right where it is and extinguished wherever it is. The Master said, "There is still a lack of observation. [The student] asked, "The Mind was enlightened in the past;
today is the Sun of Wisdom. I wonder, are these one or two? The Master said, "The assembly must examine this closely."
The student stepped forward and said, "If that is so, then as soon as a single word accords with the Way, there is neither a second nor a third.
The Master said, "That is just how you understand it."
The Master spoke again: "He asked, 'In the past, it was Mind-Seeing; today, it is Sun of Wisdom. Here, I would say to him:
'Great assembly, listen closely! Now tell me, is there a point of entrustment, or is there no point of entrustment?

As for such a question—when seeing Mind-Seeing come, and when seeing Sun of Wisdom come—is it still something that can be verified? It is not that he does not ask about this or that; it is simply so.'"
[The Master] sat. "If you do not ask, Huiri’s mouth will be like a wooden beam or a rafter. If the Senior Monk does ask Huiri, he will be left speechless, staring at the wind.
Discern this with the eye of clarity. If you have not yet attained such clarity, do not merely listen for sounds and echoes. Take care."
Ascending the hall, he remained silent for a long while, then said: "Fortunately, there is this plate of rice; one must not forcibly add pepper and ginger to it.
Even so, try tasting it for yourselves. Be careful."
One day, he addressed the assembly, saying: "The skull is ever present within the world; the nose remains as the family tradition of touch and friction.
When the ancients spoke thus, it was most intimate and essential. Nevertheless, you must still examine this closely. Consider this: how far apart are Mount Sumeru and the nostrils?
Try to investigate and deliberate upon this. He remained standing for a long time.
On the day Master Dexing of Wanshousi in Suzhou opened the hall for his formal inauguration, after the incense had been offered, he said:
"The celestial mechanism of leaving the world—who understands it thoroughly? If you have not yet realized it, wait a moment longer. He then ascended the seat. At that time, a monk asked:
"With the monastic community surrounding the seat and the imperial officials present at the assembly, what is the first phrase of Wanshou? The Master—
The Master said, "It is already too late for the beginning. The student said, "If that is so, then the Patriarchal Edict has received the Master’s intent;
the distant regions shall all be able to proclaim it. The Master said, "What did I just say to you? A student asked, "What is the house style of Wanshou?
The Master said, "It will make the whole world laugh to death. The student said, "If that is so, then I have received the Master’s [instruction]."
[This is] an indication. The Master said, "It is no longer necessary. The student asked, "The patriarchs have transmitted one to another the seal of the patriarchs;
whom do you, Master, now take as your Dharma heir? The Master said, "Is this not a transmission in vain?

The student said, "If that is so, then in the past Baizhang received the direct transmission, and today Wanshou acts for the sake of the deluded masses. The Master said, "How can you understand it in such a way?"

[The Master] said, “I have. A questioner asked, “The fourfold assembly has all gathered at this seat. I wonder, Master, whose dharma do you now succeed? The Master said, “There are many people; I do not know them.
The student said, “If that is so, then Baizhang’s single melody is being sung by the Master now; I, your disciple, shall specifically receive it to propagate it.
The Master said, “How could you, a student, possibly manage that? A questioner asked, “The high officials and ministers have all arrived.”
"In this seat, what Dharma will the Master employ to repay your kindness? The Master said, "I thank you for sharing my concerns. Question: "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "The assembly gazes upon him all at once. Question: "What is the one phrase by which the Master benefits others?
The Master said, "You must benefit yourself first. Question: "In the kingdom of Magadha, he personally issued this decree."
"What is this command? The Master said, "It is practiced throughout the world. Question: "What is the realm of Wanshou? The Master said, "Today you see it all.
The student said, "In that case, I have personally received your instruction. The Master said, "How do you understand the realm? Question:
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, [silence].
"Exhausting the Way, he returned to the Western Heaven. The student said, "In that case, one has met the Master. The Master said, "Who has met him?
The Master then said, "Question and answer are both complete; who has grasped the meaning? If you seek it from another, it becomes a mere fabrication.
For a long time I have dwelt in the deep mountains to hide my ineptitude; I never expected to arrive at Wanshou today."
"Under the Gate: It may be said that it cannot be hidden. Since it cannot be hidden, it is clearly revealed.
I do not know which of you has seen it first. If there is such a place of seeing, come forth before the assembly and disclose the news.
After a long silence, the assembly remained speechless. The Master said, "I have stood for a long time. Take care."
Chan Master Yongxi Yong of Yunmen in Yuezhou ascended the hall. A monk asked, "The dragons and elephants of the four seas are all here;
please proclaim the one phrase of the Western Come. The Master said, "The assembly shall bear witness. The student said, "The profound mechanism is lofty and steep;
it is difficult for those with limited conditions to comprehend. I beg you again for your compassion to serve as a guide. The Master said, "Compassion is for those who do not understand."
Question: "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said: "Thank you for your inspection. Question:
"In the past at Vulture Peak, the Dragon Girl offered a pearl and attained Buddhahood. When a student has no pearl to offer, what then?
The Master said: "Do not deceive the assembly. Question: "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said: "This meaning is not—"
Xiaowen asked, "How was it before the lion had emerged from its cave? The Master said, "Do not roar for now.
The student asked, "How was it after he emerged from the cave? The Master said, "Step back. A student asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "You do not understand what that meaning is. The student asked, "What is the meaning of his coming from the West?"
The Master said, "I thank you for grasping the meaning of my words. He then asked, "As for what I just said to you—that you do not understand—what was the intent?
Was it to reprimand you, or was it because there was nothing to respond to? How do you understand this?"
"If you have not yet understood, come again tomorrow to ask. Take care. [The Master] ascends the hall. A monk asks:
"The patriarchs have transmitted to one another the seal of the patriarchs; to whom do you, Master, now succeed as a Dharma heir? The Master says:

"Thank you for your thorough understanding. A monk asks: "At the head of Daixiong Ridge you personally received the essential meaning; by the banks of the Ruoshai Creek you pointed out the way for those lost."

"This is the realm of Mount Ling. The Master said, "Where is there not enough to contemplate? Once, seeing a monk reading a sutra, the Master asked the monk, "What sutra are you reading? The monk was speechless. Thereupon, the Master composed this verse: The mountain peak is high and steep; The path is difficult to traverse.

If you wish to see the Buddha, Look at the mountain flowers. If you wish to hear the Dharma, Listen to the valley streams. If you can understand this, You will know the meaning of the sutras. If you cannot understand this, You will be lost in the words.
To read the scriptures without understanding them is but a vain labor that damages the eyes; if you wish not to harm your vision,
clearly discern the verse on the emptiness of form.
Within the majestic form, there is no mark of emptiness; In the brilliant void, all forms and shapes are severed.
Directly beneath, form and emptiness are neither one nor two; The name "form" has never been my name from the start.
Master Xuanshun of Lingyinshan in Hangzhou was a native of Xiaoshan. His secular surname was Qian. In his youth, he entered the monastic life at Fushan...
Chan Master Liaowu of Zhizhiti Mountain in the prefecture received the full precepts upon leaving the household life. Later, he entered Mount Yandang in Wenzhou and established a hermitage there.
Subsequently, he resided at Lingyin Monastery in Hangzhou. Upon departing from Mount Yandang, the Master composed a verse:
Wandering freely and chanting idly down from the emerald peaks, there is not a single dharma left to contemplate.
When someone asks me the meaning of my departure from the mountains, I carry a tattered cassock upon the head of my cane staff as I return to Mount Tiantzhu.
"In every matter I am incapable; not one thing can I do. I joyfully return to India to spend my remaining years.
Hungry I eat, weary I sleep; there is nothing else to do. Do not speak of another heaven within a flask.
Later, during the Xiangfu era, the Master again spoke a verse:
When born, who comes? When dead, who departs? Birth, death, coming, and going—these are ordinary matters in a realm of many illusions.
Like a flash of lightning, so it is in all places; I too am thus, fundamentally beyond words.
I now speak these words by force of circumstance: please proceed with the cremation immediately; do not delay.
When the Master had finished speaking, he sat upright and passed away. His monastic age was fifty, and his secular age was seventy.
Chan Master Wenhàn of Yongxī Temple on Mount Zhītí in Fúzhōu was a native of Míngzhōu.
He left the household life under Chan Master Liǎowù at Jìngdé Temple on Mount Línyǐn in Hángzhōu, where he also received the seal of mind. When the Master ascended the seat, he said: "The Great..."

"Assembly, if this mountain monk did not reveal such a sharp point of spiritual resonance (*jīfēng*), would there still be the principle of continuing the Buddhadharma and turning the wheel of Dharma for the ancestors?
If you say there is no such principle, then the pure and wondrous wheel of Dharma of the Buddhas of the three periods would become a mere cessation;
thus, there would be times when it turns and times when it does not. Great assembly, if you say there is the principle that the wheel of Dharma constantly turns..."
"Why does a false mountain monk like me ascend this seat today to turn this wheel of Dharma? It would be like having two heads and three faces. Why is it so?
Consider, for instance, how throughout the worlds of the ten directions, the four seasons revolve, the eight nodes of time shift, all phenomena are generated, and the sun and moon shine;
even down to the blowing of the wind, the moistening of the rain, the heat of fire, and the cold of ice—the Triple World is vast."
Cotton. The four modes of birth are vast and expansive. Are they worldly dharmas? Are they conditioned dharmas or unconditioned dharmas?
Are they the dharma of the wheel-turning monarch? Is it possible to discern them? If you have not yet been able to discern them, this mountain monk dares to resolve your doubts.
At that time, a monk asked: "The clouds of Yao and the sun of Shun represent a spring-like radiance; how does the ancestral wind compare to the national wind?"
The Master said, "It may be said that you have come to this inquiry. The student said, "All beings among devas, humans, and the various classes of living things all receive the power of this grace.
The Master said, "Do not yet fixate on a definitive conclusion. [The student] asked, "Reclining high amidst the mists and clouds, you conceal the profound intent."

Cultivating the mind, the wisdom of cessation is like cold ashes. This morning, having already responded to the invitation of all sentient beings, may the opportunity at Shaoshi Mountain be granted directly.

The Master said, "Do not engage in such conceptualization. A monk asked, "Compassionate clouds universally moisten the three thousand worlds;
I hope the Master will bestow a single phrase for the benefit of others. The Master said, "Why are you dozing off? The monk [remained silent].
He then drew a circle and presented it to the Master. The Master said, "Do not be so strange. The student asked, "When such a device is employed, how do you respond? The Master struck him.
Chan Master Congjin of Bore Monastery on Mount Tiantai in Taizhou ascended the hall. A monk asked, "Before the Buddha appeared in the world, was there still the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "There was. The monk asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma before the Buddha appeared in the world?
The Master said, "It is that which you are asking about. The monk said, "If it already exists, then what further use is the Buddha?"
"What do you do by appearing in the world? The Master said, "Do not act like an unfilial son.
A questioner asked, "I have heard that the former worthies said, 'The principle of pure emptiness ultimately has no body. I do not yet understand the meaning of this.
The Master said, "It is very much like nailing a stake into empty space. The questioner pressed, "If empty space is the stake, what then? The Master said, "Good medicine is only..."
To save those who possess life, the Master then addressed the assembly, saying: "For those of later generations and beginners, there is no hindrance to asking here and there.
If, suddenly, beneath a single word or half a phrase, you attain a point of illumination, you will not have brought shame upon your renunciation and travels. The ancients were also like this."
In this regard, some may stop as soon as they encounter a single word or half a phrase; others may cease upon striking or bumping against something.
Although this is so, such persons are still not yet true "Great Men" (*mahāsattva*).

Even if one does not attain realization through a single word or half a phrase, it is not necessarily the case that one is not a Great Man. Why? Because realizing the Way prior to words is not yet thorough penetration.

People: "To apply a phrase according to the occasion is still not the work of a realized one. Likewise, to speak of embodying the Way before words is not yet the mark of a person of thorough penetration.
To apply a phrase after the occasion is also not the work of a realized one. How, then, can one attain the state of being exactly right?
This is called a distinct chant within the mystery, a lofty discourse beyond the ordinary. It requires such a person to engage in such a matter. If you have not yet—
"You are such a person. It would be better for you to first seek a point of understanding within the provisional expedients.
Take care. A monk asked, "The Buddhas appear in the world for the sake of one great cause; for what purpose do you, Master, now appear in the world?
The Master said, "Wait until the time I actually appear in the world, and I will tell you. A monk asked, "Regarding the cold spring water of the ancient ravine..."
"How so? The Master said, "Above all, do not drink it. The student asked, "What of those who drink? The Master said, "They lose their very life.
A questioner asked, "When there is not a single blade of grass for ten thousand miles, where does one release the white ox?

The Master said, "That 'not a single blade of grass for ten thousand miles' is not yet the place to release the ox. The student pressed further, "I do not yet know, then, what place is the place to release the ox?"
The Master said, "Go ask the stone person. [The monk] asked, "I, this student, have not yet attained realization of my own mind, nor do I clearly understand all phenomena (*dharmas*).

I beg the Master for a skillful means to point out the way through the mazes of delusion. The Master said, "Let us set aside your 'own mind' for a moment. Pointing to what, then, would you call 'all phenomena'?
[The monk] pressed on, saying, "In that case, then mind and phenomena are non-dual, are they not? The Master said, "Three, four, five. [The monk] asked, "Why?"
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Another flower blooms. The student said, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "When the fruit ripens, it is naturally formed. Question: "The blind men touching the elephant each describe a different aspect.
What is the true elephant? The Master said, "Open your eyes and look! The student said, "In that case, I have seen it."
"It is the true reality. The Master said, "You are still groping about in confusion. Question: "What is the dragon in the pool of Longji?
The Master said, "He is not within the blue waves. Questioner: "I do not know where he then resides. The Master said: [He is]... (not present).
"It has returned to the depths of the pond.
The Master said further, "He asked about the dragon in the pond of Longji; I told him it was not within the blue waves. But tell me, where is it?
Do you see? Venerable ones, if one were a person who recognizes the dragon, they would set their mind at rest upon seeing it for the first time."
Take heed. The Verse on Manifesting the Way states:
The Way is fundamentally beyond words; how marvelous, its profound vastness! It acts as the bellows for heaven and earth, encompassing all households.
Born within the human relations, its application is most extensive; yet it is called rootless and should not be said to have form.
Like the moon at the bottom of a pond or an echo in the mountain valleys, what we call "true" or "empty" are all but false conceptions.
*Verse on All Dharmas Abiding in Their Respective Positions:*
All phenomena abide in their respective positions; this is called the meaning of reality. What is the meaning of reality?
It is the absence of self and the absence of what belongs to a self. Since that which belongs to a self does not exist, one is far removed from both existence and non-existence;
thereby, seeing and hearing are cut off. The eye-element and ear-element differ from the forms, images, sounds, and voices.
The dharma-realm is primordially complete; Objects and self are utterly distinct.
The Lion’s true play—this wandering monk has once stood in the snow before the ancestral hall; His staff flies on, seeking nothing more; A single phrase is clearly understood.
Wandering freely in all directions, I gazed upon the distant waters at Lake Dongting;
Passing through Mount Lu during the waning autumn, When people asked about the matter of forgetting artifice, I spoke only of reaching the Nine Provinces.
A Herdsman’s Eulogy.
A fat, white ox climbs upon its horns; Riding through the water village at dawn, the mist is thin.
The green grass fills the fields as it grazes at leisure; Singing along with the spring breeze, those who join in harmony are rare.
— A Fisherman’s Eulogy.
Worldly affairs, as numerous as hemp seeds, do not entangle him; He dwells in carefree ease, right there amidst the waters and sky.
Having attained his golden scales, he forgets to cast his line; Upon a light single-leaf boat, he watches the moon and sleeps.

The questioner pressed, "What about right now? The Master said, "What is there right now? The Master further said, "In my school, there are no words."

Chan Master Haichan of Fazhi Chan Monastery in Zhangzhou was surnamed Chen by birth and was a native of Quanzhou.

In his youth, while traveling on pilgrimage, he met Chan Master Mingxi of Ximing in Quanzhou; they reached a mutual accord in a single word. Subsequently, he resided at Fazhi Chan Monastery in Zhangzhou.
The Master ascended the seat and said: "At the assembly on Vulture Peak, among hundreds of billions of beings, there was but one person, Kāśyapa alone, who heard [the Buddha's teachings] directly.
Today’s assembly is no different from that on Vulture Peak. Tell me, is there anyone here who has heard them directly?
If there is one who has heard them directly, they can continue the Buddha’s life-span and cause the Dharma to abide for a long time, serving as a vessel for the sea of suffering."
The sun and moon in the dark alleys of ignorance—if you have not been able to hear them directly, how are you any different from the assembly that withdrew from their seats at that time?
As for "hearing" and "not hearing," how do you understand this? Is it heard by the ear, or is it seen by the eye?
If it is heard by the ear, who is it that hears? If it is seen by the eye, what is it that sees? Why do you not investigate in this manner?
"Is there anyone among you who has a question? Come forward and speak. At that time, a monk asked: "When a secular ruler appears in the world, the four seas are cleared and pacified.
I wonder, when the Dharma King appears in the world, what means of salvation does he provide? The Master said: "How do you understand the appearance of a secular ruler?
The monk stepped forward and said: "When the Dharma King appears in the world, he has no other business; his Way accords with that of the ruler."
The Emperor praised the Great Peace. The Master said, "Do not take this as mere lip service. Question:
"If one relies on wordlessness, there would be no teaching from the World-Honored One; yet if one relies on speech, it fears leaking the secret of the Patriarch’s coming from the West.
Apart from these two paths, what is your intention, Master? The Master said, "It is all just you speaking like this. Question: "Regarding Yuntai and Yanqing..."

“I have already heard your instructions for dispelling delusion. Today, in this city of Zhangzhou, I hope you will deign to guide me. The Master said, “Try to cite the examples of Yuntai and Yanqing for me.
The student replied, “Is there not a skillful means here in this city of Zhangzhou today? The Master said, “Was it not just now that I was questioning you?
The student replied, “Delusions from both places return to the level path; the single jewel-moon rises once more in its brilliance.”
The Master said, "What words are these?
He ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas? The Master said, "It is simply right now.
The Master continued, "The Buddhas of the three periods and the six generations of patriarchs have never for a moment been separated from you; they are not otherwise."
He bestows his benevolent grace, lifting us up from the left and supporting us from the right. It is unlikely that you, O Benevolent One, would not rely upon and practice this.
How could one possibly contravene such grace? It is like the sun rising over Fusang in Jambudvīpa:

all sentient and insentient beings throughout the great earth receive its radiance, and every kind of activity they undertake exists entirely within that light and shadow. Thus it was with the ancients.

It is said: "Like fish in water, like birds flying through the air—even when they raise their fins and wag their tails, or ascend from below—once they have attained liberation from the nature of moisture and the substance of emptiness, [what remains] is non-existent.
If one were to leave behind the nature of moisture and the substance of emptiness, where would one find a place to settle the body and establish one's life?
Why not investigate this in such a manner? Those who recognize gratitude are few; those who betray it are many. I pay homage.
He exhorted the Elder: "For now, know how to be grateful; take care.
A monk asked, "I have heard the Master say that one should simply stop speaking directly. This was said after the Patriarchs arrived;
I do not yet understand what 'stopping directly' means in the present day. Where, then, is the point of 'after the Patriarchs arrived'? The Master said, "The Elder does not understand the Way."
Xiantuode asked, "If it is so, then one has personally seen the Patriarch. The Master said, "The assembly sees you all clearly.
He asked, "Before the Patriarch had yet arrived, who knew this Way? The Master said, "You do not believe the Way.
He asked, "Ordinary people and sages have never been different; there is not even a hair's breadth of discrepancy. The Master said, "Stop."

"It is so. [The student] asked, "I have heard it said in the teachings that 'seeing and hearing constitute the seeds,' whereby one transcends the eight difficulties and surpasses the stages of the ten bhūmis.

[The student] further asked, "What does it mean to transcend the eight difficulties and surpass the stages of the ten bhūmis? The Master said, "How did you understand it just now?"

The monk pressed further, "How is it that all dharmas remain unmoving and are all identical to the signless?"
The Master said, "It is you yourself who have failed. [The student] asked, "I have heard of the flowers of the five petals at Shaoshi;
today I listen to the principle of the One Vehicle. What is this principle of the One Vehicle? The Master said, "How do you listen?
[The student] stepped forward and said, "In that case, there is neither two nor three. The Master said, "Who would dare believe you? [The student] stepped forward and said, [silently].
