The Master said: "The Official has not invited me in vain. The student said: "If that is so, then the Official bears witness.
I, this student, offer my thanks. The Master said: "Do not mock the Official. A questioner asked: "The patriarchs have transmitted it from one to another..."
"The ancestral seal has been transmitted through successive generations. Whom have you now received as a Dharma heir? The Master said, "I fear the assembly does not know.
[The questioner] asked, "To speak of the ultimate truth is to oppose the mundane; to conform to the mundane is to deviate from the truth. How do you instruct people, Master? The Master said:
"You must not forget this kindness. The student said, "If I do not inquire further, how can I understand the Master's pivotal point?
The Master said, "You have grown full in the monastic groves. The student asked, "The Dharma is not hidden in every phenomenon; it has been constantly manifest throughout the ages.
What is this manifest Dharma? The Master said, "I am showing it to the assembly. The student said, "If that is so, then I, your student, shall respectfully withdraw."
The Master said: "One who recognizes their transgressions must certainly reform them.
There was the Chan Master Baoyue Zhong of Longhua Mountain Baocheng Temple in Hangzhou, a native of Yongjia. His surname was Zheng.
He left home and received full ordination at Kaiyuan Temple in his home prefecture, and subsequently went to the Dharma seat of Chan Master Yunju Qi. Yun...
Ji asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "I have come from Zhejiang. Ji said, "What kind of thing is it that comes like this?
As the Master was about to respond, Ji said, "Dull-witted teacher! Go and join the assembly.
From this point on, the Master set his mind at rest and remained in robes for several years. At the beginning of the Xiangfu era, he resided at Fayu Monastery in Hangzhou. At Tian...
In his saintly year, the abbot Li Ji invited him to reside at the Longhua Monastery.
On the day the Master opened the hall for formal teaching, a monk asked, "Yesterday was Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa; today is the rain of Dharma. I wonder, are these one or two?
The Master said, "You must examine this more closely. The monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Who does not look up to him?"
Question: "What is the meaning of [the Master’s] coming from the West? The Master said: "How many people have ever asked this?
While the Master was residing at Longhua, he ascended the hall. A monk asked: "The sovereign is enlightened; the ministers are virtuous.
As you ascend the precious seat, how do you discourse on the Way? The Master said: "How do you understand this? The student said: "In that case, it is one..."
It is said that returning lies in having the Way; the myriad phenomena emerge from the mindless. The Master said, "If you understand it in this way, how can you succeed?
On the day the Chan Master Yiyuan of Baoben Chan Monastery in Huzhou opened the hall for the assembly, the Prefect and the great multitude had already gathered.

After the Master had finished offering incense, a monk asked: "The morning assembly has commenced and the ancestral wind is fanning once more; we pray that the Master will proclaim the supreme vehicle of the lineage.
The Master said: "The Provincial Governor shall bear witness. The student said: "If that is so, then as soon as the single sound is struck, the fourfold assembly shall all hear it.
The Master said: "As for the matter of hearing—how is it? [The monk] asked: "The Master ascends the precious throne..."

The assembly gathered like clouds. [A student] asked: "Regarding the supreme vehicle (zōngchéng) from above, how do you instruct us? The Master said: "If you go to various places, take care not to misrepresent it.
[The student] further asked: "In that case, I shall accept and practice it accordingly. The Master said: "How will you accept and practice it? The student said:
"The scriptures of the Three Vehicles are expedient means for the present age. Bodhidharma came from the West to suppress them..."
[This is] a seal of approval. The Master said, "I do not yet believe you. [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "There is still more to the dialogue."
Chan Master Huizhen of Yunju Mountain in Nankang Prefecture ascended the hall for a discourse. A monk asked, "At the assembly on Vulture Peak, Kāśyapa heard it personally.
At this day’s assembly, who is it that hears? The Master said, "You, *ācārya*, are quite alert.
The monk said, "I do not yet understand how to realize this. The Master said, "I take it you are sharp-witted. A monk asked, "Before the ancient mirror..."
[The student] asked, "What is it like when it is being polished? The Master said, "How can its radiance be divided? [The student] asked, "What is it like after it has been polished?
The Master said, "Everyone sees it together. A question was asked: "The sound of the drum has just ceased, and the assembly has all gathered.
Please grant us a word for the sake of others. The Master said, "It is difficult to find one who is sharp-witted. [The student] said, "In that case, there are [beings] among humans and devas."
Master Lai said, "Idle talk. Question: "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "The great meaning is just this. Question:
"When the Dragon Girl offered her pearl and attained Buddhahood, we students have no pearl to offer;
can we still attain Buddhahood? The Master said, "Without a pearl, how could you attain Buddhahood? The student said, "If that is so,"
"The student has no share in it. The Master said, "Do not understand it in that way. The student asked, "I do not know what your meaning is, Master.
The Master said, "Wait until you have attained awakening, and then I will tell you. The Master further said, "In general, the Buddha-dharma must have a point of revelation;
only then is it effective. If there is no point of revelation, even if one were to ask a thousand questions or ten thousand questions,"
It is merely following words and chasing phrases; there is not a single point of realization, and you are thus expending your efforts in vain. I exhort all of you:
first investigate thoroughly to find a place of awakening. Be careful.
On the day Chan Master Zhen opened the hall at Ganlu Chan Monastery in Runzhou, a monk asked: "In the past, the Brahma King invited the Buddha for the sake of all living beings;
for what purpose does the Prefectural Governor invite the Master? The Master said: "Tell me, for what purpose? The monk asked: "The holy teachings say:
'Strike the bell to announce to the four quarters; we pray that the Master will preach the Dharma. The Master said: [Silence].
"You say that the great assembly does not know," the student said. "If that is so, then the gate of ambrosia universally moistens all living beings.
The Master said, "You must still be careful. The student asked, "At the assembly on Vulture Peak, Kāśyapa personally heard [the teaching].
At this day’s assembly, who is it that hears it? The Master said, "When will you arrive at Vulture Peak? The student said, "If that is so..."
"Ma" is the great assembly listening closely to the lion’s roar. The Master said, "Do not speak in confusion. A questioner asked, "I have heard an ancient saying:
'Light does not illuminate the object; the object, moreover, does not exist. When light and object are both forgotten, what is it that remains?
The Master said, "How would I dare provide another interpretation? The student said, "Is there no skillful means? The Master said, "It is not that there is nothing for those who understand."
Language. Question: It has been said of old, "Within the Vairocana-treasury there is a great scripture scroll"—I do not ask about that;
what is the Vairocana-treasury? The Master said: "The entire assembly sees it. Question: What is the house style of the Ambrosia?
The Master said: "All things are seen. The student further asked: "In this way, the enlightened ruler bestows his sagely grace upon the West."
The Patriarch’s turning [of the Dharma] is fragrant. The Master said: "You must not misunderstand this. A question was asked:
"When birth and death arrive, how can one avoid them? The Master said: "What is birth and death?"

The Master ascended the hall and said: "The Buddha-dharma does not require all this. When the Patriarch came from the West, he directly revealed the profound essence, establishing for all people a shortcut for entry.
He had them take up the ancient Buddhas right where they stand. Now, you have already taken your stand."
Now tell me, where is the Ancient Buddha? Do you all see him? If you have a point of realization, then you are a fellow student of Sudhana;
there is no need to leap over all the stages at the entrance of the pavilion, nor need you defer to being a mere fragment of any of the sages.
I grant him precedence, yet this is not enough. Since such a style exists, I ask you all to take it up and continue it. Relying on—
And so he acted accordingly. He stood for a long time. "Take care.
Master Da of Huiri Monastery on Mount Lu ascended the hall. A monk asked: "The Master has left Xiushui and arrived at Xianju."
"How is it with the Venerable Acala? The Master said, "From where have you come? [The student] asked, "The Arhat speaks thus;
Baojue speaks thus. I wonder how Huirui speaks? The Master said, "What would you do otherwise?
[The student] asked, "When Mazu ascended the seat, Baizhang rolled up the mat. What was the meaning of this?"
The Master said, "It is difficult to find a person of keen intelligence. The student said, "In that case, the Master shall return to his quarters, and the assembly shall return to the hall.
The Master said, "How do you understand this? The student bowed. The Master said, "Do not be superficial.
The Master spoke again, "When Mazu ascended the hall, Baizhang rolled up the sitting mat. If one were a true monk, he would have acted accordingly."
Knowing the proper time, he did not weary himself by standing long.
He ascended the hall. A monk asked, "The green vines and yellow creepers climb straight to the summit of the cold pine; the white clouds, pale and limpid, appear and disappear within the great void.
As a student who has come before you, I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said, "This is not your realm."

The student said, “I have not yet understood. I beg the Master for a skillful means. The Master said, “I did not deceive you just now. [The student] asked, “What is the household style of the Immortals?
The Master said, “How does it compare to those of other quarters? [The student] asked, “What is Śākyamuni’s precious sword?
The Master said, “It is not only able to crush the minds of non-Buddhists; it has also once caused the courage of the celestial Māras to fall away.”

Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "Before the patriarchs and Buddhas appeared in the world, was there still the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "When did the patriarchs and Buddhas appear in the world?
The monk pressed further, "If that is so, then they have not left Tuṣita Heaven, yet they have already descended to Jambudvīpa."
He did not cross the Yangtze River, but resided at Shaoshi. The Master said, "That is how you understand it. A question was asked:
"What is it like when 'once attained, forever attained'? The Master said, "What is the thing that you have attained?
The monk stepped forward and said, "In that case, it is like a crane beyond the clouds in the blue sky, standing alone upon a ten-thousand-year-old pine. The Master said, "I do not yet believe you."
A question was asked: "The Patriarch came from the West to point directly to the human mind, to see one's nature and become a Buddha.
I wonder, what is the meaning of this? The Master said: "Do you believe it? Question: "All people know when flowers bloom and fall;
but as autumn passes and winter comes, what is the matter? The Master said: "What is the matter that is known? He stepped forward and said: "If it is so..."
"Those who come and go grow old themselves, while the moon of the past and present remains ever new. The Master said, "What connection is there?
The Master spoke again: "The Patriarch came from the West to transmit the mind-seal outside the teachings, pointing directly at the human mind so that one may see one's nature and become a Buddha.
You venerable ones, there is no need for further repetition. Take care!"

The Master ascended the hall and said: "The true essence of the teaching in this land is pure in hearing sounds. According to capacities, he established transformations; responding to things, he applied his actions.
The ancients selected a single gate, desiring that people might easily understand and easily enter. For instance, at the assembly on the Śūraṅgama Sūtra..."
The various great sages each recounted their own accounts of awakening; how could it be that they were ignorant?
Their purpose was to ensure that future generations would follow from this point onward. Such inconceivable matters are manifested through many paths, yet none deviate from the single principle.

O Venerable Elders, this matter does not depend on extensive learning, memorization, or broad erudition regarding the past and present. One must personally realize and understand it for oneself, and then each practice accordingly. Do not...
After standing for a long time in fatigue, Master Jusu of Baofu on Mount Daimei in Mingzhou ascended the hall. A monk asked, "At the assembly on Vulture Peak, Kāśyapa heard it personally;
at this day’s assembly, who hears it? The Master said, "It is the matter that Kāśyapa heard."
Masheng advanced and said, "Is it not the case that today this question is not asked in vain? The Master said, "Just now I thought so.
Masheng said, "If that is so, then the Vulture Peak of old is today’s Meifeng. The Master said, "..."
"Let us stop for now. [The student] asked: "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said: "I do not avoid being criticized. [The student] asked:
"When the oyster contains the pearl but it has not yet been split open, what is it like? The Master said: "Thank you for showing me this. [The student] asked:
"One who wishes to enter the sea of non-action must board the Prajñā boat. What is the Prajñā boat? The Master said: "Have you reached the shore yet?"
Question: I have heard it said in the past: "Without giving rise to even a hair’s breadth of a mind for cultivation and study, one is eternally sovereign within the light of formlessness.

I do not yet understand how this principle functions. The Master said: "That would merely result in further exertion of effort. The student asked again: "I beg the Master to grant me another expedient means.
The Master said: "How about asking as the ancients did? Question: 'One is all. What is this 'one'?"
The Master said, "The incense altar; the dew-pillar. [The student] asked, "What can be done about the incense altar and the dew-pillar?
The Master said, "I knew well that you could do nothing about them. [The student] asked, "The Buddha’s true Dharma-body is like empty space.
Now that empty space is manifest before us—why do we not see the Buddha? The Master said, "It is because you have good eyes. [The student] asked, "What is the Way?"
The Master said, "Go ask the mountain pressing against the gate. The student advanced and asked, "Is this very thing it?
The Master said, "It turns out you do not know how to ask. [The student] asked, "When one speaks of knowing and seeing, both knowing and seeing are the mind.
I do not ask about knowing and seeing; what is the mind? The Master said, "This question is inappropriate. Daowu asked, "Why?"
The Master said: "It is because you lack true knowledge and insight.

He ascended the hall and said: "If you simply do not follow after the twelve categories of conditioned phenomena—such as movement and stillness, union and separation, tranquility and change, penetration and obstruction, birth and death, light and darkness—and instead pluck out one root, you will detach from clinging and return inwardly to the source; thus you shall return to the primordial truth."
The fundamental luminosity is activated; this luminous nature brings forth manifestation. All other five types of clinging should be uprooted for perfect liberation.

This knowing and seeing does not arise from external objects; luminosity does not follow the sense organs, yet it relies upon the organs to manifest. Thus, the six sense faculties function interchangeably for one another.
Venerable Elders, this is the pointing-out instruction of the Tathāgata from the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*.
That people today do not understand it is because they perceive external phenomena and internal mind as distinct, with subject and object racing against one another, thus wandering in saṃsāra.
Originally there was but a single luminous intelligence, which divided into six harmonious functions; when one function is stilled, the other six cease to operate. It is further said: "One..."
When the faculties have returned to their source, the six sense organs achieve liberation. It is simply by returning to the source that this is attained.

Once the source has been returned to, then the eyes may engage with forms, the ears with sounds, the nose with fragrances, the tongue with flavors, the body with tactile sensations, and the mind with mental objects.
Thus, one thoroughly understands according to conditions and acts freely and spontaneously according to one's nature, attaining non-obstruction. However...
"It is well understood in this way. [The Master] stood for a long time. "Take care. A monk asked, "What is the matter before the Buddha appeared in the world?
The Master said, "Everyone wants to know. [The monk] further asked, "What is the matter after he appeared in the world? The Master said:
Wait for another time to come, and I shall tell you.
Chan Master Chang, the Dharma-heir of Baoshou of Mount Qinghua in Yuezhou, was surnamed Zhu and was a native of Suzhou.
He left home and received full ordination at Kaiyuan Temple in his own prefecture. He went to Yunju Mountain and attained awakening. During the Xiangfu era, in Yuezhou... [Qinghua...]

Huashan invited the Master to appear in the world. On the day the Master opened the hall, the Rector struck the gavel and said: "In this Dharma assembly, you, the assembly of dragons and elephants, should contemplate the primary principle. The Master said: "To contemplate in this way is called right contemplation; to contemplate otherwise is not to see the Buddha. Now, let me ask: [The Master] asked: "What is the primary principle? The Rector replied: "It is the Great Way. The Master said: "If it were the Great Way, it would not be the primary principle. If it were the primary principle, it would not be the Great Way. Why? Because the primary principle has no name, and the Great Way has no form. Since there is neither name nor form, how can you say it is the Great Way? Furthermore, since there is no name, how can you call it the primary principle? You have just now said, 'In this Dharma assembly, you, the assembly of dragons and elephants, should contemplate the primary principle. Now tell me, what is the primary principle? The Rector was speechless. The Master said: "The primary principle is not something that can be grasped by the mind or intellect. It is only when one transcends the mind and intellect that one can see the Buddha. Therefore, the *Vimalakīrti Sūtra* says: 'If one contemplates in this way, it is called right contemplation; if one contemplates otherwise, it is not seeing the Buddha. The Master then asked: "Do you understand? The Rector replied: "I do not understand. The Master said: "If you had understood, you would not have been speechless. Since you are speechless, you have already seen the Buddha. Why? Because the Buddha is not something that can be sought through words and phrases. He is only to be realized within one's own mind. Do you understand? The Rector bowed and withdrew. The Master said: "This is truly the primary principle. The assembly was greatly enlightened. Thus, it is said: "When the wind blows, the grass bends. The Master then descended from the seat. The Rector struck the gavel once more and said: "The assembly has heard the Dharma; let us respectfully take our leave. The Master said: "Take care on the road. The assembly departed. The Master remained seated for a moment, then rose and left. The Rector followed him and said: "Just now, when you said, 'If one contemplates in this way, it is called right contemplation,' I did not understand. Please, Master, explain it further. The Master said: "If you had understood, you would not have asked again. Since you have asked again, you have not yet understood. Why? Because the primary principle is not something that can be explained. It is only when one attains it within oneself that one knows it. Do you understand? The Rector bowed and withdrew. The Master returned to the abbot’s quarters. The assembly gathered once more. The Rector struck the gavel and said: "The assembly has heard the Dharma; let us respectfully take our leave. The Master said: "Take care on the road. The assembly departed. The Master remained seated for a moment, then rose and left. The Rector followed him and said: "Just now, when you said, 'If one contemplates in this way, it is called right contemplation,' I still do not understand. Please, Master, explain it further. The Master said: "If you had understood, you would not have asked again. Since you have asked again, you have not yet understood. Why? Because the primary principle is not something that can be explained. It is only when one attains it within oneself that one knows it. Do you understand? The Rector bowed and withdrew. The Master returned to the abbot’s quarters. The assembly gathered once more. The Rector struck the gavel and said: "The assembly has heard the Dharma; let us respectfully take our leave. The Master said: "Take care on the road. The assembly departed. The Master remained seated for a moment, then rose and left. The Rector followed him and said: "Just now, when you said, 'If one contemplates in this way, it is called right contemplation,' I am finally beginning to understand. The Master said: "If you had understood before, you would not have said you were finally beginning to understand. Since you say you are finally beginning to understand, you have not yet understood. Why? Because the primary principle is not something that can be attained through gradual cultivation. It is only when one suddenly breaks through the barriers of the mind that one realizes it. Do you understand? The Rector bowed and withdrew. The Master returned to the abbot’s quarters. The assembly gathered once more. The Rector struck the gavel and said: "The assembly has heard the Dharma; let us respectfully take our leave. The Master said: "Take care on the road. The assembly departed. The Master remained seated for a moment, then rose and left. The Rector followed him and said: "Just now, when you said, 'If one contemplates in this way, it is called right contemplation,' I have finally attained realization. The Master said: "If you had attained realization before, you would not have said you had finally attained realization. Since you say you have finally attained realization, you have not yet attained realization. Why? Because the primary principle is not something that can be attained through effort. It is only when one lets go of all effort and returns to the source that one realizes it. Do you understand? The Rector bowed and withdrew. The Master returned to the abbot’s quarters. The assembly gathered once more. The Rector struck the gavel and said: "The assembly has heard the Dharma; let us respectfully take our leave. The Master said: "Take care on the road. The assembly departed. The Master remained seated for a moment, then rose and left. The Rector followed him and said: "Just now, when you said, 'If one contemplates in this way, it is called right contemplation,' I have finally reached the ultimate understanding. The Master said: "If you had reached the ultimate understanding before, you would not have said you had finally reached the ultimate understanding. Since you say you have finally reached the ultimate understanding, you have not yet reached the ultimate understanding. Why? Because the primary principle is not something that can be reached through conceptualization. It is only when one transcends all conceptualization and returns to the state of non-duality that one realizes it. Do you understand? The Rector bowed and withdrew. The Master returned to the abbot’s quarters. The assembly gathered once more. The Rector struck the gavel and said: "The assembly has heard the Dharma; let us respectfully take our leave. The Master said: "Take care on the road. The assembly departed. The Master remained seated for a moment, then rose and left. The Rector followed him and said: "Just now, when you said, 'If one contemplates in this way, it is called right contemplation,' I have finally attained the great liberation. The Master said: "If you had attained the great liberation before, you would not have said you had finally attained the great liberation. Since you say you have finally attained the great liberation, you have not yet attained the great liberation. Why? Because the primary principle is not something that can be liberated through effort. It is only when one lets go of all effort and returns to the state of total freedom that one realizes it. Do you understand? The Rector bowed and withdrew. The Master returned to the abbot’s quarters. The assembly gathered once more. The Rector struck the gavel and said: "The assembly has heard the Dharma; let us respectfully take our leave. The Master said: "Take care on the road. The assembly departed. The Master remained seated for a moment, then rose and left. The Rector followed him and said: "Just now, when you said, 'If one contemplates in this way, it is called right contemplation,' I have finally attained the great enlightenment. The Master said: "If you had attained the great enlightenment before, you would not have said you had finally attained the great enlightenment. Since you say you have finally attained the great enlightenment, you have not yet attained the great enlightenment. Why? Because the primary principle is not something that can be enlightened through thought. It is only when one transcends all thought and returns to the state of original purity that one realizes it. Do you understand? The Rector bowed and withdrew. The Master returned to the abbot’s quarters. The assembly gathered once more. The Rector struck the gavel and said: "The assembly has heard the Dharma; let us respectfully take our leave. The Master said: "Take care on the road. The assembly departed. The Master remained seated for a moment, then rose and left. The Rector followed him and said: "Just now, when you said, 'If one contemplates in this way, it is called right contemplation,' I have finally attained the great awakening. The Master said: "If you had attained the great awakening before, you would not have said you had finally attained the great awakening. Since you say you have finally attained the great awakening, you have not yet attained the great awakening. Why? Because the primary principle is not something that can be awakened to through practice. It is only when one lets go of all practice and returns to the state of non-action that one realizes it. Do you understand? The Rector bowed and withdrew. The Master returned to the abbot’s quarters. The assembly
"Everyone, can you still understand and observe in this way? If you cannot yet do so, ask your questions if you have doubts.
At that time, a monk asked: "It has been a long while since we heard the lion’s roar; I pray the Master will let out a single peal of thunderous sound.
The Master said: "Where have you come from? The monk asked: "The great bell is struck and the Dharma drum is heard afar; what is the meaning of this for the Master?"
"A single phrase for people. The Master said, "It is transmitted from one to another for the sake of circulation. A question was asked:

"When Subhūti proclaimed 'non-speaking' to manifest the Way, Śakra and Brahmā ceased their listening and rained down flowers. I wonder, who today is the one who hears? The Master said, "There is only a lack of raining down flowers.
Later, while residing at Guangfayan Monastery in Hangzhou, the Master passed away without illness. [The funeral rites were performed.]
His descendants collected his relics and erected a stupa at his home mountain. His secular age was fifty-two, and his monastic seniority was forty-five.
At Xiansheng Temple in Quzhou, Master Juyao ascended the hall. A monk asked: "The patriarchs have transmitted one to another the seal of the patriarchs."
"Whom have you now received as your Dharma heir? The Master said, "Before the great assembly of humans and devas.
The questioner said, "If that is so, then Yunju’s single arrow today has struck Sangu. The Master said, "I knew you would understand it in this way."
Question: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "The successive patriarchs have answered this without ceasing.
Question: "Heaven attains the One and becomes clear; Earth attains the One and becomes tranquil. How is it when the Master attains the One?"
The Master said, "What do you say about heaven and earth? The student asked, "Is there still a portion for benefiting people?
The Master said, "The assembly will laugh at you. The student asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "I have always been just like this."

On the day Chan Master Shanneng of Xinghua Temple in Tanzhou opened the hall for formal teaching, a monk asked: "The great assembly has gathered like clouds; we pray that the Master will proclaim the Dharma of our school.
The Master said, "A fine question—go ahead and ask. The monk stepped forward and said, "In that case, I shall not have disappointed the Master.
The Master said, "Do not exert effort. Another monk asked, "Having long dwelt at the Dragon Gate, how can one attain realization? The Master said, [silently].
"You are fortunately a guest of the Dragon Gate. Question: "What is the matter that is the student's deepest depth?
The Master said: "I grant you one move. Question: "What is the realm of Xinghua? The Master said:
"Beholding it is never enough. He further asked: "What is the person within the realm? The Master said: "Have you seen him yet? Question: "As for such..."
"What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Your question is not right. The student advanced and said, "I, your disciple, do not understand;
I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said, "For now, just pay your respects. Ascending the hall, he said: "O Great Assembly!
To utter a single word of essential principle is already prolixity. Nevertheless, do not misunderstand. [I have] stood long enough. Take care."
Chan Master Qing of Mount Qingxi in Jingmen Commandery ascended the hall. A monk asked, "How does one reveal oneself so as to be in accord with the Way?

The Master said, "When have you ever revealed yourself? That is precisely what is not in accord with the Way. The monk asked, "What is the wondrous power of wisdom of Avalokiteśvara? The Master said, "It is that which can save the world from suffering. The monk asked, "What is the Patriarch?

The Master said, "It is that which can save the world from suffering. (Note: This repetition of the previous answer is characteristic of the *wenda* style, where the response may be a pivot to redirect the inquiry.)
The Master said, "Go ask the pillar. The student asked, "What is the meaning of the pillar? The Master said, "What did I just tell you?
A student asked, "The ancient road is level and wide; how does one tread upon it? The Master said, "You are a wandering monk.
A student asked, "When the mind is unmoving, what then? The Master said, "You dull-witted fellow!"
A monk stepped forward and said, "In that case, I shall pay my respects to express gratitude for the Master’s kindness. The Master said, "Do not be so crude.

The Master ascended the hall and said, "Those of you with a beginner's mind who have not yet understood—try to understand! If you do understand, you will neither destroy the mundane world nor depart from it. All you venerable seniors!"

if one observes through another, it is called wrong observation. Someone asked a question, requesting instruction. At that time, a monk asked:

"If it is so, then the fine horse does not move its hoof. The Master said: "Where is the gold? A monk asked:
"When a wild wind suddenly arises and sweeps away the mist and clouds, why is it that a student like me cannot understand upon reaching this point?
The Master said: "Truly you do not understand. The monk pressed further: "If one does not probe the dragon’s neck, how can one obtain the black pearl? The Master said: "Where is the pearl?"
[The Master was] at the dwelling. A questioner asked: "What was it like before Bodhidharma had yet arrived? The Master said: "The path across the suspension bridge is perilous;

few can cross it. The questioner followed up: "And what was it like after he arrived? The Master said: "He sat idly at Shaolin for more than nine years. Question: "What was it like before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said: "Sugarcane stalks ripen in winter from the south. The questioner followed up: "And after he saw him? The Master said: [Silence].
"How is it? The Master said, "To the north, peaches are suitable for summer. [The student] asked, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world?
The Master said, "Several layers of white clouds. [The student] further asked, "How was it after he appeared in the world?

"A person on the Way. The Master said, "A dry piece of excrement. Question: "The Master has personally sung the melody of Caoxi; I wonder how one may harmonize with it in unison?
The Master said: "Try and say it yourself. [The student] stepped forward and said: "If that is so, then I thank you for raising the song. The Master said:

[The monk] asked three times, "Why do I not see the National Teacher? The Master said, "Look beneath your heels. [The monk] further asked, "How can I come to see him?
The Master said, "The sole of your straw sandals is torn. [The monk] asked, "What was it like before you had seen Master Xiian?
The Master said, "In spring, it is very cold. [The monk] further asked, "What is it like after you have seen him? The Master said, "Autumn has passed."

You will attain liberation wherever you are, and its application will manifest before you. Heaven and earth share the same root; the myriad things are one body. This is called the "eye of the patch-robed monk."

When Zen Master Zhisheng of Shengshou Monastery in Wujiang, Suzhou, first opened the hall, a monk asked:
"I know that you have long been fermenting grape wine; today, for whom do you open this compassionate aid? The Master said, "I suspect you do not yet know."
Zizhi asked, "If that is so, then the *udumbara* flower has been dissected, the Dharma-realm is fragrant, the Buddha-sun has first opened, and the dark alleys are forever illuminated.
The Master said, "There is no need for such effort. He asked, "Since you have ascended the precious throne this day..."
"Please, Master, proclaim a single phrase of our family tradition. The Master said, "Can you verify it?
The student said, "If so, then humans and devas will have their reliance, and the fourfold assembly will all rejoice. The Master said, "Idle words. Question:

"The Master has responded to the collective aspiration to propagate the ancestral Way. I do not yet know from which direction the ancestral Way descends. The Master said, "Only those of the same Way know it."
The student said, “If that is so, then in the past at Jinli you personally received the essential meaning, and today at Songjiang you deliver it to the deluded masses.

The Master said, “That, however, is not my way. A questioner asked, “When the fourfold assembly gathers before the dais on this day, for whom do you proclaim the decisive resolution of the profound mechanism?
The Master said, “You are not without sharp intelligence. The student stepped forward and said, “If that is so, then it is not only...”
The great assembly and the court officials were graced with his favor. The Master said, "Do not speak in such confusion. Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "Beyond the reach of praise by gods and men. The Master further said, "If one speaks of the Buddha-dharma, what else is there? Therefore it is said:
the mountains and rivers of past and present, the sun and moon of past and present, the human relations of past and present, and the cities of past and present."
Guo: "This is called the Dharma-gate of Equality, which transcends the limits of past and future. Can you all believe this?
If you can believe it, practice accordingly. [He stood for a long time. Take care."
On the day Chan Master Shouru of Kaishua Monastery on Mount Gongchen in Lin’an County, Hangzhou, first opened the hall for teaching, a monk asked:
"Since the high officials have extended their three requests, what Dharma will the Master employ to repay their profound kindness? The Master said: "Why do you ask so specifically? The monk asked:
"What is the single phrase by which the Master benefits people as a 'Merit-Maker' (Gongchen)? The Master said: "It has been so from the start."
[The Master] never buried anyone. [A student] asked: "I have heard it said in the teachings that 'it is originally pure and still.
How is it that all of a sudden mountains, rivers, and the great earth arise? The Master said: "Tell me, who brought this about? The student replied:

"If that is so, then there are green mountains before one's eyes with not a single tree; the eye can reach to the emerald waters where there is no ripple. The Master said: "This too is a misunderstanding."
Question: "What is the realm of the meritorious official? The Master said: "The Senior Monk ought to possess the eye of one who has traveled the pilgrimage routes.
He further asked: "In that case, Mount Emei freezes with snow a thousand fathoms deep; the back of the giant turtle towers high, enshrouded in five-colored smoke.
The Master said: "There is no connection. Question: "The drum sounds roar with power as the clouds gather; please, Master, proclaim the single phrase that benefits people. The Master said: [Silence].
[The Master] said, "You must also exert yourself further before you can succeed. [The student] stepped forward and said, "If the student merely acts in this way, what is your meaning, Master?
The Master said, "I thought you understood my meaning. The Master spoke again: "At dawn, there is one bowl of gruel."
"Everyone already knows the time. Now there is no further need for this mountain monk to give instructions; 'go drink tea,' he said, and then descended from his seat.
Entering the hall, he said: 'O Great Assembly, do you know that the Holy Monk has come here together with all of you?'"
Since you have condescended to honor us with your visit despite our fatigue, how could we dare detain you for long? Please take care.
Master Huiming of Lingyin Temple in Jingde, Hangzhou, was originally from Yunchang. His secular surname was Zhang.
At the age of thirteen, he left the household life; at twenty, he received full ordination; and at twenty-three, he began his travels to visit various masters.
In the second year of the Jingde era, while traveling in Qiantang, he eventually hung up his staff at Lingyin Temple. His predecessor as abbot was the Great Master Wen-sheng of Ciji.
One day, he addressed the assembly, saying: "Looking out with your eyes, what do you see? Upon merely hearing this, there was awakening. He then composed a verse, which says:
Looking out with my eyes, what do I behold? Mist and wind; layered peaks of emerald majesty.
"If one understands that one's own mind is not the myriad dharmas," the Patriarch—who said he came from the West?
In the second year of the Tianxi era, Lord of the Prefecture, Marshal Ma, requested him to open the hall. He ascended the seat. The *vinaya-dhara* struck the mallet and said:
"O assembly of dragons and elephants at this Dharma feast, you should contemplate the primary truth. The Master said: "Have you been able to contemplate it yet? And how so?"

[The Master] looked. Did he look toward where he had just come from, toward the place where he was ascending the seat? Or did he look toward the place where the *weina* (ritual master) strikes the mallet?
If you look in such a manner, there is no connection [to the truth]. At that time, a monk asked: "In the past, the Brahma King invited the Buddha to expound the Three Vehicles.
Today, the Minister invites the Master; what Dharma should you preach? The Master said: "How is today like the past?"
At that time, Jin said, "In that case, humans and devas have something to rely upon. The Master said, "Rely on what?

Jin asked, "The patriarchs have transmitted from one to another the seal of the patriarchs; under whom did you, Master, now receive the Dharma as a successor? The Master said, "Even you cannot verify this.
Jin said, "In that case, Lingyin has received the essential meaning, and you, Master, are his grandson. The Master said, "..."

"Do not speak in confusion. The student asked, "I have heard from the memorial and correspondence of the Senior Secretariat that you said, 'The yellow chrysanthemums and green bamboos should be cut down;
one must point directly to True Suchness. As a student who has come here, I beg the Master to point directly to it. The Master said, "The Senior Secretariat has spoken for you, Venerable.
The student pressed further, "If that is so, then Zhaozhou’s cypress tree is understood by everyone, and Lingyin’s yellow chrysanthemums are in bloom everywhere."
The Master said, "You have not yet repaid the kindness of the Minister. A question was asked: "What is the realm of Lingyin? The Master said, "Observe it as you please.
He further asked: "What is the person within the realm? The Master said, "How do you understand the realm? A question was asked:
"Without involving existence or non-existence, I ask the Master to speak. The Master said, "Your words have fallen into error."
Question: "What is the Way? The Master said: "Is the Way far away? Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "Majestic and dignified. Question:
"What is the gate through which Avalokiteśvara enters into principle? The Master said: "I have also realized it from within this.
Question: "I have heard an ancient saying: 'It is not the wind that moves; it is not the banner that moves. I do not yet understand [this]."
"What is the principle here? The Master said, "Have you even managed to come to rest? A question was asked: "The student has already traversed the double barrier of light and darkness;
I pray the Master will grant me his reception. The Master said, "Why such exertion? A question was asked: "What is the white ox on the open ground? The Master said, "Its horns are very distinct.

A question was asked: "What is the single path of true correctness? The Master said, "Its horns are very distinct. (Note: The Master's response repeats the previous answer as a conventional pedagogical device).
The Master said, "Not even a hair’s breadth can pass through. The student asked, "If that is so, then shall I act in accordance with this?

The Master said, "Do not run about recklessly. A question was asked: "What is it like when the mountains and peaks are without deficiency? The Master said, "White clouds lie across the mouth of the cave."
Ascending the hall, he said: "I offer you, venerable elder, a single thread of the Way. But how do you go about discussing the Buddha-dharma?
If it were as impenetrable as water being blocked from leaking through, there would be no place for you, venerable elder, to establish yourself or sustain your life.
At such a time, even if the Patriarchs and Buddhas were to appear, they too would receive twenty blows. Having spoken thus, does this mountain monk have any fault? Have you not seen?"
Master Yunmen said: "When the World-Honored One was born, he walked seven steps, looked around in the four directions, pointed one finger at heaven and one finger at the earth, and declared:
'Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored. Had I seen him then, I would have struck him dead with a single blow and fed him to a dog.
Why do I say this? It is because he sought to achieve peace throughout the world. But tell me, what about Yunmen?"
When the Master speaks in this manner, does it possess the principles of the Buddha-dharma or not? Even so, Yunmen possesses only one eye.
[The assembly] has stood for a long time. Take care.
In autumn, he addressed the assembly:
The autumn wind is desolate as yellow leaves wither; In many places, the sound of the laundry mallets rings out keenly.
This is the gate of entry into the principle of perfect realization— Where else could I be asked to explain it again?
Dwelling in the mountains, I cherish solitude; dwelling in the mountains, I alone preserve my simplicity. As white clouds come and go, how could they ever be distant?
Sometimes, after tea, I depart into the forest; following where my feet lead, my steps are never in vain.
The second couplet:
I love dwelling in the mountains, embracing their solitude; How could it compare to the clamor of worldly affairs?
The pine gate stands alone amidst mist and clouds; Only those who arrive know the path is not far.
On the day Chan Master Guize of Jianfu Monastery in Changzhou ascended the hall, a monk asked: "I request a word from the Master to enable this student to realize the source.
The Master said, "You are a wandering monk. The monk pressed further: "What about one who has not yet realized it?
The Master said, "Who is it that has not yet realized it? A monk asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?"

The Master said, "The sound of the bell strikes from the eastern side. [The student] asked, "I know that you have already sung the song of the Hu family; I wonder, whose lineage of the ancestral wind do you succeed?
The Master said, "Who does not know the lineage of the ancestral wind? [The student] further asked, "I have already received the Master’s performance of the single song;
how is it when the student claps his hands? The Master said, "You are not yet one who knows the music."
On the day of the opening of the hall by Chan Master Huizhong of Xuanhua Monastery at He Mountain in Huzhou, the Rector struck the gavel and said:

"In this Dharma assembly, you dragon-like and elephant-like multitudes should contemplate the primary truth. The Master said: "It lies solely in clear contemplation; there is no need to seek it elsewhere."
"So it is. Having thus announced it, he proceeded to repeat the verse. According to what the *vinaya-dhara* (ritual master) had just reported, everyone should have dispersed;

yet since they have not dispersed, you may ask about matters as you wish. At that time, a monk asked: "When a Buddha appears in the world, the heavens rain four kinds of flowers and the earth shakes in six ways.
When the Master appears in the world, what auspicious signs are there? The Master said: "There are none more than these."

[The Master] intended to rain down flowers. Jìn said, "If that is so, then the assembly shall receive your grace; this student bows in thanks. The Master said, "I, however, thank you. A question was asked:
"The *utpala* flower is easy to see, but a true spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*) is difficult to encounter. This student has no question to ask."
He requested [an answer], but the Master did not respond. The student said, "Do not deceive the Great Elephant. He pressed further, asking, "Is there anything beyond this?
The Master said, "What do you call 'anything beyond'? [The student] asked, "What is the realm of this mountain?
The Master said, "When the rain falls, the mountain colors darken; when the clouds emerge from the cave, it is bright. He pressed further, saying, "Today I have personally attained it."
[The monk] said, "It is for sightseeing. The Master said, "What do you see? [The monk] asked, "When the Buddhas appear in the world, they turn the Great Dharma Wheel.
When the Master appears in the world, how do you benefit people? The Master said, "Where have you seen the Buddhas appear in the world?
[The monk] further said, "Is there anything extraordinary about it? The Master said, "Do not speak in your sleep. [The monk] asked, "The Patriarchal wind has spread far and wide..."
[The monk] asked, "What is it like when one is in a state of total dissolution? The Master said, "You are a wandering monk.
Daitō Zenji (Master Huīduān) of Lìfēngshān Tàishǒu Chányuàn in Hangzhou was originally surnamed Lǚ. He was a native of Wúxī County in Chángzhōu.
He left home and received full ordination under Chán Master Wùchéng of Longhuá Monastery in Hangzhou, and he attained the Dharma from [his master].

The Master never traveled elsewhere again. When the Master first ascended the seat, a monk asked: "The *udumbara* flower has withered and all have understood; how is it when the Patriarch’s command is personally enacted?
The Master said: "One who knows the Dharma is afraid. The monk pressed further: "In that case, there is a basis for its implementation.
The Master said: "A small person with a large heart. The monk asked: "I have heard that you, Reverend, saw [the Buddha] face-to-face."
“Longhua,” [the student] asked. The Master said, “I have heard someone say this. [The student] advanced and said, “It has already been fulfilled in the *Shanzhi*;
why forget the merit of standing in the snow? The Master said, “Idle words. [The student] asked, “What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, “One person raises the command. [The student] asked, “How does one comprehend it? The Master said, “The four seas are peaceful and clear.”
Question: "The Brahma King invited the Buddha for the sake of all sentient beings; when a patron invites a Master, what should be done?
The Master said: "There are few who can provide witness. The questioner continued: "The patron is sincere; the student prostrates. The Master said:
"Those words are still ringing in my ears."
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “Squeezing. The monk pressed further, “I do not understand;
how does one cultivate and realize it? The Master said, “Adding more mud on top of the highest ground. A monk asked, “What is nirvana? The Master said, “Fine mountains and fine waters.
The monk said, “I do not understand. The Master said, “Benefiting the son and benefiting the grandson.”
The Master ascended the hall and said: "The precincts are solemn and still; who can distinguish guest from host? The seas are calm and the rivers clear; sovereign and minister are in accord.

Throughout heaven and earth and the great world, this is the家风 (family style) of the ancient Buddhas. Across ten ages of past and present, this is the ancestral patriarch’s command. To proclaim it in such a manner—"
This is still like buying a hat to fit a head. If one were a monk of the fundamental division, they would be ten thousand eight thousand miles away. Take care!
When Master Yue of Haihui Monastery in Huzhou first opened the hall, after he had finished offering incense, a monk asked:
"What is the primary meaning? The Master said: "I do not wish to say it twice or thrice. The monk pressed further: "In that case, may I hear it?"
The Master said, "What is the matter that you have heard? The student replied, "It has been transmitted exclusively.
The Master said, "You must examine this even more closely. A question was asked: "In the past, in the kingdom of Magadha, he personally issued this command.
How do you, O Monk, provide the skillful means today? The Master said, "You intend not to comply. The student replied, "Suddenly a thunderclap startles me from the heavens."

"The universe! There is not a single being among humans or devas who does not receive your grace. The Master said, "Idle talk. A question was asked: "The dragon emerges from its cave; thunder rolls through the heavens.
The Master ascends the precious seat and the fourfold assembly has all gathered. We beg the Master for a word regarding the supreme vehicle of the ancestral school.

The Master said, "I leave it entirely to you to judge and critique. The student stepped forward and said, "If that is so, then this disciple offers his thanks. The Master [said], "... (text fragment).

[The Master] said, "What have you attained? [The student] asked, "When the Brahma King invited the Buddha, it was for the sake of all sentient beings. When a donor invites the Master, for what purpose should it be?
The Master said, "I thank you for being my witness. [The student] further asked, "If that is so, then all classes of beings, including gods and humans, shall all receive this power of grace.
The Master said, "A person who recognizes their debt of gratitude is hard to find."
Chan Master Puguang of Kaishan Monastery on Mount Ruiyan in Mingzhou ascended the seat.

A monk asked, "Having just left the realm of the Azure Clouds, you have already arrived at the site of practice in the Jing River valley. What is the Immovable Honored One? The Master said, "You are trying to gain the upper hand."
Question: I have heard it said in the *Pingshu* (Petition and Commentary) that the "iron ox" and "stone maiden" are talk for the sake of awakening;
that on the Snowy Peaks and at Caoxi, the beauty of the ancestral lineage was successfully inherited; and that the fourfold assembly flocked there like the wind.

I pray you grant us further instruction. The Master said: "Scholar, have you seen this question? He replied: "While the events of this day may indeed be verified, who was it that first brought forth the Three Powers before they had even manifested?"
The Master said, "Are you not creating too much trouble? He replied, "If that is so, for the sake of the assembly, I venture to let out a lion’s roar.
It is a profound labor to leak the source-mechanism of fearlessness. The Master said, "How could you possibly do so?
A question was asked: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does he succeed? The Master said, "You say the assembly does not know."

The monk Zhìyán of Jingde Temple in Tokyo was a native of Shouchun and surnamed Xǔ. He received his training at the Qījùzhī (Seven Koṭis) Cloister of this same temple and regularly attended the lecture series on the *Lotus Sūtra*.
One day, he suddenly felt a disturbance in his mind; he became unrestrained and wandered about without any restraint.

His deportment was most extraordinary. Whenever he encountered people on the road, he would repeatedly write characters in the air; at other times, he would show them to others on paper or bamboo slips.

His calligraphy was elegant and beautiful, and its contents often proved to be in accordance with reality. It was only after a long time that he began to recite the *Lotus Sūtra*, through which he gained renown. He was ultimately called the "Wind-Whistling Recluse" (*Yanfengzi*).

Nevertheless, his eating habits were irregular, and his clothes remained filthy and unwashed, yet he bore no resemblance to the appearance of common folk. [This account is from] the *Jixian lu* (Records of the Assembled Immortals) by Wang Zhi.

The implements for the secret trial were set out with a midday meal. Thereupon, [Huangbo] was invited into the meditation hall and questioned: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
Huangbo replied: "The shadows of green mountains compete to drench the mist; the lofty chanting of the jeweled pagoda stirs the morning breeze."
It is further said: "When Fa-hua was asked to offer incense, he replied: 'I have never sought it through fasting or precepts; I do not seek it from the Buddhas or the Sangha.
Later, when a monk asked, "Are you an ordinary person or a sage? Fa-hua pointed with his finger and said, "I dwell right here.
Subsequently, Xu Yue, an assistant lecturer at the National Academy, asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?"
He said: "At the eastern end of the street. The student asked: "I do not understand. He said: "Three kinds of people may not ask this. Furthermore, someone asked:
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? He said: "Mañjuśrī is inside this temple; do not ask him at the steps.
Those who realize this are called "scattered sages" (*san-sheng*), such as Buddhatara, Hanshan, and Shide.
Therefore, it is appended here.
*Tiansheng Guangdeng Lu*, Volume Thirty (End).
